73:Tb3a,## What

Replaces the 27-deep `LifeOpsService` class-mixin chain with **namespaced sub-service composition**. The mixin system is removed entirely.

### Before
`service.ts` composed 26 `withX` mixins via a 27-deep generic chain. TypeScript can't track type identity past ~6 chained generic mixins (TS2589 instantiation-depth), so every mixin carried an `as unknown as MixinClass<>` return cast and an `as unknown as <X>MixinDependencies` dependency cast; `service.ts` added a `Constructor<StatusMixinDependencies>` cast and 4 `Omit<>` collision deconflicts plus a `noUnsafeDeclarationMerging` interface merge. ~39 load-bearing casts in one package, hiding real cross-domain type drift.

### After
- **`LifeOpsContext`** (`lifeops-context.ts`) — the shared state/infra surface (runtime, repository, identity, ownership, generic audit, logging, events), derived via `Pick<LifeOpsServiceBase>` so it can't drift.
- **26 domain sub-services** under `lifeops/domains/*-service.ts`, each `class XDomain { constructor(ctx, deps) }` — cast-free, taking cross-domain dependencies as typed `deps` (no `this`-casts). The **browser↔screentime cycle** is broken via DI; the **reminders hub** (~5500 LOC) is one domain that its 5 consumers (definitions/goals/workflows/x/status) inject.
- **`LifeOpsService`** is now a single **concrete** `class extends LifeOpsServiceBase` holding the 26 domains, 263 flat delegators (preserving every existing call site byte-identically), and 26 typed **namespace getters** (`service.goals.x()`, `service.gmail.y()`, …). A concrete class surfaces every method directly, so the interface-merge, the 4 `Omit<>`s, and all assembly casts are gone.

## Why
The mixin god-class was not ideally factored: 22.9k LOC of 27 domains melted onto one class via a cast-laden inheritance chain whose casts were a genuine workaround for TS depth limits + method-name collisions. Composition removes the depth limit, the collisions, and the casts, and gives real domain separation.

## Result
- Repo-wide `as unknown as` **117 → 82** (−35); the plugin's mixin/assembly casts went from ~39 to **2** documented bridge casts for genuine pre-existing cross-package type drift (`LifeOpsGoalRecord` narrow re-decl; `LifeOpsDerivedEvent` vs `LifeOpsWorkflowEvent`). Domains are cast-free. Type-safety ratchet baseline lowered 117 → 82 to lock it in.
- **No behaviour change** — pure structural refactor; the flat public surface is preserved.

## Verification
- `tsgo` typecheck: **0 errors** in `src/lifeops/` (and `src/`).
- `vitest run src/lifeops/`: **16 files / 112 tests pass**.
- Each of the 8 commits is an independently-green slice (foundation → leaf domains → cross-dep domains → cycle break → reminders hub → dependent cluster → facade collapse → residual-cast cleanup).

  - If `canvasOpen` is true, `<CanvasLayout />` renders.
  - If `canvasOpen` is false, `<DashboardLayout />` renders instead, unmounting the canvas to prevent page navigation from triggering unintended canvas events.
  - While in `<DashboardLayout />`, the floating assistant pill [cloud-assistant-pill.tsx](file:///Users/home/Documents/eliza/packages/cloud-frontend/src/components/canvas/cloud-assistant-pill.tsx) remains overlayed in the bottom-center of the viewport, so pressing `cmd + k` or clicking the orb seamlessly slides back into the Interactive Canvas.

## 2. Voice-Driven Canvas Interaction UX

### Core Features
- **Unified Voice Hooks:** Integrated `useVoiceChat` and `useContinuousChat` from `@elizaos/ui/hooks` with a stabilized React Ref (`handleSendRef`) to avoid stale closure state during voice/speech callbacks.
- **Dual-Mode UX State Flow:**
  - **Text Mode:** Canvas is open with the text input bar expanded. A microphone button is available next to the close button to switch to voice mode.
  - **Voice Mode:** Input bar collapses into a floating circular orb (56x56 px). centring states like recording (`Mic`), thinking (`Loader2`), or speaking (`Volume2` bounce animation). Real-time preview transcript is shown in a small card overlay.
- **TTS Responses:** Automatically speaks out assistant responses on query execution success, along with helpful voice-guided prompts.

8c:T5df,## What
Adds dynamic plugin-view routing and an agent-driven interaction channel — the agent can **open / close / close-all / split / tile** plugin views, and views expose a server-side `interact` entrypoint so they can be driven programmatically.

## Changes
- **core** (`types/plugin.ts`): `ViewDeclaration.serverInteract` — plugins declare a server-handled interact entrypoint.
- **ui**: `DynamicViewLoader` + `view-interact-registry` (unmounted view clients stay silent; requestId dedup to drop stale replies), `app-navigate-view` wiring, `App` integration.
- **agent**: `views-routes` serverInteract handler, `views-registry`, `builtin-views`.
- **plugin-app-control**: `VIEWS` action close/close-all/split/tile sub-handlers, `views-client`, and a `view-followup-routing` evaluator.

## Scope notes
- The `plugin-simple-views` test fixture and the `ViewCatalog` restyle from the original branch are **intentionally excluded** — develop's `ViewCatalog` is used unchanged, and no new default plugin is registered. This keeps the PR to the routing infrastructure.
- All touched files are untouched on develop, so this rebases clean.

## Testing
`bun run --cwd packages/ui test` (view wiring/loader/interact-registry), `--cwd plugins/plugin-app-control test` (views), `--cwd packages/agent test` (views-routes) → **87 passing**. Cross-package typecheck via CI.

## Context
Extracted from #8340 (closed; drifted ~249 commits behind develop). Third in the focused-PR split, after #8443 and #8444.8d:Td61,Completes the **#9956** recall-bench work-order, building on the IR-metrics foundation **#10153** laid (`metrics.ts` + `metrics.test.ts`). This adds the real-`@elizaos/core` harness, per-mode metrics, the fail-open regression gate, registry registration, and a CI lane — exactly the checklist #10153's README left open.

## What it does
Drives the **genuine** recall pipeline (no Python/mock reimpl) over a deterministic, seeded, labelled corpus:
- Boots a real `AgentRuntime` + `@elizaos/plugin-sql` (PGlite, in-process) + the real `documentsPlugin`, registers a deterministic content-hash `TEXT_EMBEDDING` model, ingests via the real `DocumentService.addDocument`, then runs `searchDocuments` (hybrid/vector/keyword), the low-level `searchMemories`+`embedRecallQuery` path, and the `scoreMemoryText` keyword chat-search surface.
- Emits per-`SearchMode` **Precision@K / Recall@K / MRR / nDCG@K / HitRate@K + p50/p95 latency** via the shared `metrics.ts`, with the memperf honesty contract (`null`, never `0`, for unmeasured rows).
- **Hard fail-open assertion:** forces `embedRecallQuery → null` and asserts hybrid/vector recall collapses to the keyword baseline — the silent-degradation risk #9956 names, now a CI gate.
- Registered as `recall_bench` in the orchestrator (`commands.py`/`scores.py`/`__init__.py`/`adapters.py`/`ci_coverage.py`) **and** ships a memperf-style `budgets.json` + `.github/workflows/recall-bench.yml` exit-code gate.

## Measured baseline (live run, standard tier — 1040 fragments / 200 queries)
| mode | recall@5 | nDCG@10 |
|---|---|---|
| hybrid | 0.553 | 0.693 |
| vector | 0.551 | 0.692 |
| keyword | 0.466 | 0.571 |
| **runtime-vector** (raw cosine, no BM25 rerank) | **0.787** | **0.966** |
| keyword-chat-search (`scoreMemoryText`) | 0.281 | 0.448 |

**Fail-open delta = 0.000** (forcing the query embed to throw collapses hybrid+vector recall@5 to the keyword baseline 0.466). Vector/hybrid beat keyword; pure runtime-vector is strongest.

**Real finding (documented):** `runtime.searchMemories(…, { query })` BM25-reranks vector hits and drops zero-lexical-overlap candidates, capping `DocumentService` vector/hybrid recall; `runtime-vector` (no rerank) isolates the embedding's true semantic recall.

## Design note
The embedding is a **deterministic content-hash** model registered through the real `Plugin.models` layer — so it *is* the real recall path (the runtime dispatches to it exactly like a cloud model), just reproducible and key-free, which makes it a reliable CI regression gate. An optional real-provider embedding mode (OpenAI 1536 / local gte-small 384) for absolute semantic-quality numbers is a documented follow-up, as is the FACTS-provider slice (the four other recall surfaces fully exercise the path).

- `recall-eval.test.ts` (real runtime, PGlite): **3 pass**
- `tsc -p tsconfig.check.json`: clean

91:T7f9,## Problem

A planner that re-issues a tool call **identical** to one that already **succeeded** this turn (same tool name + arguments) cannot get new information — but nothing stopped it.

Observed live: `gpt-5.5` re-issued the same `WEB_FETCH` (same URL) on every planner iteration; each call succeeded, the evaluator said `CONTINUE`, and the loop ran until `maxTrajectoryPromptTokens` aborted the turn — the user got a generic *"sorry, something went wrong"* apology instead of the data that had been fetched 17 times.

This is the success-side analog of the existing `maxRepeatedFailures` guard (which only catches *failing* repeats).

## Fix

In `runPlannerLoop`:

- **Identity:** identify calls by name + **sorted-key** argument serialization (`canonicalParamsString`), so re-emissions that differ only in key insertion order (common across LLM turns) map to one identity.
- **Skip redundant:** partition each iteration's non-terminal calls into genuinely-fresh vs repeats of an already-succeeded call; execute only the fresh ones.
- **Bound + synthesize:** when every planned call is a redundant repeat, count a dead round; past the new `maxRepeatedToolCalls` bound (default **2**), force **one** tool-less synthesis call so the model writes the final answer from results already in the trajectory.
- **Relax toolChoice:** once a non-terminal tool has executed, relax `toolChoice` from `required` → `auto` (made explicit, since `callPlanner` defaults `undefined` back to `required`) so the planner may synthesize a terminal `REPLY` instead of being pushed to re-call a tool every iteration.

All structural (tool-call identity + trajectory state), no text heuristics.

## Test

Adds `stops re-executing an identical successful call and forces a terminal synthesis` to `planner-loop.test.ts` — same `WEB_FETCH` returned every iteration, asserts it executes **once** and the loop terminates with the synthesized answer. Full planner-loop suite: **45/45 pass**.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)95:T13b7,Closes #10202.

The app is an OS shell for loadable plugin/system/developer **views**, but the shell had only two states — mounted (active tab) or unmounted. No `hide`/`pause`/`evict` vocabulary, per-view crash isolation only for remote plugin views, no per-view render/memory/resource telemetry, and three places (`retained-lazy`, `DynamicViewLoader`, `GameViewOverlay`) each re-implementing their own visibility/memory-pressure pause+evict listeners. This delivers a real, **code-level** view lifecycle contract.

## New primitives (`packages/ui`, exported from the barrel)

- **`ViewLifecycleController`** (`state/view-lifecycle.ts`) — the single state machine + registry: phases `mounted/active/inactive/paused/evicted/crashed/recovering`, a device-memory keep-alive **LRU** with **pinned exemptions** (`chat`, `background` never evicted), and **one** shared `APP_PAUSE/APP_RESUME/visibilitychange/memorypressure` signal bus. `resolveViewLifecyclePolicy` + `registerViewPolicy`.
- **`KeepAliveViewHost`** — the new view host: renders active ∪ retained keep-alive, each wrapped per-view boundary → telemetry profiler → lifecycle slot. **Default policy is unmount-on-hide**, so builtin-view mounting is behaviorally identical to the old `ViewRouter` (the `App.navigate-view-wiring` suite stays green).
- **`useViewLifecycle` / `usePausableInterval` / `usePauseAware`** — the view-author pause/resume API for timers, polling, media, and native subscriptions.
- **`ViewErrorBoundary`** — standardized, keyed, resettable per-view crash container with crash telemetry + recovery, wired into `App.tsx` and `DynamicViewLoader` (the canonical `ErrorBoundary` gains an optional `onError` hook).
- **`ViewTelemetryProfiler` + `view-runtime-telemetry.ts` + `resource-counters.ts`** — per-view render count / p95 commit duration / JS heap / active subscriptions / pending timers / heavy resources (WebGL/audio/video) on a bounded ring + CustomEvent + `[ViewTelemetry]` log; plus per-view rerender-storm detection.
- **`bounded-view-lru.ts`** — single home for the device-memory tier helpers (deduped out of `retained-lazy` + `DynamicViewLoader`) + keep-alive sizing.
- **`view-memory-budget.ts`** — pure monotonic-growth detector for repeated view-switch heap samples (mirrors `hooks/frame-budget.ts`).
- `AppShellPageRegistration` gains `keepAlive?`/`pausable?` so plugin pages opt into retention.

Contract doc: **`packages/ui/src/components/views/VIEW_LIFECYCLE.md`**.

## Acceptance criteria → where met

- documented contract reflected in code-level primitives → `VIEW_LIFECYCLE.md` + the primitives above
- consistent pause/resume for timers/polling/media/native subs → `useViewLifecycle` + `usePausableInterval` + the controller signal bus
- bounded eviction with explicit exemptions → keep-alive LRU + `PINNED_VIEW_IDS`
- per-view error boundaries so one crash can't destabilize the shell → `ViewErrorBoundary` on every routed view
- telemetry makes expensive/leaking views visible in logs/artifacts → `view-runtime-telemetry`
- tests catch **1 rerender storm, 1 listener leak, 1 crash, 1 unbounded memory growth** + full matrix → see below

## Tests (all green)

Unit (jsdom): controller state machine + LRU + exemptions + signal bus + TTL; resource-counters leak/pause; memory detector; crash containment + recovery; rerender storm + sibling containment; **full builtin view-matrix coverage** (every tab). Existing `retained-lazy`, `agent-surface`, and `App.navigate-view-wiring` suites stay green (306 tests in the regression sweep).

E2E (`bun run --cwd packages/ui test:view-lifecycle-e2e`, esbuild → headless Chromium over the **real** `KeepAliveViewHost`): bounded retention (max 3 ≤ cap), RAF pause flatlines, LRU eviction, leaky-sub visible, per-view storm flagged (not calm siblings), crash containment + recovery, and a gc'd heap trend (24 samples) fed to the pure detector → **not leaking**. 0 unexpected page errors.

## Evidence

`.github/issue-evidence/10202-view-lifecycle/` — 5 screenshots (initial / after-switch-cycles / storm / crash-contained / crash-recovered), `view-lifecycle-walkthrough.webm`, and `telemetry.json` (maxRetained, the 24 heap samples + memory verdict, storm count, last 20 per-view telemetry events).

**Real-LLM trajectory / backend logs / audio:** N/A — presentation + runtime-infra + test work; no agent/model/prompt/server path touched.

## Note: `main.tsx` `appModuleCache` left unbounded — by design

It caches module *promises*; module code stays in the JS heap once imported regardless, so evicting yields no memory benefit and risks re-import races. The bounded-eviction criterion is met by the keep-alive view-**instance** LRU.

## Mobile Resource Workbench

End-to-end on-device resource profiling for elizaOS local inference on **iOS + Android** — battery, peak/steady RSS, prefill/decode tokens/sec, TTFT, thermal-state timeline, and low-power transitions — built on the proven `loadperf` budgets/results/CI-gate pattern. `loadperf` measures host load; this measures the *phone*.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] iOS native probe returns a **live** resource snapshot (resident `phys_footprint`, available RAM via `os_proc_available_memory`, thermal state, low-power mode, CPU time) — not the one-shot `getDeviceCapabilities` with `availableRamGb: NSNull()`.
- [x] iOS **MetricKit** (`MXMetricManager`) payloads (CPU/energy/runtime) captured to disk and ingested by the harness.
- [x] Android exposes a `ResourceProbe.getResourceSnapshot` Capacitor method (parity with iOS): thermal status, `BatteryManager` level/charge-counter, `Debug.getMemoryInfo` PSS; `dumpsys` hooks in the host probe.
- [x] Per-generation **prefill and decode tokens/sec** computed from the on-device `generateResult` (`durationMs`/token counts + measured TTFT) and aggregated per workload, per tier.
- [x] **Peak and steady RSS** recorded on-device with an RSS-leak flag (reused leak heuristic).
- [x] **TTFT** recorded on-device (text now; voice loop wired, tied to #8785/#8786).
- [x] **Battery drain** (% and, where available, µAh) across a fixed-duration workload.
- [x] **Thermal-state timeline** + low-power transitions across a sustained run (not a single probe).
- [x] CPU/GPU/ANE/NPU utilisation captured where the OS exposes it (MetricKit / batterystats), else explicitly recorded as missing — never faked.
- [x] `budgets.json` + `BASELINE.md` per device-class × tier (`0_8b`/`2b`/`4b`); runner writes `results/<workload>/latest.json` + a report and exits non-zero on budget regression.
- [x] `workflow_dispatch` (+ nightly) CI job: PR-path-filtered harness smoke + dispatch-only Android (self-hosted arm64) / iOS-sim lanes, uploading the report; kept off PR-blocking lanes until baselines are stable.
- [x] Missing measurements recorded as null/missing, never fabricated zeros (AGENTS.md §3/§7).

### What changed

**Shared / runtime (unit-tested):**
- `@elizaos/shared/local-inference` `computeGenerationThroughput` — differences `generateResult` into prefill/decode/combined tok/s (TTFT split); `null` when unmeasurable.
- Capacitor adapter captures first-token wall-clock (TTFT) → relayed through both hand-synced `device-bridge` copies → surfaced via `subscribeGenerationMetrics` + a recent-metrics buffer + `GET /api/dev/device-resource-metrics`.
- `DeviceResourceMetrics` accumulator generalises `VoiceRunMetrics` (tok/s, RSS+leak, battery, thermal timeline, low-power).
- `memory-monitor` reports real in-process RSS (`process.memoryUsage().rss`) on the FFI path (was a `null` stub).
- `inference-capabilities` adds a sampled `ResourceSnapshot` type + pure `thermalThrottleDecision()` policy.

**Native probes:** iOS `ElizaIntent.getResourceSnapshot` + MetricKit sink; Android `ResourceProbePlugin` (registered in both app trees). JS bridge accessor + normaliser.

**Workbench (`packages/benchmarks/mobile-resource/`):** runner + workloads (cold-load / single-turn / sustained-chat / voice-loop), adb/simctl probes, per-tier budgets, report, and `node --test` unit tests for the aggregation + budget logic.

### Testing

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->99:T834,## Problem

Live-data turns — "current bitcoin price", "weather in tokyo" — mis-routed: the agent **showed a VIEWS panel** or **spawned a coding sub-agent** instead of fetching the data and answering. On a text connector (Discord) that means a useless panel or a 3-minute multi-spawn with "working on it" acks, often ending in "Sorry, something went wrong."

## Three structural causes, each fixed

1. **VIEWS view-emphasis** (`plugin-app-control`) — `VIEW_ACTION_CONTEXTS` listed `web/crypto/finance/research/browser/payments`, which the action catalog turns into **keyword-retrieval terms**, so "price"/"weather" *retrieved VIEWS* and the planner navigated to a panel. VIEWS only displays panels — it doesn't fetch — so those live-data contexts are dropped.
2. **Stage-1 candidate-narrow drops the top tool** (`core/action-tiering`) — WEB_FETCH retrieved at score **1.0**, but Stage-1's `candidateActions` came back `[MESSAGE_SEARCH, VIEWS]`, so `tierActionResults` **demoted WEB_FETCH off the surface** — the planner physically couldn't pick it. Now a **near-certain match (score ≥ 0.97)** stays exposed even when Stage-1's narrow omits it. It does not force the choice — only keeps a dominant match available.
3. **Planner routing** (`core/planner` template) — a one-shot live/current/public-data lookup is *not* coding work: call WEB_FETCH / WEB_SEARCH directly; don't spawn a sub-agent.

All structural — no text heuristics on model output.

## Verification

- `action-tiering.test.ts`: **14/14** incl. new cases (near-certain non-candidate match stays exposed; a merely-good 0.8 match still demotes).
- **Live across all three planner backends** (cerebras/zai-glm, claude, codex): the same weather query routes to WEB_FETCH and answers cleanly on each.

> Note (for the planner side): a weak planner model (`gpt-oss-120b`) still mis-routes even with these fixes; a reasoning model (`zai-glm-4.7`, claude, gpt-5.5) routes correctly. These fixes make the *right* route reachable; the model has to take it.

9a:Tc5c,## What & why

Closes the **deepest** part of #9967: "the Kotlin that runs on a phone is executed by
no test, on no device." Before this PR the entire `plugin-native-*` set had **zero**
Android instrumented tests; the only coverage drove the React views against a **mocked
`Capacitor.Plugins` bridge in desktop Chromium**, so the real Kotlin — the launcher's
Phone/SMS/Home/Assistant gating — ran untested.

Root cause of *why* it was untested: the native logic was welded to the Capacitor
`Plugin`/`Bridge`/`PluginCall` objects, which only exist inside a running app, so it
could not be asserted from `androidTest`. This PR fixes that at the source.

### Changes
- **`RoleStatus`** (added in the prior commit): the launcher/comms role read is
  extracted out of `SystemPlugin` into a pure, `Context`-taking object — `RoleManager`
  / `TelecomManager` / `PackageManager` / `Telephony` reads with **no** bridge
  dependency. `SystemPlugin.getStatus` just delegates, so runtime behavior is unchanged.
- **`RoleStatusInstrumentedTest`** now lives in the plugin's *own* `androidTest` source
  set (`@elizaos/capacitor-system`) and runs the real `RoleStatus.read()` against the
  device's actual system services — the first on-device test in the native set.
- **plugin `build.gradle`** gains `AndroidJUnitRunner` + `androidTest` deps so the
  plugin library is instrumentable **standalone** — no full-app build (voice/inference
  JNI, fused `.so`, omnivoice submodule) is needed to run it. That's the pattern the
  rest of the native-plugin × view matrix can follow.

untestable native Kotlin testable and proves it on hardware, establishing the

9c:Teb4,## What

Lands the first **"Needs CI infra"** deliverable spun out of #9476 (tracked by #10333): run the MiniWoB++ benchmark suite against a **real Chromium engine** instead of JSDOM web mode.

The benchmark adapter was already engine-agnostic (`BrowserCommandExecutor`), so this is a **new executor + a gated lane — not a rewrite**. `report.engine` flips from `"jsdom-web"` to `"chromium"` and every action runs through a real browser process, mirroring how plugin-computeruse's OSWorld `*.real.test.ts` lanes drive a real OS.

## How

- **`src/benchmark/chromium-executor.ts`** — `createChromiumBenchmarkExecutor` (puppeteer-core, already a dep), `launchChromiumBenchmarkBrowser` (one browser per suite, fresh page per episode), `resolveChromiumExecutablePath` (env → playwright-core → system Chrome; `null` → lane self-skips). Command semantics mirror `browser-workspace-web.ts` **exactly** (type appends, fill replaces, check sets `checked`, get value/checked/text/count/url/title, snapshot, network-route via request interception with a hard external-network seal), so the **identical oracle sequences solve every task on both engines** — the engine-parity proof.
- **`src/benchmark/__tests__/miniwob-chromium.real.test.ts`** — gated `.real.test.ts` lane: oracle solves every task on every seed (reward 1), noop scores 0, on real Chromium.
- **`vitest.real.config.ts`** — opts the `.real.test.ts` lane back in (the root config excludes `**/*.real.test.ts`) while keeping the `@elizaos/*` source aliases. The "(or a dedicated config)" the issue called for.
- **`.github/workflows/browser-real-bench.yml`** — CI gate: `bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium`, run the lane + upload artifacts (nightly + dispatch + on benchmark changes), alongside the other heavy real lanes.
- **`scripts/run-miniwob-chromium-benchmark.mjs`** + `bench:miniwob:chromium` / `test:real-chromium` scripts.
- `BrowserWorkspaceMode` gains `"chromium"` (emitted only by this executor, never by `executeBrowserWorkspaceCommand`) so results carry an accurate engine tag.

a0:Tede,## What

Closes the one Definition-of-Done deliverable [verified missing on `develop`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/9476#issuecomment-4830133507) for #9476:

> **≥1 benchmark wired through `plugin-browser`** (mirror `plugin-computeruse/src/osworld/adapter.ts`), with a committed run artifact.

The other three DoD items already landed (CI-asserted parity matrix, JSDOM real-code lane, typed error contract). The web benchmarks (Mind2Web, WebShop, VisualWebBench) all **bypass** plugin-browser via the inference layer — no benchmark drove the BROWSER command surface end-to-end. This adds one that does.

## How

A **MiniWoB++-style** web-interaction benchmark (the canonical web-agent benchmark) under `plugins/plugin-browser/src/benchmark/`, the plugin-browser analog of `plugin-computeruse/src/osworld/`:

- **`adapter.ts`** — `BrowserBenchmarkAdapter` with the same observation/action/step seam as `OSWorldAdapter`, driving an engine-agnostic `BrowserCommandExecutor`. The workspace executor binds the **real** `executeBrowserWorkspaceCommand` router (the same mock-free path the `browser-workspace-web-real-code` lane uses) — no mock service stands in for the browser.
- **`tasks.ts`** — 6 tasks (`click-button`, `click-link`, `enter-text`, `enter-text-dynamic`, `click-checkboxes`, `multistep-purchase`). Pure markup, **no page scripts** (web mode hard-blocks script exec, GHSA-mhhr-9ph9-64j7); deterministic per seed; reward computed from **observable DOM state** read back through real BROWSER `get` commands (`value`/`checked`/`url`/`title`).
- **`policy.ts`** — `OraclePolicy` (deterministic solver) + `NoopPolicy`/`WrongPolicy` negative baselines.
- **`runner.ts`** — `runBenchmarkSuite` drives every task×seed episode, scores it, aggregates.
- **`__tests__/miniwob-adapter.test.ts`** — CI-asserted real-code lane (runs in the default `vitest run`).
- **`scripts/run-miniwob-benchmark.mjs`** + `bench:miniwob` — runnable harness that writes a JSON run report.

## Evidence (real, on a Windows 11 host) — see `.github/issue-evidence/9476-browser-benchmark/`

| Policy | Result | Proves |
|--------|--------|--------|
| oracle | **18/18 solved (100%)** | the suite is solvable end-to-end through real BROWSER commands; every action step records `resultMode: "web"` (the live router ran it) |
| noop   | **0/18** | doing nothing scores 0 — reward is grounded in real DOM state, not hard-coded |
| wrong  | **0/18** | wrong-target / wrong-text near-misses score 0 — reward discriminates |

Test lane locally: **5/5 passing**. Benchmark sources type-check clean (verified with a resolvable `@types/node`; the package's default `typecheck` hits a pre-existing worktree `typeRoots` quirk unrelated to this change). The broader plugin-browser suite's 8 core-barrel-dependent suites can't load under this box's light-install (a pre-existing `uuid`→`drizzle-orm`→`yaml`→`@noble/*` cascade, identical before this change); all 80 runnable tests pass, including the new lane.

## Reproduce

```bash

bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-browser bench:miniwob           # oracle (writes artifact)
bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-browser bench:miniwob -- --policy noop

a5:Te26,# Relates to

New plugin. Opens discussion around ERC-8183 as a lifecycle standard for agent-to-agent commerce in elizaOS.

# Sync with develop

# Risks

Medium.

This PR adds a new opt-in plugin under `packages/plugin-agent-commerce-pqc`. No existing runtime behavior is modified.

The plugin registers:

- 1 Service (`agent_commerce`)
- 4 Actions
- 1 Provider

State is persisted through the existing `runtime.createMemory()` API using the `erc8183:job:` namespace.

Known operational risks:

- hydration currently loads up to 1000 job records per agent
- rate limiting is process-local and not distributed
- reputation persistence is memory-backed by default

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds an ERC-8183-inspired commerce workflow for elizaOS agents.

The plugin enables one agent to:

1. Create a job
2. Fund a job
3. Submit a deliverable
4. Evaluate the result
5. Complete, refund, expire, or abort the workflow

State machine:

OPEN → FUNDED → SUBMITTED → COMPLETE
                           ↘ REFUND
              ↘ EXPIRED
         ↘ ABORTED

## Registered extension points

| Type | Name |
|--------|--------|
| Service | agent_commerce |
| Action | CREATE_SECURE_JOB |
| Action | FUND_SECURE_JOB |
| Action | SUBMIT_DELIVERABLE |
| Action | JOB_STATUS |
| Provider | COMMERCE_CONTEXT |

## Persistence

Jobs are stored through `runtime.createMemory()` using:

erc8183:job:<jobId>

Each state transition appends a new memory record.

On restart, the store lazily hydrates from memory records and reconstructs the latest job state using the highest `updatedAt` value.

## Security features

- SHA-256 payload attestation
- Deliverable hash verification
- Reputation-based funding gate
- Rate limiting
- State transition validation
- Idempotent terminal transitions

## What kind of change is this?

Feature (non-breaking).

All changes are additive.

# Documentation changes needed?

No.

The package includes its own README.

Distributed deployments require a custom reputation backend and shared rate-limit implementation.a6:T9ec,## What

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)a9:Taec,## What

Extends `@elizaos/plugin-cloud-apps` (read-core in the parent PR) with the **create → deploy → live** loop, safe destructive delete, and the deploy-success **facts cache** — so a user can build, ship, and manage a monetized app entirely from chat (app / Discord / Telegram).

Builds on the merged read-core (#10277, now in `develop`); diff is **plugin-only** (the create/deploy/delete additions).

## Actions added
- **`CREATE_APP`** — parse name/description/monetization intent → typed `client.createApp(...)`, offer to deploy.
- **`DEPLOY_APP`** — deploy, then a real **completion gate** (`deploy-gate.ts`): poll `getAppDeployStatus` until `READY` (bounded exp-backoff + timeout; ERROR/FAILED short-circuit), then probe the authoritative post-deploy `production_url` `/health` for 2xx. Only `READY + reachable` reports "live"; `timeout`/`error`/`unreachable` are honest failures. **A 202 is never "done."**
- **`GET_APP_DEPLOY_STATUS`** — formats DRAFT/BUILDING/DEPLOYING/READY/ERROR + url.
- **`DELETE_APP`** — DESTRUCTIVE → **two-phase, connector-agnostic confirm** (`safety.ts`): first ask names the app + what's destroyed (container + tenant DB) and does NOT delete; only an explicit confirmation in the follow-up calls `deleteApp`. Never relies on GUI buttons; a bare "yes" is insufficient.

## Safety + memory
- **`safety.ts`** — reusable two-phase confirm + a neutral `buildConnectorCta({label,url,kind})` (https-only) seam for the deferred paid actions; money/credentials never transit the connector.
- **`app-facts.ts`** — on a verified-live deploy, writes ONE durable fact to the real `facts` memory table via `runtime.createMemory`, keyed on `app.id`, idempotent (re-deploy updates in place). Convenience recall cache — **explicitly NOT the completion gate**. (This is the "save completed app to facts/knowledge" idea, done right.)

## Evidence
- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-cloud-apps test` → **68 pass / 0 fail** (mocks only the SDK client, runtime memory, and the `fetch` boundary; actions/gate/safety run for real). Covers gate progression/timeout/error/unreachable, create intent + no-name/no-key/error + API-key-never-echoed, delete first-ask/confirmed/bare-yes/not-found, facts idempotency.
- Plugin typecheck + biome clean; `packages/agent` typecheck clean; plugin build OK.

## Notes
- **Real end-to-end deploy is gated on the staging deploy backend (#9853 / Phase 4)** — can't fire until armed, so the proof here is the mocked status-progression + reachability gate tests.
- Deferred to a follow-up (TODO in `index.ts`): `UPDATE_APP`, `UPDATE_MONETIZATION`, `GET_APP_EARNINGS`, `WITHDRAW_APP_EARNINGS` (paid → reuse the CTA seam), `REGENERATE_APP_API_KEY`, `BUY_APP_DOMAIN` (domain last).
- Part of the apps launch (tracker #8434).
aa:Td06,## Summary

Extracts the **entire** calendar surface out of `@elizaos/plugin-lifeops` into a new first-class **`@elizaos/plugin-calendar`**, keeps LifeOps fully working via thin wrappers + delegation, and wires the Odysseus `CalendarView` to the canonical calendar API (resolves #8203).

## What now lives in `@elizaos/plugin-calendar`
- **`CalendarService`** (former 1209-line mixin) + **`CalendarRepository`** + **drizzle schema** — same `app_lifeops.life_calendar_*` tables (no data migration).
- **Apple bridge**, **Google delegates**, **normalize helpers**.
- **Client methods** (`api/client-calendar.ts`, side-effect augmentation of the `@elizaos/ui` `ElizaClient`).
- **HTTP routes** — `handleCalendarRoutes` in `routes/calendar-routes.ts` (paths unchanged: `/api/lifeops/calendar/*`).
- **CALENDAR action + ~4280-line LLM handler** — `createCalendarActionRunner(deps)` + `extractCalendarPlanWithLlm`.
- **Dashboard UI** — `CalendarSection`, `EventEditorDrawer`, `useCalendarWeek` (exported via a server-graph-free `./ui` barrel).
- **Contract types** in `@elizaos/shared/contracts/calendar` (the only layer both `@elizaos/ui` and the plugins can depend on without a cycle).

## The seam (no dependency cycle — strictly `lifeops → calendar`)
Cross-domain concerns calendar can't own are **injected** from thin LifeOps wrappers (mirrors the documented plugin-health owner-action pattern):
- `CalendarHostGate` — Google connector grants + reminder-plan/audit persistence (default gate resolves Google directly + no-ops reminders; LifeOps injects the real impl at init).
- `CalendarRouteDeps` — LifeOps' HTTP plumbing (telemetry/schema-bootstrap, rate limiting, body parsing).
- `CalendarActionDeps` — trajectory LLM model runners, recent-conversation context, optional travel-time buffer.
- `CalendarSectionProps` — dashboard-shell deps (chat launcher, selection, event priming).

LifeOps retains only thin wrappers (delegation shim for the service methods, gate impl, the `CALENDAR` owner-action wrapper with `hasLifeOpsAccess` gating, the `LifeOpsCalendarSection` wrapper) — plus the legitimate cross-domain consumers (reminders/google reading the calendar cache).

## Odysseus (#8203)
`CalendarView` overlays a **read-only provider feed** (Google/Apple via the calendar client) on top of the existing local-first calendars + `.ics` (the **augment** option). Stale header fixed.

## Verification (all green)
- `@elizaos/plugin-calendar`: typecheck (0 errors) + build + **31 tests** (Apple bridge, normalize/merge units, real-PGlite `CalendarService` CRUD asserting persistence, feed aggregation, next-event context, and gate reminder-plan side effects).
- `@elizaos/plugin-lifeops`: full build (js + **views bundle** + types) + 53 calendar-touching unit tests.
- `@elizaos/plugin-task-coordinator`: build + 25 tests. `@elizaos/shared`: 777 tests + typecheck. `@elizaos/ui`: typecheck.
- No `@elizaos/plugin-lifeops` import anywhere in `plugin-calendar` (cycle-free).

## Follow-up (noted, low-harm)
A few calendar-specific formatters/delegates were copied into plugin-calendar and are now unused inside LifeOps' shared `google/format-helpers.ts` / `google-plugin-delegates.ts`; surgical removal from those multi-export files was deferred.

This PR hardens the desktop/mobile shell for Cloud-first startup and limited Cloud-agent bases:

- removes the separate native desktop pill window path; the in-canvas chat pill remains the single desktop surface
- wires external Cloud API bases into Electrobun renderers early and avoids local desktop RPC fallbacks for configured external bases
- recovers localhost/dev shells with stale local-backend state into first-run/Cloud selection instead of wedging on `Booting up...`
- gates full app-shell routes when the active base is a shared/dedicated Cloud chat adapter, avoiding unsupported `/api/views`, `/api/apps/runs`, `/api/workbench/todos`, `/api/approvals`, `/api/lifeops/inbox`, `/api/computer-use/approvals`, `/api/coding-agents`, and `/api/orchestrator/*` calls
- prevents localhost `:2138` Cloud sign-in from probing `/api/cloud/status` when no local backend exists
- polishes chat overlay, springboard/home ordering and image-backed tiles, route back behavior, and related startup failure UI

## Why

The reproduced browser logs were three separate problems:

1. Local Vite shell running without app-core behind it returned same-origin `/api/*` 502s.
2. A selected Cloud agent base is a limited chat adapter, not a full app-shell runtime, so desktop widgets/hydration were polling unsupported routes and creating CORS/404 noise.
3. The `My Eliza Cloud key isn't authorized for inference` message was traced in #8434 to a revoked key on a throwaway validation agent; that remains a cloud/phone provisioning self-heal follow-up, not a desktop UI route issue.

This PR fixes the desktop/UI-side causes and leaves the provisioning guard to the cloud/phone lane.

## #9948 — canonical role model
- **One `CANONICAL_ROLE_RANK`** source of truth; `roles.ts` + `context-gates.ts` derive from it (kills the two-disagreeing-rank-tables hazard).
- **Drop the `RoleGateRole = … | (string & {})` escape** → `Role | "USER"` (a gate can no longer name an arbitrary string that silently ranks 0). Core typechecks clean; every `minRole`/`roles` literal across agent+plugins is already canonical.
- **`resolveBoundaryRole` + `ensureMinRole`** — a role tier on the binary HTTP boundary; the tokenless same-machine caller resolves to a NAMED OWNER principal instead of ambient trust. Fails closed.
- **Provider role-gating** routed through the canonical `satisfiesRoleGate` (the 6th lowercase vocabulary is now just an override-map alias).
- **`public:true` allowlist regression test** — a new public route can't be added unauthenticated without tripping the guard.
- **Wallet sign routes**: loopback-only CORS, dropped credential reflection.

## #9949 — should-respond injection gate
- Pure `extractRiskFactors` in the `parallel_with_should_respond` hook, role-keyed (OWNER/ADMIN bypass), borderline USER/GUEST → one fail-closed `TEXT_LARGE` adjudication, only when `shouldRespond=true`. 23 adversarial tests.
- **One injection pattern bank**: `SecurityModule` and `external-content` now share `injection-primitives` (prompt-injection phrasing vs external-content dangerous-command indicators are split deliberately so the gate doesn't flag dev chat).

## #9947 — connector embed seam
- Fail-closed **embed-auth handshake** (Telegram `initData` HMAC, timing-safe + 24h replay guard; Discord OAuth2), maps to entity, OWNER/ADMIN-only via the single core `hasRoleAccess` (the duplicate `hasRoleAccess` is consolidated).

- **Role-gated launch surfaces**: Telegram `web_app` button (https-enforced, OWNER/ADMIN-gated) + Discord `/app` Activity command. Live launch needs platform creds.

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>b4:T834,## What

New `@elizaos/plugin-cloud-apps` — lets the agent answer **"what apps do I have on Eliza Cloud?"** and "tell me about app X" from chat, on **every connector** (in-app, Discord, Telegram, cloud-hosted) from one registration. Closes the gap where the "What apps do I have?" suggestion chip was a false promise (no action behind it).

This is the **read-core**; the mutating actions (create/deploy/manage/monetize) land in a follow-up PR.

## How

- **`LIST_CLOUD_APPS`** (similes `MY_APPS`/`WHAT_APPS_DO_I_HAVE`/…) → `ElizaCloudClient.listApps()`, formats name/url/status; empty + no-key + error handled.
- **`GET_APP`** → by name or id, formatted detail; graceful not-found.
- **`CLOUD_APPS` provider** → injects the user's app inventory into context, modeled on `creditBalanceProvider`: 60s cache, context-gated to apps/finance/settings topics, EMPTY when no cloud key.
- **Dual registration (both sites — the whole point):**
  - (a) `core-plugins.ts` `CORE_PLUGINS` — reaches local/native + Discord/Telegram via the shared runtime pipeline (default on, read-only).
  - (b) `agent-loader.ts resolvePlugins()` — as a **full** plugin (not via `AVAILABLE_PLUGINS`, which strips to models-only), gated behind **`CLOUD_APPS_PLUGIN_ENABLED`** (**default OFF** — it runs on every dedicated prod agent, so it must be staged + proven with real trajectories first).
- Suggestion chip `"What apps do I have?"` now matched by `LIST_CLOUD_APPS`'s similes.

## Evidence
- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-cloud-apps test` → **20 pass / 0 fail / 63 expect()** (mocks only the SDK client; actions/provider/formatters run for real).
- Plugin typecheck + biome clean; `packages/agent` typecheck 0 errors; `packages/cloud/shared` typecheck 0 errors.
- A live-only scenario (`cloud-apps-read-core.scenario.ts`) asserts `LIST_CLOUD_APPS` fires on "what apps do I have?" — runs once a live model + Cloud key are available (follow-up evidence).

<details><summary><h3>Greptile Summary</h3></summary>

This PR adds end-to-end support for custom Docker image provisioning through the Eliza cloud API: the `dockerImage` field is now accepted on agent creation, validated with a regex schema, persisted to the database, and surfaced in list and detail API responses. The dashboard is wired to pass the persisted image through sandbox creation, and new E2E tests cover both the API path and the dashboard UI flow.

- **API layer** (`route.ts` for both agents and `[agentId]`): `dockerImage` is validated via a zod schema with a character-class regex, stored on create, and returned in list/detail DTOs — including the fix in `Page.tsx` that was previously hardcoding `docker_image: null`.
- **E2E stack hardening** (`stack.ts`): migrations now run as an explicit logged step before the API server starts, `DATABASE_URL` is set earlier in the process, and the stack switches to `cloud-api-e2e-server.mjs`.
- **Frontend fixes** (`agent-card.tsx`, `glass-composer.tsx`, `sandbox-proxy/page.tsx`, `vite.config.ts`): accessibility improvements (aria-label, aria-pressed), an inlined Vite alias for es-toolkit/compat shims, and a switch from `process.env.NODE_ENV` to `import.meta.env.PROD` for the sandbox proxy guard.
</details>

    participant ProvisionAPI as POST /agents/:id/provision
    participant ControlPlane as Control Plane

    Client->>CloudAPI: "POST /api/v1/eliza/agents {agentName, dockerImage?}"
    CloudAPI->>CloudAPI: dockerImageSchema.safeParse()
    CloudAPI->>SandboxSvc: "createAgent({agentName, dockerImage})"
    SandboxSvc->>DB: "INSERT (docker_image = dockerImage)"
    DB-->>SandboxSvc: agent row
    SandboxSvc-->>CloudAPI: agent
    CloudAPI-->>Client: "201 {id, dockerImage}"

    Client->>ProvisionAPI: POST /api/v1/eliza/agents/:id/provision
    ProvisionAPI->>DB: read docker_image
    ProvisionAPI->>ControlPlane: schedule provisioning job (image)
    ControlPlane-->>ProvisionAPI: 202 accepted
    ProvisionAPI-->>Client: "202 {agentId}"

    Note over Client,ControlPlane: poll GET /agents/:id until status=running
```
</details>

   <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=9" align="top"></a> **Lockfile integrity bypassed on failure**

   The `|| bun install --no-frozen-lockfile` fallback means that whenever the lockfile is out of sync with `package.json` — the exact condition `--frozen-lockfile` is supposed to catch — CI silently falls through to an unconstrained install. Packages resolved during that fallback install may differ from what the lockfile records, making the build non-reproducible and removing the supply-chain integrity guarantee the frozen flag provides. If the frozen install is failing in CI today, the correct fix is to regenerate the lockfile and commit it, not to bypass the check on every future run.

<!-- /greptile_comment -->b9:Teb0,# Overall Project Monthly Summary (June 2026)

## Executive Summary
June 2026 marked a major milestone for ElizaOS with the launch of "Eliza Cloud Apps," a new platform capability that allows for secure, isolated, and scalable agent hosting. By hardening our infrastructure and modularizing our core architecture, we have significantly improved both the enterprise-grade reliability of our cloud services and the ease of use for local developers.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Launching Scalable Cloud Hosting**
_Goal: We wanted to provide a robust, secure environment where users can host their own AI agents with professional-grade reliability._
*   We introduced a new hosting model in [elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza) that keeps each user's agent data and operations completely separate, ensuring better security and performance.
*   We simplified the billing and management process by unifying how users track their spending and credits, making it easier to manage autonomous agent costs ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza)).

**Building a Modular and Flexible Framework**
_Goal: We aimed to make the ElizaOS framework easier to customize and extend by breaking down complex, monolithic systems into smaller, specialized parts._
*   We refactored our core systems in [elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza) to allow developers to use specific, domain-focused plugins rather than one large, rigid system.
*   We improved how agents coordinate tasks, allowing them to act more autonomously while staying within the limits set by their owners ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza)).

**Enhancing the User Experience**
_Goal: We focused on making the platform more intuitive for new users and more efficient for those running agents locally._
*   We updated the chat interface in [elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza) with helpful prompt suggestions and smoother visual effects to make interacting with agents more natural.
*   We optimized the desktop experience in [elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza) to ensure the application starts up faster and runs more smoothly on local machines.

The legacy QJL/TBQ fused-attention routing is moot for the shipped Gemma tiers (head_dim 512/256 ≠ the kernels' 128).c5:T15e6,## Eliza Cloud Apps (Product 2) — scaling + ingress gaps to close before go-live

A code-level audit of the apps data plane (per-tenant DB + isolated container deploys). **The core design is sound and standard** — per-tenant `DATABASE`+`ROLE` with `REVOKE CONNECT` (real cross-tenant isolation), per-app `--internal` network + DB ambassador, `ClusterPool` sharding. This is *not* jank. But the current code's realistic ceiling is **~dozens of concurrently-running apps, not ~1000**, and the front-door router isn't installed yet. Filing the prioritized gaps (all evidenced) so they're tracked before flipping `APPS_DEPLOY_ENABLED` in prod.

Context: terraform apply is also currently blocked on the staging Hetzner **server limit** (see #8318). Apply bugs (SSH-key 409, retired `cpx41`) are fixed in #8318.

### 🔴 P0 — pre-launch blockers (serve ~0 reachable / isolation maybe inactive)
1. **Ingress not installed.** `cloud-init/app-node.yaml.tftpl:62-63` leaves Caddy as a `STAN:` TODO — only squid is installed. No per-app `<id>.apps.elizacloud.ai` hostname routes to any container (nothing terminates TLS / reverse-proxies 80/443 → the random high host port). **Serves 0 reachable users until added.** (config)
2. **Postgres connection ceiling.** `cloud-init/tenant-db.yaml.tftpl:12` leaves `max_connections` at the default 100, and there's **no pgbouncer** anywhere; each app's plugin-sql pool is `max:20 / min:2` (`plugins/plugin-sql/src/pg/manager.ts:16-17`). Exhausted at ~5 apps under load / ~50 idle — `ClusterPool` shards DB *count* (2000 cap), not connections. (config + a pooler)
3. **Env-var contract unverified.** Orchestrator injects `DATABASE_URL` (`app-deploy-orchestrator.ts:82`) but plugin-sql's primary path reads `POSTGRES_URL`. The cloud eliza loaders *do* map `DATABASE_URL→POSTGRES_URL` (agent.ts:10, settings.ts:100, …), so it's satisfiable — but must be confirmed for the actual app image, else the isolated DB is provisioned and never used (silent PGlite fallback) → per-tenant isolation isn't even active. (code/verify)

### 🟠 P1 — required before real scale (multi-node)
4. **App placement is single-node.** `container-executor-deps.ts:42-52` always picks `seed.split(',')[0]` — every container piles on node 1; extra terraform app nodes get no placements. No `node_id`/`incrementAllocated` for app containers (`app-container-store.ts`). (code)
5. **Docker network exhaustion.** One `--internal` bridge per app exhausts the default 172.x address pool at ~31 networks/node; `daemon.json` `default-address-pools` not set in cloud-init. Caps a node at a few dozen tenants regardless of CPU/RAM. (config)
6. **Multi-node ingress LB.** Wildcard DNS hard-codes `app_node["1"]` (`main.tf:184,190`); no `hcloud_load_balancer`. The moment `app_node_count>1`, apps on node 2+ are dark. (config)
7. **Tenant-DB slot leak.** `tenant_db_clusters.database_count` only increments (`tenant-db-clusters.ts:44`); no `releaseSlot`/decrement, and `tenant-db-provisioner.deprovision()` (DROP DATABASE/ROLE) has **zero non-test callers** — `UserDatabaseService.cleanupDatabase` only deletes Neon. Under churn, slots ratchet up + orphan DBs accumulate. (code)
8. **Host-port collisions.** `allocateHostPort()` is a blind random pick in 20000-39999 with no in-use check (`container-executor-deps.ts:86-90`), unlike the agent path's `getUsedDockerHostPorts`. Flakes docker-create at a few hundred containers/node. (code)
9. **App-plane autoscaler.** `node-autoscaler.ts` is agent-image/platform hardcoded (lines 133,233,435); no autoscaler cron; app provisioning never registers allocation → app demand triggers nothing. Adding app capacity is manual. (code)
10. **Billing cron at scale + idempotency.** `cron/container-billing/route.ts:391-440` is one serial Worker pass with an N+1 per-org prefetch + inline emails (presses Worker wall-time in the low thousands; can't resume a cut-off pass), and `recordSuccessfulDailyBilling` (`container-billing.ts:153-212`) has **no unique constraint on (container_id, billing_period)** → a duplicate cron fire / manual re-run double-bills. *(2AM-owned billing surface.)*
11. **Defense-in-depth written but unused.** `buildAppNodeNftablesRules` (drops 169.254.169.254 metadata + RFC1918 pivots), per-app `buildSquidAllowlistConf`, `buildHetznerAppFirewallRules` have **zero non-test callers** — egress is one shared squid + static global allowlist, the metadata/lateral block is code-only, and `-p` binds `0.0.0.0` so app ports are world-exposed until the firewall's applied. (NB: reconcile the nftables RFC1918 drop with the ambassador's legit 10.30.x DB path.) (both)

### 🟡 P2 — later / hardening
12. Single Postgres superuser per cluster = shared fate (rotation + a non-superuser provisioning role); tighten `operator_ingress_cidrs` (SSH `0.0.0.0/0`); real tenant-DB TLS cert (hostssl vs the `sslmode=disable` fallback).
13. Kernel sandboxing decision (gVisor/Kata/userns + seccomp) + per-app `--cpus` (only `--memory`/`--pids-limit` set today). Right-size `max_databases` (2000 is misleading until pooling exists). Tenant-DB-node scaling runbook.

c7:Tea0,## Summary

Every chat to a **dedicated cloud agent** returns the canned fallback:
```json
{"text":"Sorry, I'm having a provider issue","agentName":"Eliza","failureKind":"local_inference"}
```
in ~130ms, on every message. `failureKind: "local_inference"` (`classifyChatFailure` → `isLocalInferenceError`, `packages/agent/src/api/chat-routes.ts:1528`) means the agent **attempted local/on-device inference and errored** instead of using the cloud inference plane. For a dedicated *cloud* agent that should never happen — it implies cloud text-generation isn't wired in the container, so it falls back to a local model that isn't present (or hits ENOSPC).

`isLocalInferenceError` matches: `local inference | local model | on-device | device bridge | llama | gguf | no local model | model download | enospc | no space left | disk full`.

## Launch impact

**P1 / likely launch blocker.** If this reproduces on every freshly-provisioned dedicated agent, no dedicated-agent chat works (the user-visible symptom is the phone showing "Sorry, I'm having a provider issue" forever). Confirmed live on-device (Seeker) + via the management API.

## Repro

1. Provision a dedicated agent (`POST /api/v1/eliza/agents {agentName, dockerImage:"ghcr.io/elizaos/eliza:sha-7032a6a", autoProvision:true}`) → it reaches `status: running`, healthy heartbeat, base `200`.
2. `POST /api/v1/eliza/agents/:id/api/conversations/:cid/messages {text:"hi"}` → `200` with `{"text":"Sorry, I'm having a provider issue","failureKind":"local_inference"}`.

## What's ruled OUT (already chased)

- **Stale image** — no. A brand-new agent on the **current** prod image (`sha-7032a6a`) fails identically. (Pre-existing agents were on stale immutable images `sha-2e08c1d`/`sha-7a5d4f9`, but image is not the cause.)
- **Revoked injected key** — the failure is `local_inference` (tried local), not an auth/cloud error, so it's not "cloud key 401 → fallback".
- **Tailnet/provisioning outage** — separate issue (CP `tailscaled` had died → fleet-wide provision wedge), already fixed; agents now provision + reach `200`. This `local_inference` failure is underneath that and persists after recovery.
- **#8769** (cloud containers use cloud **embeddings** not local gte-small) is **MERGED** — but that was embeddings; **text generation** still appears to attempt local inference here.

## Root-cause direction (needs agent-container env/logs — I don't have node SSH)

Likely the container's **text** model provider isn't pointed at cloud (missing `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_ENABLED` / `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_*_MODEL` overrides / cloud key for generation), so generation falls through to a local llama/gguf path that errors. Open questions for whoever has container access:
1. Is `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_ENABLED=true` + the cloud model overrides + cloud inference key actually injected into the agent container env at provision time?
2. Does this reproduce for an agent provisioned via the **normal app first-run / shared→dedicated handoff** flow, or only via the bare management-API create? (i.e. is the cloud-config injection create-path-dependent?)
3. The matcher also hits `enospc/disk full` — are the agent nodes (esp. `eliza-core-prod-2` / 178.63.251.122) low on disk? That would make a generation/model write fail with a disk error that classifies as `local_inference`.

Earlier this session a fresh agent passed `Say PONG` 20/20 on `sha-7032a6a`, so either something regressed or the working path differs from the one above.

## Affected
- nubs's dedicated agents (now re-provisioned to a single fresh `316438e9` on `sha-7032a6a`, healthy infra, still failing `local_inference`).

- Each item below: re-confirm the exact file:line in the current tree before changing (the audit was a snapshot).
- Land as small, reviewable PRs grouped by the sections below. P1 items are the gate before opening to non-allowlisted users.

---

### P1 — security gates (do first; required before any external / self-serve user)

1. **Rate limiting everywhere it's missing** — global, anonymous-session minting, and the metered inference paths; add sybil control on the free-credit grant. *Today these are unthrottled, so a loop against the anon/inference path is unbounded cost.* **Effort: M**

6. **CI gate against unscoped tenant DB reads** + run the existing isolation-verify script in CI. Tenant isolation currently rests on every handler remembering to pass `organization_id`; one slip = cross-tenant read. **Effort: S–M**

9. **One end-to-end staging test of the full user chain**: create app → build → isolated DB → live URL. Today it's only covered in disconnected pieces; the "user's own code" build leg is least exercised. **Effort: L**
10. **Finish the consumer payout/redemption side** (currently "temporarily unavailable") and **replace the Cloudflare registrar dev stub** before charging for custom domains in prod. These are live money paths that charge but don't fully deliver yet. **Effort: M**

11. **Env kill-switch for feature flags** (they're hardcoded `enabled: true` with no runtime override — no way to disable a feature mid-incident). **Effort: S**
12. **Confirm/re-enable the promo duplicate-redemption guard** on the free-credit path (currently commented out → repeat bonus possible). **Effort: S**
13. **Refresh stale comments** (the "no build service yet" header is now wrong) and **re-audit the public-path prefix allowlist**, especially `/api/internal` and `/api/webhooks` that lean on per-handler secret checks (one mis-scoped `startsWith` exposes a subtree). **Effort: S–M**

c9:T269f,## Summary

Make **"hey &lt;character name&gt;"** a first-class, battery-efficient, cross-platform wake word that:

1. **Activates voice when it is not already on** — saying the wake word opens a listening window that stays open until the agent responds (already partially landed; see *Current state*).
2. **Works inside transcription mode** — while the app is recording a long-form transcript (replies suppressed), the wake word makes the agent **respond inline once** and the conversation **continues as a parallel chat inside the transcript**, without exiting transcription.
3. **Follows the character's name** — the user can rename the character in settings; the wake phrase tracks that name (`"hey eliza"` → rename to *Ada* → `"hey ada"`), zero config.
4. Uses **native acceleration on Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, Windows** and is cheap enough to run always-on on battery.

This issue captures the full design, the backend decision, the work breakdown, and the validation matrix (unit → state fuzz → real audio → iOS simulator → physical device), with recorded **video + audio** evidence.

---

## Current state (what already exists)

**Detection backends — two of them:**

- **openWakeWord** (`plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/wake-word.ts`, `wake-word-ggml.ts`) — a dedicated tiny GGML hotword model (mel filterbank → 96-dim embedding → per-phrase classifier head), fused into `libelizainference` (`eliza_inference_wakeword_*`). **~0.23 ms / 80 ms frame on native CPU**, native acceleration across all platforms via the fused lib. Default head `OPENWAKEWORD_DEFAULT_HEAD = "hey-eliza"` (`wake-word.ts:74`). A real "hey eliza" head has been trained and verified end-to-end; training pipeline lives in `packages/training/scripts/wakeword/` (`train_eliza1_wakeword_head.py`, `synthesize_wakeword_corpus.py` — **TTS-synthesized corpus**, `convert_openwakeword_to_gguf.py`). **Constraint: phrases are not zero-shot — each needs a trained classifier head.**
- **Swabble** (`plugins/plugin-native-swabble/`) — a Capacitor plugin that runs **continuous native OS ASR** (`SFSpeechRecognizer` / Android `SpeechRecognizer` / Web Speech / desktop Whisper.cpp) and fuzzy-matches the transcript against `triggers: string[]`. **Arbitrary phrases (incl. a renamed character) work zero-shot**, but continuous full ASR is **not battery-efficient for always-on**, and it already emits a typed `wakeWord` event (`{ wakeWord, command, transcript, postGap, confidence? }`).

**UI / orchestration already landed (PRs in this branch lineage):**
- `packages/ui/src/voice/wake-listen-window.ts` — pure state machine: `idle → open → awaiting-response → idle`, idle timeout + safety cap + re-arm.
- `packages/ui/src/voice/useWakeListenWindow.ts` — subscribes to the Swabble `wakeWord` event, drives the hands-free mic, stays inert under always-on.
- Wired into `packages/ui/src/components/shell/useShellController.ts`.
- Settings: `VoiceConfigView.tsx` `WakeWordSection` (triggers default hardcoded `["eliza"]`), `VoiceSection.tsx` wake toggle.

**Transcription mode (the surface feature 2 plugs into):**
- Client suppresses replies by *never sending* a transcription-intent final — it accumulates into `TranscriptSessionAccumulator` (`packages/ui/src/voice/transcript-session.ts`).
- Server safety net: `transcriptionModeActive(message)` + the `core.transcription_mode` evaluator (`packages/core/src/services/message.ts:1689,2939`) returns `IGNORE` + `clearReply` when `metadata.transcriptionMode === true`.
- `ContinuousChatOverlay` `ThreadLine` already renders interleaved user/assistant bubbles — an inline reply needs **no new UI**.

---

## Backend decision

| | openWakeWord (GGML, fused) | Swabble (native OS ASR) |
|---|---|---|
| Always-on battery | ✅ ~0.23 ms/frame, native CPU | ❌ continuous full ASR |
| Cross-platform incl. Linux/Windows desktop | ✅ fused `libelizainference` | ⚠️ Electrobun/Whisper bridge only |
| Native acceleration | ✅ Metal/Vulkan/CUDA/CPU | OS ASR (mobile), CPU desktop |
| Arbitrary/renamed phrase zero-shot | ❌ needs trained head | ✅ |
| Already wired into voice pipeline | ✅ engine.ts | ❌ opt-in, unwired into pipeline |

**Decision — a two-stage name-aware wake:**

- **Stage A (always-on, cheap, battery):** openWakeWord generic detector (or native VAD) runs continuously. This is the only thing burning power at idle.
- **Stage B (confirmation, on candidate):** when Stage A fires, open a **short ASR window** (we already have STT/ASR + fused transcription) and **fuzzy-match the transcript against the current character name** (`"hey <name>"`). This gives **zero-shot, rename-following** name support while keeping idle cost at Stage-A levels.
- **Head fast-path:** if a trained head exists for the current name (shipped `hey-eliza`, or auto-trained via `synthesize_wakeword_corpus.py` + `train_eliza1_wakeword_head.py`), Stage B is skipped — pure-openWakeWord, lowest latency.
- **Swabble** stays as the **fallback detector** where the fused FFI is unavailable (e.g. some browsers), reusing its existing `wakeWord` event.

This unifies both backends behind one `WakeController` whose default phrase is **derived from the character name** (`s.characterData?.name` → `agentStatus?.agentName` → `"eliza"`, per `App.tsx:1523`).

---

## Work breakdown

### A. Name-aware triggers
- Derive the default wake trigger from the live character name (`useAppSelector(s => s.characterData?.name ...)`), so renames propagate. `VoiceConfigView.tsx` default `["eliza"]` becomes name-derived.
- A pure **name-matcher** (`packages/ui/src/voice/wake-name-match.ts`): normalizes + fuzzy-matches `"hey <name>"`, `"<name>"`, `"hey, <name>"`, handles homophones/ASR slop (Levenshtein ≤ threshold), exposed for Stage-B confirmation and Swabble triggers.
- On rename, update the persisted Swabble `triggers` if they still equal the old name (don't clobber a user-customized phrase).

### B. Transcript-mode inline reply ("parallel chat")
- In `useShellController` transcription branch: when an utterance **matches the wake phrase**, send it as a **reply-eliciting** turn (`VOICE_DM`, *without* `metadata.transcriptionMode`) instead of silently accumulating — the agent replies and speaks once.
- Record both the user's wake turn and the assistant reply **into the transcript session** as speaker-labeled segments, so the parallel chat appears inline in the transcript and the finalized record.
- Transcription **does not exit** — the re-listen loop resumes recording after the reply.
- New pure helper + `transcription-exit.ts`-style detection so it is unit-testable.

### C. Wake activation when voice is off
- Already landed via `wake-listen-window` / `useWakeListenWindow`; extend so the same wake event drives (a) open-mic-if-off, and (b) the transcript inline-reply path when transcription is active.

### D. Detection pipeline (`WakeController`)
- Stage A openWakeWord/VAD always-on → Stage B ASR-confirm vs character name → emit unified wake event.
- Head fast-path + Swabble fallback selection by platform/capability.
- Optional: auto-train a head for the current name via the existing TTS corpus pipeline (follow-up; gated by training availability).

---

## Testing, validation & verification matrix

| Tier | What | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Unit** | `wake-listen-window` reducer, `wake-name-match` (homophones, accents, slop), transcript inline-reply branch, name-rename propagation | vitest, frozen clock |
| **State fuzz** | random event sequences over the wake + transcription state machines (wake during open/awaiting/transcription/always-on, double-wake, exit-phrase races) — assert invariants (mic never stuck open, transcription never silently exits, exactly-one inline reply per wake) | property/fuzz test (mirrors `ContinuousChatOverlay.fuzz.test.tsx`) |

| **Real audio (acoustic loop)** | play "hey eliza" through the **Mac speakers**, capture via the **Mac microphone**, assert wake fires end-to-end | host harness + ffmpeg avfoundation capture |
| **iOS simulator** | boot the app in the booted iPhone 16 Pro simulator, drive the wake/transcript UI, screen-record | `xcrun simctl` + app build |
| **Physical device** | install on the paired iPhone 16 Pro Max, exercise on-device openWakeWord + mic, screen-record with audio | device build + `xcrun devicectl` |

- [ ] In transcription mode, the wake word yields exactly one inline agent reply (spoken), recorded into the transcript, **without exiting transcription** (test + video).
- [ ] Idle always-on detection runs on the battery-efficient openWakeWord path; Swabble only as fallback (documented + measured).
- [ ] Cross-platform: validated on macOS host + iOS simulator + physical iPhone; Android/Linux/Windows paths documented and unit-covered.
- [ ] State-fuzz suite green; mic-never-stuck and exactly-one-reply invariants hold.
- [ ] Recorded video+audio evidence attached for unit/real-audio/sim/device tiers.

## Non-goals (this issue)

- Shipping trained wake heads for every possible name (auto-train pipeline is a follow-up; Stage-B ASR covers arbitrary names today).
- Re-architecting TTS/ASR — reuse the existing fused stack.
ca:T13a6,Evidence-based audit of the Apps (Product 2) hosting + per-tenant-DB billing. **Bottom line: profitable on the happy path, but 4 leaks must be fixed before go-live.** Nothing is bleeding *today* (the apps lane isn't armed/deployed yet) — these are pre-launch fixes.

## ✅ Profitable on the happy path
- **Hosting:** a default app bills ~**$1.17/day** ($0.67 base × 1.75 CPU multiplier from the schema default `cpu=1792`) vs **~$0.29–0.58/day** real Hetzner cost → **~2–4× gross margin**, break-even ~1 container/node. Apps **are** enrolled in billing (our deploy sets `billing_status='active'` by schema default → 2AM's `container-billing` cron picks them up like agents). Not hosting for free.
- **Inference:** end user pays (`cost = provider_cost × 1.20`); platform never subsidizes; creator/affiliate markups stack **on top** of the user's bill. Always net-positive.

## ⚠️ Leaks / correctness bugs (owner-tagged)

### CRITICAL
- [ ] **[ours] Suspended containers are never `docker stop`ped.** `suspendContainer()` only flips DB flags (`container-billing.ts:117-126`); the node container runs `--restart unless-stopped` (`client.ts:249`) and no reconciler stops `billing_status='suspended'` rows. After suspend the row drops out of `listBillableContainers` forever → a deadbeat's app **runs indefinitely on Hetzner, billed never** (~$210/yr, unbounded). *Fix:* on the shutdown branch, SSH `docker stop` (via our provider) + decrement node allocation, and add a reconciler. (Cross-ref: `suspendContainer` is 2AM's; the stop is ours.)
- [ ] **[ours] Deleted isolated-DB apps never drop their Postgres + never release the cluster slot.** `SqlTenantDbProvisioner.deprovision` exists (`tenant-db-provisioner.ts:166`) but has **zero live callers**; there is no `releaseSlot` (only `tryClaimSlot` increments). `app-cleanup` drops domains/repo/secrets but not the DB; `cleanupDatabase` handles only the Neon path. → every deleted isolated app **strands a live DB we pay for + burns 1/2000 cluster slots permanently**. *Fix (focused lifecycle PR):* enqueue a deprovision **job** on app delete (DROP DATABASE/ROLE needs `pg` → daemon) + add `releaseSlot` (`database_count = GREATEST(0, database_count-1)`) + extend `cleanupDatabase` for the `direct_pg`/isolated path. **This is the missing half of #8338 (opt-in per-tenant DB).**
- [ ] **[2AM] `container-billing` cron has no idempotency gate.** It writes `last_billed_at`/`next_billing_at` but never reads them (`container-billing.ts:57-81`); a Cloudflare retry or duplicate POST **re-debits every running container a full extra day** → over-charge → chargebacks. *Fix:* port the agent-billing rebill guard + a unique partial index on `(container_id, billing_period)`.

### HIGH
- [ ] **[design — nubs] Per-tenant DB / storage / bandwidth bill $0.** The ccx33 tenant-DB node (~$2.05/day incl. 200GB vol) has **no billing line**; an `isolated` app and a `none` app are billed identically. At low density the apps lane runs **negative** (break-even ~3 paying containers; 1 container = −$1.67/day). *Decision:* (a) add a per-isolated-DB daily line (amortized floor ~$0.035/DB, realistically $1–3/mo) gated on `databaseMode='isolated'`, **or** (b) fold DB cost into the container fee + set a minimum density before provisioning the dedicated ccx33.
- [ ] **[design — nubs] Deploy takes no upfront charge / no balance precheck** (and bypasses the quota check). Grace-window hosting is free; repeatable spin-up/tear-down costs us. *Fix:* charge `DEPLOYMENT` ($0.50) at create, or require `credit_balance ≥ 1–2 days` before provisioning.

### MEDIUM / LOW
- [ ] **[2AM] `organizations.credit_balance` DEFAULTS to `$100`** (`organizations.ts:33-35`) — any future org-create that omits the field grants ~$100 free hosting. *Fix:* default `'0.00'`; grant starter credits explicitly.
- [ ] **[2AM] Daily debit is a non-atomic JS read-modify-write** (absolute balance) → lost-update vs concurrent inference debits/top-ups. *Fix:* route through `creditsService.deductCredits` (relative decrement with a guard).
- [ ] **[ours] No `--cpus` limit** — we bill a CPU tier (1792→1.75×) but enforce only `--memory`; and our app containers actually provision at `cpu:1/512MB` (`APP_CONTAINER_DEFAULTS`) while billing assumes 1792/1792. *Fix:* reconcile the provision defaults with the billed dimensions + add `--cpus`.
- [ ] **[design] Copy says $0.67/day; real default is $1.17/day**; cost-basis constants are AWS references, not Hetzner. Reconcile copy / cost basis.

## Numbers
- Revenue: $0.67/day base ×1.75 (cpu=1792) = **$1.17/day**. Real Hetzner: ccx23 ~$0.79/day (app node), ccx33 ~$1.74/day + 200GB ~$0.31/day (tenant DB). Container margin ~2–4×; full-lane break-even ~3 containers.
- Inference: `cost_to_user = provider_cost × 1.20`, always positive.

cd:Tf9c,## Summary

When the planner narrates a coding sub-agent's `task_complete` back to the user, the **deliverable** (the printed value / command output) is frequently dropped, truncated, or buried under process chatter — while the underlying sub-agent work is correct. This is a *presentation* defect, not a capability one.

Evidence: a live 48-prompt sweep (30-scenario battery + smart/normie/harden suites) across all three backends found **0 capability-broken defects** — every answer was correct, every spawn produced its artifact, every safety probe handled. The **only** remaining defect class is this narration-envelope.

## Manifestations (all observed live)

1. **Deliverable drop on combo / printed-value tasks.** On the no-change-set completion path, `composeNarration` → `stripToolTranscript(response)` (`sub-agent-router.ts`) deletes the entire `[tool output: …] … [/tool output]` block. For a "print a value / run a command and report the output" task (no files changed → no diff), that block *is* the deliverable, so it's gone before the user sees it.
2. **Value truncation by the parent model.** The synthetic `task_complete` memory is re-rendered by the parent `RESPONSE_HANDLER` (a weak planner in some deployments), which truncates the value — e.g. `2026-06-02` → `202`, a BTC price `70234` → `705`. Per-backend signature: opencode truncates, codex emits verbose process narration + `Completed <task>` banners, claude is cleanest.
3. **Stale retry attempts leak.** When a first attempt errors (e.g. `session_state_lost` / an ACP crash) and a respawn recovers, the user sees *both* `"the sub-agent was blocked / crashed, let me try again"` **and** the eventual deliverable.
4. **Process chatter.** Sub-agents (esp. codex) narrate their steps (`"I'll load the workspace context first"`, `"rg is not installed"`, `"reverse.py already exists"`); the parent relays it.

## Proposed structural fixes

**(a) Carry the printed-value deliverable verbatim (fixes #1, mitigates #2).** A structural carrier that mirrors the existing verified-URL carrier:
- *Producer* (`sub-agent-router.ts`): on the `task_complete && !changeSet && verifiedUrls.length === 0` path, recover the captured stdout from the **raw** `response` (before `composeNarration` strips it) via the inverse of `stripToolTranscript`, and stamp it as `metadata.subAgentDeliverable` (gated to a short single block, ≤2KB, so multi-KB transcripts stay on the model-rendered path). *(I have a ready, tested producer patch for this.)*
- *Consumer* (`evaluators/sub-agent-completion.ts`): when `subAgentDeliverable` is present, relay it **verbatim** instead of letting the model re-summarize/truncate it — parallel to how `subAgentVerifiedUrls` is already consumed.

**(b) Terminal-reply filter (fixes #3, #4).** Emit only the *terminal* sub-agent reply; suppress stale `blocked`/`failed`/`state_lost` attempts that a later retry superseded, plus raw tool chatter and `Completed <task>` banners. **Caveat — needs care:** the `session_state_lost` error event is currently *coupled to the respawn trigger* (re-injecting it is what prompts the parent to respawn), so suppressing the user-facing narration requires an internal-only routing path that keeps the respawn signal. This is the part that needs design discussion.

**(c) Already shipped — source-side mitigation.** #8158 adds an output-discipline section to the scaffolded sub-agent operating manual ("lead with the deliverable, don't narrate process, no `Completed <task>` banner, a bare workspace has no SOUL.md/USER.md — don't hunt for them"), which measurably reduced #4 at the source (codex re-probes went from a verbose banner to a bare `5050` / `2026-06-02`).
