## Open questions

- **Where should the speaker→transcript join happen** — in a new app-core ingestion route, in the native `engine-bridge` (if we wire it), or by having the diarization route also call ASR? This determines whether we keep the HTTP-route architecture or revive the in-process engine.
- **Is the native voice-session engine (`runVoiceTurn`) meant to be the on-device production path, or legacy?** If it stays unwired we should delete it; the answer drives proposal item 5.
- **Multi-agent room semantics:** when multiple Eliza agents share a `VOICE_GROUP`, is turn-taking deterministic (e.g. owner-addressed agent only), round-robin, or model-decided per agent? Needs a product decision before building item 7.
- **Wake-word vs always-on default per surface:** desktop ambient mode opens the mic continuously; should group/multi-speaker rooms require a wake word by default to avoid cross-talk storms?
- **Privacy/consent for bystander voices:** confident-bystander suppression exists (`BYSTANDER_SUPPRESS_CONFIDENCE = 0.7`), but should unenrolled voices be transcribed/extracted at all, or dropped pre-pipeline?
ff:T4623,## Summary

elizaOS already ships a deep, production-grade voice pipeline (VAD, streaming ASR, EOT classifier, barge-in, diarization, speaker imprint/profiles, Kokoro/OmniVoice TTS) plus a sprawling but **fragmented** set of voice test harnesses — a pure scoring library, a two-agent `voice:duet` harness, native benchmark `.mjs` scripts, Python benchmark suites, and a single-turn headful self-test screen. None of these are unified, and the headful surface only covers a **single-speaker, single-turn STT→agent→TTS** round-trip. The product-owner scenarios (multi-voice, pauses, respond/don't-respond, capture-and-simulate, multi-speaker, entity extraction, voice→entity recognition, diarization accuracy, EOT latency, transcription-mode entry/exit, multi-agent rooms) have **no headful coverage and no scenario-runner home**. This issue proposes a single **Voice Workbench** that unifies headless API tests + headful real-frontend tests + a benchmark layer (EOT latency, false-trigger rate, diarization accuracy, WER) over a shared corpus of TTS-generated scenario audio.

## Current state

### What exists and is genuinely strong

**The voice pipeline itself is mature** (`plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/`, ~90 source files):
- EOT detection: `eot-classifier.ts` (`CompositeEotClassifier`), `eliza1-eot-scorer.ts`, `fused-eot-scorer.ts`, `eot-classifier-ggml.ts`; `composite-eot-classifier.test.ts` exercises the heuristic/model blend. Backend selected via `ELIZA_VOICE_EOT_BACKEND`.
- VAD: `vad.ts`, `vad-ggml.ts`, with `vad.test.ts`, `vad.v1-v4.test.ts`.
- Diarization + speaker ID: `live-diarization-session.ts`, `speaker-imprint.ts`, `profile-store.ts`, `voice-emotion-classifier.ts`, plus `speaker/` and `streaming-asr/` subdirs.
- Barge-in / pause handling: `barge-in.ts`, `voice-state-machine.ts` (explicit IDLE→LISTENING→PAUSE_TENTATIVE→SPEAKING state machine with C1 checkpoint rollback), `optimistic-policy.ts`, `optimistic-rollback.ts`, `partial-stabilizer.ts`.
- Entity binding: `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/runtime/voice-entity-binding.ts` emits `VOICE_TURN_OBSERVED` / consumes `VOICE_ENTITY_BOUND`; `IDENTIFY_SPEAKER` action (`src/actions/identify-speaker.ts`) names a recent unidentified voice. Routes in `src/routes/voice-speaker-profile-routes.ts` bind/unbind a voice centroid to an elizaOS entity.

**Headless scoring library** — `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/e2e-harness.ts` is the one genuinely shared piece: pure functions `wordErrorRate`, `scoreTtsAsrRoundTrip`, `scoreBargeInInterruption`, `scorePauseContinuation`, `scoreOptimisticRollbackRestart`, `scoreFirstResponseLatency`, `summarizeVoiceE2e` + `assertRequiredVoiceArtifacts`. It is **pure** (no model loading) — hardware scripts feed it measurements (`packages/app-core/scripts/voice-e2e-hardware.ts`). Tested by `e2e-harness.test.ts`.

**Two-agent duet harness** — `packages/app-core/scripts/voice-duet.mjs` (`bun run voice:duet`) wires two `LocalInferenceEngine` instances A↔B over an in-memory `DuetAudioBridge` (`packages/app-core/scripts/lib/duet-bridge.mjs`), records `ttftFromUtteranceEndMs` etc. Shape-tested headlessly in `voice-duet.test.ts` with fake backends; real-model run gated in `voice-duet.e2e.test.ts`.

**Synthetic speech generation already exists** — `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/__test-helpers__/synthetic-speech.ts` produces formant-resonator speech-like PCM that Silero VAD reads as speech (no recorded WAV needed). `packages/benchmarks/voice/three-voice-scenario.mjs` already builds a 7-turn, 3-voice (alice/bob/eliza) diarization scenario with should-respond logic ("turns containing 'Eliza' should respond; turn 5 Bob→Alice should NOT").

**Native + Python benchmark suites** — `packages/benchmarks/voice/` (diarizer, speaker-encoder, enrollment, owner-voice, real-diarization, three-voice e2e), `voicebench/` (TS latency runner: transcription, response-decision, TTFT, TTS, e2e p95/p99), `voiceagentbench/` (Python: voice-in→tool-call, 5,757 queries, multi-turn coherence, safety/refusal, multilingual), `voicebench-quality/`, `voice-emotion/`, `voice-speaker-validation/`.

**Headful (Playwright)** — `packages/ui/src/voice/voice-selftest/voice-selftest-harness.ts` (`runVoiceSelfTest`) drives the REAL production client functions (`transcribeLocalInferenceWav`, `ElizaClient.sendConversationMessageStream`, real TTS fetch + `decodeAudioData` + playback graph) and emits a machine-readable per-stage report with a DOM mirror (`data-testid="voice-selftest-overall"`). Reached via `?shellMode=voice-selftest` (`packages/ui/src/App.tsx:86,358`). Driven by:
  - `packages/app/test/ui-smoke/voice-selftest-e2e.spec.ts` (mocked backends, `wav-direct`)
  - `packages/app/test/ui-smoke/voice-realaudio.spec.ts` (real `getUserMedia` capture via Chromium `--use-file-for-fake-audio-capture`, mocked backends)
  - `packages/app/test/ui-smoke/voice-desktop-selftest.spec.ts`
  - `packages/app/test/android/voice-selftest.android.spec.ts` (REAL on-device round-trip on a Pixel 9a)

### What is weak, missing, or broken

1. **No unified workbench. Five disjoint harness families** (pure scoring lib, `voice:duet` mjs, native benchmark `.mjs`, Python benches, headful self-test) with no common scenario format, no shared corpus, no single entrypoint, and divergent metric definitions (e.g. WER is implemented **twice** — `e2e-harness.ts:wordErrorRate` and `voice-selftest-harness.ts:wordErrorRate`; latency thresholds are scattered as inline `?? 1500` / `?? 250` defaults).

2. **Headful coverage is single-speaker, single-turn only.** `runVoiceSelfTest` has exactly three stages (ASR→SEND→TTS) for one phrase. There is **no** headful test for: multiple voices, pauses mid-utterance, respond-vs-not-respond, multi-speaker turn-taking, diarization in the UI, entity extraction/inference from conversation, voice-recognition matching an existing entity, EOT "jump in / don't jump in", transcription-mode entry/exit, or multi-agent room participation. The rich `voice-state-machine.ts` / `live-diarization-session.ts` logic is **never exercised through the real frontend**.

3. **scenario-runner cannot host voice scenarios.** `packages/scenario-runner` boots a real `AgentRuntime` over PGLite and runs scripted turns, but the turn model (`ScenarioTurnExecution`, `TurnReport.kind`) is text/http/connector only — there is **no audio/voice turn kind**, no PCM/WAV input, no diarization/EOT/speaker assertions. Grep of `packages/scenario-runner/test/scenarios/` for `voice|audio|asr|tts|diariz` returns zero voice scenarios. This is the natural home for "real voice-generated scenarios" and it is empty.

4. **"Capture user voice to simulate" ('talk about X for a few minutes') has no harness.** There is no tool to TTS-synthesize a long, multi-paragraph monologue (with pauses) from a prompt and feed it as a single user turn to test long-form ASR stability, EOT suppression across pauses, and partial-stabilizer behavior.

5. **Metrics are computed but never aggregated into benchmark verdicts that gate.** EOT latency, false-trigger rate (respond-when-shouldn't), diarization accuracy (DER), and WER each have *some* code path, but there is no single report that runs the matrix and produces pass/fail with regression baselines. `voicebench` reports latency; `e2e-harness.ts` scores latency; nothing rolls EOT false-trigger-rate or diarization DER into a gating summary.

6. **Backends are mocked in every CI-runnable headful test.** `voice-selftest-e2e.spec.ts` / `voice-realaudio.spec.ts` mock ASR/agent/TTS routes; real-backend coverage exists only on physical Android (`voice-selftest.android.spec.ts`) and gated hardware scripts. There is no documented "headful + real local Eliza-1 backend on a dev host" lane that the workbench could standardize.

7. **No shared, versioned audio corpus.** Fixtures are ad hoc: a hand-rolled `tinyWav()` 220 Hz sine inlined in each Playwright spec, `packages/app/test-results/.voice/known-phrase.wav`, `packages/benchmarks/voicebench/shared/generated/*.wav`, and on-the-fly synthesis. No labeled multi-speaker corpus with ground-truth diarization/EOT/transcript labels for accuracy benchmarking.

## Proposed work

Build a **Voice Workbench** package (proposed `packages/voice-workbench/`, or a `voice/` subtree inside `packages/scenario-runner`) that unifies the three execution modes over one scenario format and one corpus. Ordered scope:

1. **Define a shared voice-scenario schema and corpus.**
   - A `VoiceScenario` type: ordered `VoiceTurn[]` where each turn carries `{ speaker, text|audioRef, ttsVoiceId, pausesMs[], expectRespond: boolean, expectedTranscript?, expectedSpeakerLabel?, expectedEntity? }`, plus scenario-level `participants` (named voices/entities) and `assertions` (diarization labels, EOT decisions, WER ceilings, latency budgets).
   - A **corpus generator** that TTS-synthesizes each turn from text using the existing TTS routes + `samantha-preset` / Kokoro voices, splices in pauses, and mixes multi-speaker streams — extend `packages/benchmarks/voice/three-voice-scenario.mjs` and reuse `__test-helpers__/synthetic-speech.ts`. Persist labeled WAV + ground-truth JSON under a versioned `corpus/` dir so accuracy metrics are reproducible.
   - Add the long-form "talk about X for a few minutes" generator (synthesize a multi-paragraph monologue with natural pauses) as a corpus recipe.

2. **Consolidate the metric layer.** Promote `plugins/plugin-local-inference/src/services/voice/e2e-harness.ts` into the single source of truth for voice scoring (it is already pure). Delete the duplicate `wordErrorRate` in `voice-selftest-harness.ts` and import the shared one. Add the missing scorers: `scoreEotDecision` (EOT latency + false-trigger/false-suppression rate over a labeled stream), `scoreDiarization` (DER / speaker-confusion against ground-truth), `scoreRespondDecision` (respond-when-should vs respond-when-shouldn't), `scoreEntityExtraction` (inferred name/entity match), `scoreVoiceEntityMatch` (recognized voice → existing entity binding).

3. **Headless mode — API/runtime tests.** A workbench runner that, given a `VoiceScenario`, feeds the corpus audio through the real services *without* a browser:
   - ASR via `/api/asr/local-inference` (`local-inference-asr-route.ts`).
   - Diarization via `LiveDiarizationSession` / `/api/voice/audio-frames` (`live-diarization-route.ts`).
   - EOT via the selected `ELIZA_VOICE_EOT_BACKEND` classifier.
   - respond/don't-respond + multi-agent room via a real `AgentRuntime` (reuse scenario-runner's PGLite boot).
   - entity extraction/voice→entity via `VOICE_TURN_OBSERVED`/`VOICE_ENTITY_BOUND` + `IDENTIFY_SPEAKER`.
   - TTS round-trip via `/api/tts/local-inference`.
   This is where the **scenario-runner** gets an `audio`/`voice` turn kind so voice scenarios become first-class `.scenario.ts` files.

4. **Headful mode — real frontend over the APIs.** Extend `VoiceSelfTestShell` (`packages/ui/src/voice/voice-selftest/`) from a single-turn self-test into a **scenario player**: accept a `VoiceScenario` over `window.__voiceWorkbench(scenario)`, drive the real client pipeline (capture → ASR → SSE → TTS → playback) turn-by-turn including injected pauses (Chromium `--use-file-for-fake-audio-capture` per turn), transcription-mode entry/exit, and multi-speaker streams, and emit a per-turn machine-readable + DOM-mirrored verdict. Add Playwright specs under `packages/app/test/ui-smoke/` (`voice-workbench-*.spec.ts`) that run each scenario class headful: multi-voice, pauses, respond/no-respond, multi-speaker, diarization, entity-extraction, voice-recognition, EOT, transcription-mode, multi-agent-room.

5. **Benchmark/report layer.** A single `voice:workbench` entrypoint that runs the scenario matrix in both modes and rolls up: EOT latency (p50/p95) + false-trigger rate, diarization DER, transcription WER, first-audio/TTFT latency, respond-decision accuracy, entity-match accuracy — into one JSON + Markdown report with baselines, mirroring `voicebench`'s p95/p99 output and the existing `summarizeVoiceE2e` shape. Wire a CI lane (real local backend where provisioned; `skipped` — never `pass` — where artifacts absent, matching the existing self-test honesty contract).

6. **Document and dedupe.** One README that maps the consolidated workbench to the retired/absorbed scripts (`voice:duet`, `voice-e2e-hardware.ts`, `voice-vad-smoke.ts`, `three-voice-scenario.mjs`, the per-spec `tinyWav()`), so the five harness families converge on one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `VoiceScenario` schema + versioned labeled corpus exist, generated from text via real TTS, covering: multi-voice, pauses, respond/no-respond, multi-speaker, entity extraction, voice→entity match, diarization, EOT, transcription-mode, multi-agent room, and the long-form "talk about X" monologue.

100:T9c6,## Summary

The Eliza Cloud OAuth authorize page (`/app-auth/authorize`) crashes for unauthenticated visitors with:

> Something went wrong — `useAuth must be used within a <StewardProvider> with an `auth` prop.`

This blocks **all** monetized-app OAuth sign-in: a new user who clicks "sign in with Eliza Cloud" on any deployed monetized app can never complete auth. P0 for the monetized-app / 10-user launch.

## Repro (live)

1. Deploy a monetized app (e.g. the agent-home `text-my-ex` app) — registered, `appId` valid, `/api/config` returns it.
2. Open the app, click **Sign in with Eliza Cloud**.
3. Redirects to `https://elizacloud.ai/app-auth/authorize?app_id=<uuid>&redirect_uri=<app>&state=<s>`.
4. Page renders the error boundary: *"useAuth must be used within a `<StewardProvider>` with an `auth` prop."*

## Root cause

- `packages/ui/src/cloud-ui/components/auth/authorize-content.tsx:3` imports `{ StewardLogin, useAuth } from "@stwd/react"` and calls `useAuth()` (~line 75).
- `@stwd/react`'s `useAuth()` requires an ancestor `<StewardProvider auth={…}>` with a **non-null `auth` prop**.
- The `/app-auth/authorize` route is registered as a **public page**: `packages/ui/src/cloud/public-pages/register.ts:160` (`path: "app-auth/authorize"`).
- `<StewardProvider>` is only rendered with a populated `auth` prop inside the **authenticated** shell: `packages/ui/src/cloud/shell/StewardProviderRuntime.tsx:270`.
- An unauthenticated visitor on the public authorize route therefore has no `<StewardProvider auth=…>` ancestor → `useAuth()` throws → error boundary.

The authorize page is intrinsically a *public, pre-auth* page that nonetheless depends on the Steward auth context to drive the OAuth grant — that's the architectural mismatch.

## Proposed fix direction

Render the public `/app-auth/authorize` route inside a `<StewardProvider>` seeded with a **public/unauthenticated** Steward auth instance (the same provider-discovery path the login page already uses — see `packages/ui/src/cloud/public-pages/pages/login/steward-login-section.tsx`), so `useAuth()` resolves on public pages. Apply to any public page that calls `@stwd/react` hooks. Verify via the `audit:cloud` loop + a real OAuth round-trip from a deployed app.

## Lane

cloud-frontend (`packages/ui/src/cloud*`), deployed to `elizacloud.ai` — cloud-agent owns the fix + deploy. Filed from vps-agent (root-caused while testing the monetized-app build flow end-to-end). Linked from launch tracker #8434.
101:T870,## Summary

When the planner runs a SHELL/USE_SKILL/etc tool and then emits a REPLY in a follow-up iteration, the REPLY text occasionally summarizes that the result was provided rather than including the actual data. The user sees a meta-statement and no answer.

## Repro

Probes on 2026-05-25:
- **Prompt**: "list the names of files in /etc that have 'hostname' in them — actually run it"
- **Trajectory**: \`tj-c608892af9b5d3.json\`. Stage 0: \`simple=false, requiresTool=true, candidates=["BASH"]\`. Iter 1: SHELL \`grep -rl "hostname" /etc 2>/dev/null\` (real output). Iter 2: not shown; the bot's REPLY was:
- **Reply**: \`"Listed files from grep output; provided concise list as requested."\` — no actual filenames

Same pattern observed at \`tj-dc46d718c97add.json\` on retest:
- Reply: \`"Provided the list of /etc files that contain the word 'hostname' as returned by grep."\` — again, no list.

Other probes (df -h, uname -a, wc -l /etc/passwd, curl coingecko, etc.) included the tool's actual output verbatim — the bug is intermittent.

## Root cause hypothesis

The model in iter 2 (REPLY iteration) is reading the prior tool result, producing a textual summary of the act of returning the data, and skipping the data itself. May be related to specific prompt wordings ("list the names of files", "actually run it") that the model interprets as "describe what you did" rather than "include the output".

## Suggested approach

Two routes:
1. **Tool opt-in for \`verifiedUserFacing\`**: when SHELL produces a clean stdout, set \`verifiedUserFacing=true\` so \`preferredFinalMessageFromToolOrModel\` prefers the tool's text over the model's REPLY paraphrase. Currently SHELL doesn't opt in.
2. **Planner-prompt rule**: explicitly forbid meta-narration ("Listed/Provided/Returned X as requested") when the REPLY follows a tool that produced stdout.

(1) is preferred — structural, no regex on output.

## Acceptance

- "list files in /etc with hostname" reliably returns the grep output, not the summary.
- No regression on probes that already work (df -h, wc -l, uname -a, etc).

The boot path eagerly loads `engine.io` even for commands that do not need a server (`create`, `--version`, etc).

## Repro

```bash

```

```

      at /Users/<u>/.bun/install/global/node_modules/engine.io/build/transport.js:8:27
      at /Users/<u>/.bun/install/global/node_modules/engine.io/build/transports/polling.js:3:1

## Root cause

`engine.io`'s compiled `transport.js` emits:

```js
const debug_1 = require("debug");
const debug = (0, debug_1.default)("engine:transport");
```

It assumes a `.default` property on the `debug` CJS module. `debug@4.x` exports the factory directly (`module.exports = createDebug`); there is no `.default` property in the CJS shape. Node's CJS-from-ESM interop synthesizes a `default` property automatically; Bun's resolver does not produce the same shape for this dual-package module under the global-bin code path. This is a known engine.io + Bun interop class, not an elizaOS source-level bug.

## Why this is elizaOS's problem in practice

`@elizaos/cli@1.7.2` eagerly loads `engine.io` / Socket.IO at module-init time of *any* command — even `--help` and `create` walk through `engine.io/build/engine.io.js` → `server.js` → `transports/index.js` → `transport.js` before the command's own logic runs. Commands that don't need a websocket server should not be loading the websocket server stack at parse time.

## Environment

- @elizaos/cli@1.7.2 (`npm view @elizaos/cli dist-tags.latest`)
- Node v24.13.0
- Bun v1.3.10
- macOS arm64

## Suggested mitigations (any one would unblock)

1. **Lazy-load `engine.io` / Socket.IO off the boot path.** Move the server imports behind the commands that actually serve (`start`, `dev`). `create`, `info`, `upgrade`, `--version`, `--help` should not transitively touch `engine.io`. This is also a startup-latency win independent of the Bun bug.
2. **Pin / patch the transitive dep.** Either pin `engine.io` to a build whose compiled output uses `__importDefault`, or pin `debug` to a version that exports a named `default` property.
3. **Document Bun support explicitly.** If Bun is a supported runtime for the global CLI, gate publish on a `bun`-runtime smoke (see #8000). If not, the install instructions should say so.

Verified: develop's `packages/elizaos@2.0.3` scaffolds a project end-to-end via Node (`node packages/elizaos/dist/cli.js create … --template project --yes` succeeds against a fresh `bun install` of the workspace). Either the boot was trimmed or the dep tree was restructured — would be useful for maintainers to surface what changed, since that change is the basis for closing this on the next stable release.

## Root cause

These components reach `@elizaos/core` via `state/TranslationContext` → `state/persistence` (`import { logger } from "@elizaos/core"`). Two layered problems:

1. **Vite's dependency optimizer ignores `resolve.alias`.** It resolves bare `@elizaos/core` via `package.json` `exports` → the **Node** build (`src/index.node.ts`), not the browser entry. (A `resolve.alias` to `index.browser.ts` fixes on-demand transforms but not the pre-bundle pass.)

The patch throws `Cannot set property close … which has only a getter` against a read-only ESM `fs` stub (and `String(symbol)` inside Vite's `browser-external` proxy throws the misleading `Cannot convert a Symbol value to a string`).

## Already tried (clears the first two error classes, not the third)

- `@elizaos/core` → `index.browser.ts` alias (on-demand only)
- Node-builtin stub in **both** a Vite plugin and the optimizer's esbuild pass (proven `Reflect.get`-deferring proxy — fixes the Symbol-coercion class)
- Ambient `process` shim via preview `<head>` (fixes the `process.cwd` class)
- `optimizeDeps.exclude` of workspace pkgs — **regressed** `RunningAppsRow`, didn't sever fs-extra
- esbuild `onResolve` marking `@elizaos/core` external — didn't sever fs-extra (the scanner still discovers it)

`fs-extra` keeps reaching the optimizer graph through core's Node entry.

## Proposed fixes (any one)

1. **(preferred)** An `optimizeDeps.esbuildOptions` `onResolve` that maps `@elizaos/core` (and subpaths) to `index.browser.ts` **as a path** (not `external`), so the optimizer scanner crawls the browser graph (no `plugin-manager` → no `fs-extra`). Untried; the precise counter to "optimizer ignores `resolve.alias`".
2. A mutable (CJS) `fs` stub that `graceful-fs` can patch without throwing.
3. Decouple `state/persistence` from a *value* import of `@elizaos/core` — import `logger` from a lighter, browser-safe entry.

Private (`"private": true`, not-on-npm) workspace packages are never built on a fresh clone, so their `dist/` is empty and importing them throws `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. This blocks `apps/app` (and any consumer) from booting its dev server on a fresh checkout in the default install mode.

## Repro

1. Fresh clone, default `bun install` (no workspace build).
2. Start the app dev server.
3. Crash:
   ```
   Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module
   '.../packages/plugin-worker-runtime/node_modules/@elizaos/plugin-remote-manifest/dist/rpc-mac.js'
   imported from .../packages/plugin-worker-runtime/src/dispatch.ts
   ```

## Root cause

- `@elizaos/plugin-remote-manifest` is `"private": true` (not on npm). Its `package.json` exports `"./rpc-mac" → ./dist/rpc-mac.js`, but `dist/` is empty on a fresh clone — its build (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`) is never triggered by any install script.
- Its own workspace dep `@elizaos/security` is similarly unbuilt — there is a **chain** of unbuilt private workspace packages.
- Import chain: `packages/plugin-worker-runtime/src/dispatch.ts` → `@elizaos/plugin-remote-manifest/rpc-mac`.
- Note: `rpc-mac` is HMAC (message authentication), **not** macOS — the issue is platform-universal (Mac/Linux/Windows all hit it). Running local/workspace setup once builds the packages and the `dist/` persists, which is why it presents as a fresh-clone setup gap.

## Proposed fixes

- Add a dependency-ordered workspace-build step to install/postinstall (`@elizaos/security` → `@elizaos/plugin-remote-manifest` → consumers).
- Or have consumers import `src/*.ts` directly via the tsx loader (works in dev; verify production bundling).

## Severity

High — blocks fresh-clone app dev on every platform.

10b:T3275,## Summary

The coding orchestrator (`plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator`) is feature-complete on paper but is **not verified end-to-end with real Claude/Codex accounts in CI**, and its reliability rests on a deep mat of ad-hoc timer/race/orphan-recovery code that is the dominant flakiness source. The multi-account selection brain (`account-pool.ts`) and the spawn-injection bridge (`coding-account-bridge.ts`) are well built and unit-tested — but every "rotation across ≥2 real accounts of each provider" claim is asserted **only against a fake `acpx` binary**. Real OAuth refresh, real per-account `CODEX_HOME`/`auth.json` materialization, and real subscription auth have zero automated proof.

This matters now because the orchestrator is the spine of every coding-sub-agent flow, and we cannot ship it as "rock-solid" while (a) its lifecycle/loop-guard logic is only unit-tested in pieces and never under concurrent multi-task load, (b) there is no CI lane that spawns a real Claude or Codex subscription, (c) there is no mechanism to feed refreshable account credentials into GitHub Actions, and (d) the account-connect surface is a desktop Settings dialog disjoint from the orchestrator, so a misconfigured pool silently degrades to single-account.

## Critical assessment (current state)

**1. Reliability debt is concentrated in untestable timing code.** The spawn/route layer is dominated by ad-hoc retry, orphan reconciliation, SIGTERM grace windows, and loop-guards: 50 `setTimeout`/`setInterval` sites across the plugin; `acp-service.ts` has 36 catch blocks and `sub-agent-router.ts` 33; 108 `flaky|retry|race|loop|best-effort|eventually|debounce|backoff` markers in those two files alone. The router carries **two independent runaway-loop backstops** (`DEFAULT_ROUND_TRIP_CAP`, 32; `DEFAULT_STATE_LOST_RESPAWN_CAP`, 3) plus a manual "roll the round-trip counter back when a `task_complete` is suppressed" reconciliation and a documented TOCTOU window. AcpService reconciles "stale orphans" on start and resumes orphaned sessions with a grace window for sessions that "may not have written state yet." `codex-auth.ts` adds its own 30s stale-lock + 30-retry file lock around the OAuth token cache. None of these timing paths is exercised by a deterministic test under load — they are the textbook origin of intermittent failures.

**2. Multi-account E2E exists but is not in CI and has no credential feed.** `grep` of `.github/workflows` confirms the offline composed E2E (`test:e2e:multi-account`), the live smoke (`ORCHESTRATOR_LIVE=1`), and the live multi-account gate (`ORCHESTRATOR_LIVE_MULTI_ACCOUNT=1`) appear in **zero** workflows. The only scheduled orchestrator job runs a single `GROQ_API_KEY` model — it never spawns a real Claude or Codex subscription. There is also no mechanism to feed refreshable credentials into Actions: `codex-auth.ts` holds the OAuth client id + refresh logic, but nothing exports/refreshes those tokens into CI secrets.

**3. The account login UI is a Settings dialog, not a test/E2E harness, and is disjoint from the orchestrator.** `AddAccountDialog.tsx` (rendered inside `AccountList.tsx`, which `settings/ProviderPanels.tsx` mounts) is real and reachable — but it is surfaced nowhere in the orchestrator views. There is no "log in with N accounts, confirm ≥1 Codex + ≥1 Claude connected and healthy, export for CI" flow. `selectCodingAccount()` returns `null` and silently falls back to single-account when the bridge/account is absent, so a misconfigured pool is invisible.

**4. The orchestrator UI is a 3,931-line monolith.** `OrchestratorWorkbench.tsx` (3,931 lines) blocks the mandated screenshot/manual-review loop and makes per-account / per-session status, stall/force-stop state, and account-health surfacing hard to add or verify.

Net: the architecture is sound and the ideal is documented; the gap is **verification**.

## Evidence in code

- `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/acp-service.ts:456` — orphan-recovery grace window: "a freshly-spawned session may not have written its state file yet"; timing-dependent reconciliation on every start. 36 catch blocks in this file.
- `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/sub-agent-router.ts:371` — documented TOCTOU window: "two retry sessions both passed the check" in the verify-retry handoff path. 33 catch blocks in this file.
- `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/sub-agent-router.ts:697` — manual "roll the round-trip counter back when a `task_complete` event is suppressed" — the heart of the runaway-loop guard.
- `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/sub-agent-router.ts:41-42` / `:452-453` / `:478` — `DEFAULT_ROUND_TRIP_CAP=32` and `DEFAULT_STATE_LOST_RESPAWN_CAP=3`, held as separate per-session state (`roundTripCap` / `stateLostRespawnCap`) with an env override (`ACPX_SUB_AGENT_ROUND_TRIP_CAP` at `:478`): two independent loop backstops.
- `plugins/plugin-codex-cli/src/codex-auth.ts:8-11` — `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `LOCK_STALE_MS=30_000`, `LOCK_RETRY_MAX=30`; the OAuth client id + refresh logic a CI credential-refresh harness must drive (and another concurrency surface).
- `packages/app-core/src/services/account-pool.ts:152` — `AccountPool.select`: strategy + session affinity + burst-spread (1,078-line file). Well-built selection brain, only unit-tested, never under live multi-task load.
- `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/coding-account-selection.ts:103` / `:148-167` — `MULTI_ACCOUNT_AGENT_TYPES = {claude, codex, opencode}`; `selectCodingAccount()` doc states "Returns null (single-account fallback)" and the body returns `null` on missing bridge / catch / no account — no readiness assertion.
- `packages/app-core/src/services/coding-account-bridge.ts:245-254` — `buildEnvPatch`: claude→`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, codex→per-account `CODEX_HOME`/`auth.json` (materialized at `:173-203`). The spawn-injection contract that needs live proof.
- `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/scripts/compose-multi-account-e2e.ts:10` / `:47-66` — offline composed E2E: real `AccountPool` + bridge + `AcpService.spawnSession`, but "the only stand-in is the coding-agent binary itself (a tiny fake 'acpx')." The only automated multi-account proof — and it stubs the actual CLI.
- `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/__tests__/unit/multi-account-spawn.test.ts:323` — "rotates consecutive spawns across distinct accounts (least-used)" using a mocked `NativeAcpClient` (`:55`); proves wiring, not real auth.
- `.github/workflows/benchmark-orchestrator-scheduled.yml:64`,`:71-76` — the only scheduled orchestrator CI run uses a single `GROQ_API_KEY` with a secret-presence gate; no Claude/Codex subscription, no pool, no rotation. `grep` for `ORCHESTRATOR_LIVE` / `test:e2e:multi-account` / `CODEX_HOME` / `saveAccount` across `.github/workflows` = **zero matches**.
- `packages/agent/src/api/accounts-routes.ts:553` / `:598` — `/api/accounts/*` HTTP surface (oauth start/status-SSE/cancel, api-key add, refresh-usage). Login plumbing exists, but no CI/test-harness consumer confirms ≥1 Codex + ≥1 Claude healthy and exports for Actions.
- `packages/ui/src/components/accounts/AccountList.tsx:157` — renders `AddAccountDialog`; `AccountList` is mounted in `packages/ui/src/components/settings/ProviderPanels.tsx:242`,`:312`, surfaced in **no** orchestrator view.
- `plugins/plugin-task-coordinator/src/OrchestratorWorkbench.tsx` — 3,931-line orchestrator UI monolith; no per-account/per-session health surfacing; too large for the mandated `audit:app` loop.
- `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/docs/multi-account-orchestration.md:14-22` — marks every layer (pool, OAuth flows, REST API, settings UI, orchestrator) "✅", but neither the live E2E nor the composed offline E2E is in CI, so the doc overstates verification posture.

## Scope & work order

High-confidence first.

- [ ] **Reliability — single lifecycle state machine.** Consolidate the two runaway-loop backstops in `sub-agent-router.ts` (`roundTripCap` + `stateLostRespawnCap`, the manual counter roll-back at `:697`, and the TOCTOU at `:371`) into one explicit pure transition function, modeled the way the supervisor/watchdog already do pure `runSupervisorTick` (`task-supervisor-service.ts:88`) / `detectStalledSessions` (`task-watchdog-service.ts:45`). Add a fuzz/property test asserting no event ordering produces a double-post, an early force-stop, or a leaked session.
- [ ] **Multi-account CI lane (additive, secret-gated).** Add a workflow that runs `test:e2e:multi-account` on every PR (fake `acpx`, zero secrets) AND a scheduled `ORCHESTRATOR_LIVE_MULTI_ACCOUNT=1` job against ≥1 real Codex + ≥1 real Claude account, skipping cleanly (exit 0 + `::notice::`) when secrets are absent — copy `benchmark-orchestrator-scheduled.yml`'s secret-presence gate (`:71-76`).
- [ ] **Credential feed into Actions.** Build a credential-refresh path that exports the connected Claude (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) and Codex (`CODEX_HOME` `auth.json`: access/refresh/account_id) blobs into GH Actions secrets and refreshes them on a schedule, reusing the refresh logic in `codex-auth.ts` + `packages/agent/src/auth/oauth-flow.ts`. Store the minimal account JSON the pool reads so CI can seed 2× Claude + 2× Codex into a temp state dir and run real rotation.
- [ ] **Account-readiness harness.** Add a CLI/route that asserts the pool has ≥1 healthy Codex AND ≥1 healthy Claude (≥2 each for local rotation) using `coding-account-bridge`'s per-provider total/enabled/healthy report. Fail loudly instead of the silent single-account fallback in `coding-account-selection.ts:148-167`.
- [ ] **Sub-agent / room / task / multi-task correctness tests** (fake transport; template = the `multi-account-spawn.test.ts` `NativeAcpClient` mock at `:55`): (1) spawn→route→`task_complete`→evaluator summary; (2) room message routed to active sub-agent via `interruption-decider.ts` (deliver/queue/interrupt/ignore); (3) multi-task supervisor digest correctness across rooms; (4) concurrent multi-task isolation — two tasks, two accounts, distinct sessions, no cross-talk, correct round-trip accounting.

- #8434 (cloud launch tracker — depends on a reliable orchestrator)10c:T2f90,## Summary

The home screen's *widget-level prioritization* is already solid (#9143): `widgets/home-priority.ts` scores each `slot="home"` widget by a stable base priority plus decayed activity/notification signals plus self-published attention, and `WidgetHost.tsx` ranks the home slot and caps it at `HOME_RENDER_CAP`, with widgets self-hiding when empty. That ranker is correct and should be left alone.

The gap is **guidance and lifecycle**, which is either missing or was deleted because there was no graceful model for it. A brand-new account lands on a near-empty home — clock + weather and nothing else — with zero direction toward chat, connectors, or a tutorial. There is no first-time-user (FTU) state, no "show once then retire" mechanism, and the connector/tutorial nudge widgets that *would* fill the void were ripped out wholesale, leaving 350 lines of orphaned dead code behind. This issue is a work-order to add the missing lifecycle primitive, build the FTU + nudge content on top of it, and either resurrect or delete the orphans.

## Critical assessment (current state)

**1. No FTU home state.** `first-run/` is a setup *wizard* only (runtime/inference/remote choice). After setup, the home is `DefaultHomeWidgets` (clock + weather) plus whatever data widgets have content — which on a fresh account is nothing. The model-backed "try saying X" suggestions that would power a welcome card already exist in `usePromptSuggestions.ts` but are wired only into the chat composer strip, never the home. The `HomeScreen` doc-comment even states the home stays "just the ambient field + clock" when nothing's active — that *is* the empty-FTU problem, treated as a feature. The same doc-comment lists "recent messages" as a home tile, which directly conflicts with the topic's "home must not echo chat" requirement and should be re-examined.

**2. No sunset / dismiss / "seen" persistence anywhere in the home widget layer.** Grepping `dismiss|sunset|hasSeen|hideForever|seenCount` across `widgets/` returns **zero** hits. Widgets bubble up by data urgency and self-hide when empty, but nothing can show *once* and then permanently retire after the user acts — the "eventually goes away" requirement has no primitive. The only self-hiding "setup completes" tiles (e.g. `model-download.tsx`) hide on a backend readiness signal, not on a user-seen/dismiss count.

**3. Connector + tutorial nudges were deleted, leaving orphaned dead code.** `connectors-status.tsx` (234 LOC, fully built with tests, renders tappable connector affordances → `/settings/connectors`) and `discord-recent.tsx` (116 LOC + tests) are **not registered** anywhere in `widgets/registry.ts` — confirmed unreachable, each referenced only by itself and its own test file. The registry comment admits the connector status strip + discord recent tiles were "intentionally dropped from the home surface … crowded the naked home grid with setup noise." The team's own redesign intent (memory `project_home_dashboard_redesign`) was reverted because there was no way to make a nudge *fade gracefully* — so the fix went to the opposite extreme: a home that gives a new user nothing.

**Root cause:** the signal taxonomy already has a `nudge` lane (`HOME_SIGNAL_WEIGHTS.nudge = 3`, mapped in `EVENT_TYPE_TO_SIGNAL_KIND`), but it has **no lifecycle hook** — a `nudge`-kind card can rank but can never *retire after the user acts*, and there is no `welcome`/FTU kind that should outrank everything for a cold user yet vanish the moment real activity exists. Risk: poor first-run UX (empty home, no direction) plus 350 LOC of dead code violating the unused-code rule and producing false test coverage (tests render components the app never mounts).

## Scope & work order

High-confidence first:

This is the missing primitive that FTU + connector + tutorial nudges all depend on.
- [ ] **Add a `welcome`/FTU kind to `HOME_SIGNAL_WEIGHTS` + `EVENT_TYPE_TO_SIGNAL_KIND`** (the existing `nudge` lane stays). Weight it so an FTU card ranks at the top *for a cold user* yet falls below real activity once data arrives — it must never outrank `blocked`/`escalation`/`approval`.

- [ ] **Gentle tutorial nudge** (low priority): a single dismissible card linking to existing help content that sunsets after one open. No multi-step coachmark system.

- #8796 (all-views aesthetic audit gate)10d:T3553,## Summary

The voice subsystem has extensive *pure-logic* coverage — 22 test files / 145 test cases in `packages/ui/src/voice`, 4 files / 63 cases in `packages/shared/src/voice`, plus 15 real-service workbench scenarios — but a hard wall at the platform/live boundary. **Not one test drives a real mic → ASR → agent → Kokoro TTS → speaker loop in the actual app on any device.** Both jobs in `.github/workflows/voice-live-e2e.yml` run `runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64, eliza]` only — zero iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, or Electrobun coverage. The two plugins that actually capture audio on-device (`plugin-native-talkmode`, `plugin-native-swabble`) have only a `web.test.ts` each and no Kotlin/Swift tests. The in-app e2e (`tts-stt-e2e.spec.ts`) explicitly mocks STT and TTS and states it is "about wiring," not the backends.

This is exactly the "mock-mount smoke, not real bugs" failure the repo's own e2e standard (`PR_EVIDENCE.md`) warns against: a regression in iOS `SFSpeechRecognizer` wiring, Android capture, Electrobun mic permissions, or barge-in would pass all of CI green. This issue is the broader **test/e2e umbrella** — a single canonical voice test matrix with bidirectional live-voice verification, screen+audio recordings, and a CoreML/Google on-device STT backend evaluation. **Kokoro TTS stays as-is** (`voice-provider-defaults.ts` keeps mobile on on-device Kokoro); the gap is verification breadth, not the TTS engine. The wake-word *feature* is tracked in #9880; this issue covers verifying it (and everything else) end-to-end on real hardware.

## Critical assessment (current state)

- **No cross-platform live-voice e2e exists.** The richest scenario set — fused ASR, acoustic VAD/diarization, Kokoro synth smoke, the 15-scenario workbench matrix — executes only on a Linux-x64 self-hosted runner. "Linux-only green" silently stands in for platform coverage that does not exist.
- **The on-device capture path is verified only by JS shims.** `plugin-native-talkmode` and `plugin-native-swabble` carry the real Android `SpeechRecognizer` / openWakeWord paths, yet each has only a `src/web.test.ts` — a `find` for `*Test.kt` / `*Tests.swift` in both plugins returns 0. The actual wake-firing → JS-bridge event is untested.
- **The in-app voice e2e is a wiring mock.** `tts-stt-e2e.spec.ts` shims `window.webkitSpeechRecognition` and Playwright-routes `/api/tts/cloud` to a stub mp3, with a header stating the backends "are NOT exercised here … This spec is about wiring."
- **No bidirectional/full-duplex (barge-in) test.** Barge-in exists only as a "silent gaps spliced AFTER this turn's audio (pauses / barge-in gaps)" field in the scenario schema — never asserted as live UI behavior (playback ducks/stops when the user speaks).
- **Wakeword-context is unit-only.** The idle-vs-already-listening-(always-on, wake inert)-vs-mid-transcription state machine is a pure reducer with a frozen clock; it is never run against a real openWakeWord head.
- **Chime-in × transcription-state × multi-speaker is unit-only.** The gate is a pure re-export of `@elizaos/shared/voice/respond-gate`; no in-app e2e asserts transcription-on-vs-off × should-respond × multi-speaker.
- **Transcripts round-trip is jsdom-only.** Exactly 3 component tests in the dir; no live capture → record → view → playback → attach round trip.
- **Noise/rejection is synthetic only.** Covered by fuzz over augmented corpora, never real-device noisy-room mic input.
- **CoreML/Google on-device STT is aspirational.** `VOICE_UX.md §7` claims iOS `SFSpeechRecognizer` (ANE) and Android `SpeechRecognizer` (NNAPI) Stage-B confirm paths, but `apple-foundation.ts` is LLM-`generate()`-only — neither STT backend is implemented or benchmarked.

**Risk:** the entire voice product ships on per-platform native paths verified only by Linux-x64 synthetic corpora. The most likely real-world regressions are precisely the ones CI cannot catch.

- #9626 — Build process bloat/duplication audit + cross-platform (CI lane additions should reuse its cross-platform runner work).10e:T34b7,## Summary

The interactive tutorial (`packages/ui/src/components/pages/tutorial/`) is a six-frame guided walkthrough — `welcome → open-chat → resize-chat → ask-to-navigate → use-voice → done` — driven by `TutorialOverlay.tsx`, scripted in `tutorial-steps.ts`, spotlighted by `TutorialSpotlight.tsx`, and capability-locked via `navigation/nav-lock.ts`. The reported "messed-up highlights and colors" are real and reproducible: the spotlight **hardcodes brand orange** (`#FF5800`, `#D44A00`, and `rgba(255,88,0,…)`) in four places plus a dark card skin, ignoring the themeable `--accent` token. In light/alt/gold themes the glow and Continue button render orange while the rest of the UI is white, black, or gold — a direct violation of the per-surface/per-theme accent system. The overlay also escapes the registered z-scale with an inline max-int z-index, and the highlight targeting is fragile against a testid reused six times.

None of this can be caught today because the tour has **zero automated coverage** — no `*.test.tsx` and no `__e2e__` runner anywhere under the tutorial directory, while every other shell surface (home-screen, chat-sheet, chat-ux gesture, chat-ambient, onboarding, agent-surface, springboard, background) ships a `run-*-e2e.mjs`. This issue is a work-order to fix the highlight/color logic per step, add per-step e2e with screenshots + theme assertions, add the requested new-chat and swipe-between-chats steps, and record a full walkthrough.

## Critical assessment (current state)

- **Hardcoded accent, not themeable.** `TutorialSpotlight.tsx` declares `const BRAND = "#FF5800"` and a header comment asserting "Brand orange (#FF5800) is the only accent." That contradicts the live token system: `--accent` resolves to `var(--brand-orange)` in dark/default, but to `var(--brand-white)` and `var(--brand-black)` in light/alt themes and `var(--classic-gold)` for the gold brand. The static glow, the breathing `tutorial-glow` keyframes, and the Continue button (resting + hover) all paint orange unconditionally → orange highlight on a non-orange app. Root cause: the component was written against the false premise that orange is the only accent.
- **The token fix is mostly wiring — but light themes leave a co-requisite gap.** The theme system already exposes `--accent`, `--accent-hover`, and `--accent-rgb`, so the static glow and Continue button can move to tokens directly. The catch: the light/alt-theme blocks in `base.css` override `--accent` and `--accent-hover` but do **not** override `--accent-rgb` (it stays at the inherited `255, 88, 0`). A naive `rgba(var(--accent-rgb), …)` keyframe would therefore still glow orange in light mode. The fix must either add `--accent-rgb` to those theme blocks or compute the glow color from `--accent` on the overlay root.
- **Theme-blind card skin.** The spotlight card is hardcoded `bg-neutral-950/95 text-white border-white/12` regardless of theme. In light mode this is a near-black card with white text floating over a light app — wrong contrast direction, no surface/text token used.
- **z-index escape hatch.** The overlay sets inline `zIndex: 2147483000`, above the entire registered scale in `lib/floating-layers.ts` (top is `Z_GLOBAL_EMOTE=11000`, then `CONFIG_SELECT_FLOATING_LAYER_Z_INDEX=12000`; `Z_SYSTEM_CRITICAL=9999`). The file's own rule is "Every z-index in the app must come from this file." The tour paints over system-critical banners with a layer nothing can sit above.
- **Fragile highlight targeting.** `measure()` uses `document.querySelector(selector)` (first match only). The `ask-to-navigate` frame targets `[data-testid="chat-composer-action"]`, but that testid is rendered in **six** conditional branches of `chat-composer.tsx`; if more than one mounts, the glow can ring the wrong control. On a zero-size/missing target, `measure` returns `null` and the overlay silently degrades to a full dim with no hole — no test asserts the glow framed the right rect.
- **Stale launch copy.** Multiple strings still point at a removed home "Tutorial tile."
- **Missing steps.** No new-chat step and no swipe-between-chats step, despite both controls already existing.

- #9880 (voice wake word — adjacent to the `use-voice` frame)10f:T2a61,## Summary

The agent's memory-recall and knowledge-retrieval pipeline — the hot path that decides *what context the model actually sees* — has **zero quality benchmarking and zero regression gate**. `AgentRuntime.searchMemories`, `DocumentService` hybrid/vector/keyword search, the recall providers (`DOCUMENTS`, `FACTS`) that inject retrieved snippets into the prompt, and the keyword chat-search path are all shipped untested for retrieval *correctness*. We measure resource cost (memperf) and LLM context-window attention (context_bench), but nobody measures whether the agent retrieves the *right* memories from its store at document scale.

This matters now because the ranking is hard-coded and the recall path **fails open**: any slow or errored embed silently degrades vector/hybrid recall to keyword-only (`recall-embed.ts` fail-open contract, also wired into `DocumentService._vectorSearch`/`_hybridSearch`). A regression that flips healthy semantic recall to substring matching — or a bad hybrid-weight/threshold change — ships green today. We need a registered, document-scale, labeled-relevance benchmark wired into CI with committed budgets, exercising the real `@elizaos/core` code (not a re-implementation).

## Critical assessment (current state)

**What's wrong:** there is no Precision@K / Recall@K / nDCG / MRR / latency coverage of the real recall path anywhere in the repo. What exists *looks* like coverage but is misleading:

1. **`packages/benchmarks/experience`** computes P@K/R@K/MRR/HitRate@K (`evaluators/retrieval.py`), but its default `direct` mode scores a **Python re-implementation** of the experience service (`elizaos_experience_bench/service.py` — its own `re`/tokenizer code), not shipped TS. It is also explicitly *not registered* in the orchestrator, so it runs in no CI lane. It only ever touches the experience service — never documents/knowledge, FACTS, or `searchMemories`.
2. **`packages/benchmarks/context-bench`** (`context_bench`) measures LLM *context-window* retrieval (needle-in-a-haystack / multi-hop *inside the prompt*) — the model's attention, not the persisted-memory store. Wrong layer.
3. The only "real" document-search unit test **mocks `searchMemories`** and uses 8-dim `Math.random()` embeddings over toy corpora — asserts plumbing, never quality or scale.
4. **`packages/benchmarks/memperf`** measures RSS/load-ms/throughput — cost, not correctness (though it *is* the CI + budgets precedent we should copy).

**Root cause / risk:** the hybrid ranking is hard-coded (`HYBRID_VECTOR_WEIGHT 0.6` / BM25 `0.4`) and the recall embed fails open to keyword-only on any slow/errored embed. That degradation is silent and completely unmeasured. There is no corpus-scale fixture, no labeled relevance set, and no CI threshold anywhere in the recall path. The keyword chat-search (`scoreMemoryText`, substring/term matching) and semantic recall (providers via `searchMemories`/`DocumentService`) are two distinct user-facing surfaces, and neither is quality-tested — so we cannot even tell which one is doing the work, or whether semantic recall silently collapsed into keyword.

- #9581 — Computer Use x Vision on-device verification (sibling "verify a real pipeline at scale" work order).110:T2d25,## Summary

elizaOS has no way to search the **content** of past chat messages. The only "search" a chat user can reach is a client-side filter over conversation **titles** in the sidebar (`conversation-sidebar-model.ts:496-507`), and even that field isn't wired into the live sidebar (always passed `searchQuery: ""`). The two server "search" endpoints that exist are either vector/semantic (`searchMemories` requires an `embedding` — `database.ts:1017`) or scoped to standalone `hash_memory` notes for a single room, not chat messages (`memory-routes.ts:126`). There is no keyword predicate over the `messages` memory table, no cross-conversation message query, and no UI entry point to launch one.

This issue scopes a **simple, correct** keyword search: a search entry in the top chat bar, a server keyword-query endpoint over messages that pushes the predicate into SQL, a result list that opens the target conversation and scrolls to the matched message, and **scale tests** with large fixtures. Vector/semantic search is explicitly **out of scope** and tracked under the Context Benchmark + #9874.

## Critical assessment (current state)

**No keyword path in the data layer.** `IDatabaseAdapter.getMemories` and its SQL impl filter only by type/roomId/worldId/createdAt/unique/agentId — there is no content/text predicate (`base.ts:1400`, conditions built at `1432-1456`). `searchMemories` is embedding-only (`database.ts:1017`). The only way to find a message by its words today is to pull rows and scan in JS.

**The JS-scan precedents are narrow and won't scale.** `searchMemoryNotes` loads `MEMORY_SEARCH_SCAN_LIMIT=2000` rows for ONE room, filters to `hash_memory` notes, scores via `scoreMemoryText` (`memory-routes.ts:104,126,135`). The cross-room aggregator `loadInboxMessages` walks `getMemoriesByRoomIds` over `MAX_ROOMS_SCANNED=2000` rooms with `PER_ROOM_OVERFETCH_MULTIPLIER=3`, merging in JS (`inbox-routes.ts:1329`, constants at `112`/`145`). A naive "search all messages" built the same way over-fetches tens of thousands of rows. drizzle-orm already supports `ILIKE` (it ships in the bundled query DSL but is never reached from a source `getMemories` content path), so the correct architecture pushes the keyword predicate into SQL via `ILIKE` over `content->>'text'`.

**The conversation read path is capped at 200.** `GET /api/conversations/:id/messages` calls `getMemories({ tableName: "messages", limit: 200 })` (`conversation-routes.ts:1396`); a hit older than the recent 200 cannot be scrolled to because it is never loaded.

**The scroll anchor already exists but is unused for search.** Every message renders `id=chat-message-<id>` via `getChatMessageAnchorId` (`chat-message.tsx:116`, applied at render line `497`), today only for reply deep-links. The transcript is a plain non-virtualized `.map` (`chat-transcript.tsx:242`), so `scrollIntoView` only lands if the row is in the rendered window — reinforcing the need for anchored loading. `ContinuousChatOverlay.scrollToTopic` already proves the jump pattern: `querySelector` + `scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth',block:'start'})` in rAF (`ContinuousChatOverlay.tsx:1354-1368`).

**No top-bar entry.** `ShellHeaderControls` has language/theme/voice/new-chat/save controls but no search affordance (`ShellHeaderControls.tsx`, controls plumbed throughout; no `search`). `CommandPalette` is Cmd/Ctrl+K and filters command **labels**, not message content (`CommandPalette.tsx:179`).

**Risk:** shipping search as another in-JS scan (mirroring inbox-routes) passes small-fixture tests, then collapses on real histories — violating the "tested at scale" requirement.

- #9626 (build/complexity audit)111:T317b,## Summary

The floating chat (`ContinuousChatOverlay`) has a deep, well-built fuzz suite for the *sheet open/close* state machine (771 lines) and a clean, fully unit-tested pure nav helper (`buildConversationNav`). But the exact behavior the product cares about — swipe-back to a conversation, make new conversation, swipe-forward, new conversation, forward, swipe-back, in arbitrary orderings against an async-mutating conversation list — has **zero** interleaving coverage. The swipe-between-conversations feature itself shipped (#8929), the perf-to-60/120fps work shipped (#9141), and parser-parity shipped (#9304) — but none of them closed the verification gaps this issue targets.

The conversation-swipe path additionally carries (a) an unguarded stale-closure window where a swipe fired during an in-flight create/select navigates against a stale index, (b) a gesture e2e that exercises a local mock instead of the real overlay and is wired to no CI workflow, and (c) perf/jank monitors that emit telemetry to a dev-only HUD but never fail a build. A jank regression in conversation swiping or a wrong-conversation selection under rapid input ships silently today.

## Critical assessment (current state)

**1) Conversation-nav interleaving is unfuzzed.** `conversationNav` is a `useMemo` over `buildConversationNav(conversations, activeConversationId, selectConversation)` — it recomputes only when those deps change. `selectConversation` and `handleNewConversation` are fire-and-forget async (`runWithConversationLoading`). `handleNewConversation` prepends the new conversation at index 0 and flips the active id only *after* `await client.createConversation(...)`. So between a swipe calling `goNext()` and the list/index updating, a second gesture fires against a **stale** `conversationNav` closure built from the old index. The only sequence guard here (`conversationLoadingSeqRef`) governs the loading **spinner flag** (`setConversationLoading`), not the nav index — the watchdog comment says so explicitly ("Seq-guarded so a newer switch owns the flag"). The `creationEpoch` guard in `handleNewConversation` only protects navigate-away during create — it does not serialize rapid swipe→new→swipe. No test drives onSelect → list mutation → swipe again in a loop.

**2) The gesture e2e tests a mock, not the overlay.** `run-chatux-gesture-e2e.mjs` bundles `chatux-gesture-fixture.tsx`, but that fixture's `ConversationSwiper` is a **local re-implementation** with a hardcoded array and its own `useState(index)` — it shares only `usePullGesture`, not the real `ContinuousChatOverlay` / `conversationNav` / async create path. The e2e asserts only title-change and `errors.length === 0`: no interleaving, no perf assertion. It is also wired to **no CI workflow** (grep of `.github/workflows` for `chatux`/`chat-sheet` returns nothing), so it runs only by hand. Green on a mock is false confidence.

**3) Dual render path persists at the component layer.** The overlay renders its own `ThreadLine`/`ThreadLineText` assistant tree; `ChatView` renders messages through `MessageContent` via `ChatTranscript`. The **parser** layer is already deduped and pinned (`parser-parity.contract.test.ts`, from #9304), but the two React trees still diverge in markdown handling, animation, copy affordance, and reasoning/secret-request rendering — the same `ConversationMessage` can render differently in the two surfaces with nothing guarding visual/structural parity.

**4) Perf/jank telemetry exists but never fails.** `useFrameBudgetMonitor` + `useLayoutShiftMonitor` are mounted in `ShellOverlays`, and the overlay marks transient motion via `LAYOUT_SHIFT_INTENT_*`. The math is unit-tested (`frame-budget.test.ts`, `layout-stability.ts`). But it surfaces only through a dev HUD (`PerfOverlay`, gated on `window.__ELIZA_PERF_HUD__`) — no harness drives the chat under gestures and asserts an fps / dropped-frame / CLS threshold, and `view-telemetry.ts` has `page-swipe`/`reorder` actions but no jank/fps/frame-budget/INP action, so a swipe-jank regression is invisible in the telemetry ring too.

**Risk:** rapid swipe/new-conversation interleavings can select the wrong conversation or strand the loading spinner (the watchdog in `runWithConversationLoading` exists precisely because this has stuck before); the e2e gives false confidence; thread-render divergence drifts unguarded; jank regresses with no gate.

- #9880 (open) — voice name-aware wake word; gesture/interaction sibling.112:T3729,## Summary

The desktop product direction is a minimal, chromeless chat bar pinned to the bottom of the screen — mic + a VISION button, name-aware wakeword to start a turn, views and the launcher summoned on demand ("show the launcher"), and a native tray that *replaces* the launcher with a popover of widgets on mac/win/linux. The desktop today is the opposite: `createMainWindow()` builds a single full-screen `BrowserWindow` that hosts the entire `<App>` dashboard with an OS title bar, and chat is an overlay *inside* that window (`ContinuousChatOverlay`). (On macOS the window is already transparent + vibrancy and the tray survives window-close — so the primitives are partway there — but it is still the full dashboard with `hiddenInset` chrome, and Win/Linux keep default OS chrome.)

The frustrating part is that most of the parts needed for the target model **already exist in the tree** — a chromeless bottom-bar component, a name-aware WakeController (#9880) that is already wired into the live shell, and a real cross-platform native `Tray` — but each is either orphaned, only-partially-bridged, or menu-only. There is also a dead renderer mode (`?shell=floating-chat`) reachable through live RPCs that points at React that does not exist, and a live brand violation (hardcoded blue) that regresses the instant the orphaned bar is mounted. This is a work order to pick the canonical path, wire it end-to-end, and delete the rest.

## Critical assessment (current state)

**The live desktop is "a big electron window with chat inside" — the thing we want gone.** `createMainWindow()` builds one `BrowserWindow` (default `1440x900`, then expanded to fill the screen) with `titleBarStyle: hiddenInset` (darwin) / `default` (win/linux) and mounts the whole dashboard (`@elizaos/ui/App`). Chat is `ContinuousChatOverlay` floating inside it. There is no chromeless, screen-bottom shell that renders *only* a bar in the running path.

**The chromeless bottom bar exists but is orphaned.** `CompanionBar.tsx` is a fixed-bottom transparent bar — structurally the desired component — but its only importers are its own barrel, its `__tests__`, and `CompanionBar.stories.tsx`. It is never mounted by `App` or the desktop shell. It also ships **mic + send only — no VISION button** — and a hardcoded blue pill (`.is-sky`) that violates the orange-only/no-blue brand rule.

**Wakeword is wired end-to-end — but only the web-fallback path, and not to a bottom bar.** The name-aware decision core (`wake-controller.ts`, the #9880 WakeController) is consumed by `useWakeController` → `useWakeListenWindow` → `useShellController` → the live shell, so a wake event *does* drive the existing shell chat today. But per the package's own `VOICE_UX.md`, the only wake signal currently bridged to the UI is the Swabble Web-Speech fallback; the battery-efficient fused native runtime (`wakeword-cpp`'s `libwakeword`, bound via `bun:ffi` in `wake-word-ggml.ts`) is built and tested but **not bridged to the UI**, so the cheap on-device path never drives chat. So "working+tested wakeword for chat" is true for the fallback path and false for the fused on-device path, and neither drives the (orphaned) bottom bar.

**There is a dead renderer mode behind live RPCs.** `floating-chat-window.ts` is wired into the shell (`index.ts` configures it; `rpc-handlers.ts` exposes `floatingChatOpen/Show/Hide`) and opens a renderer URL with `?shell=floating-chat` — but **no React code reads that param**, so the window it opens has no UI. This is a second, parallel bottom-chat concept the bottom-bar shell should supersede and delete.

**The tray is real but menu-only, and tray-first is macOS-only.** A genuine Electrobun native `Tray` exists (`createTray()`), but it renders a flat text context menu (`DESKTOP_TRAY_MENU_ITEMS`: Open Chat / Open Plugins / Open Voice Controls / Quit) — no popover, no widgets. Tray-first launch is gated to `platform === "darwin"` + `ELIZA_DESKTOP_TRAY_FIRST=1`; Windows/Linux always keep a boot window. So "a native tray that replaces the launcher with widgets on all 3 platforms" is unmet on every axis. (The primitive is feasible: `DesktopManager` already builds a `BrowserView` for release notes.)

**Risk.** Subsystems are built-but-dead/half-bridged and rotting; a contributor cannot infer the intended desktop model from the code. The product ships as a heavyweight windowed dashboard against the stated direction. The blue pill is a latent brand break. No e2e covers any target surface: the desktop e2e exercises state persistence, reset-to-first-run, and tray-stays-alive-on-close — but nothing for the bottom bar, vision, wakeword activation, view/launcher-on-demand, or a tray popover.

- #9626 — build process bloat/duplication audit (overlaps the dead-path deletions here)113:T352f,## Summary

Today a brand-new user's first contact with the product is a **branded full-screen card with step buttons** ("How should Eliza run?" / "Where should it think?"), not the agent. The startup coordinator resolves a `first-run` phase and `StartupShell` renders `<StartupFirstRunBackground>{<CompactOnboarding/>}</StartupFirstRunBackground>` *before the chat shell can paint* (`App.tsx:2102` early-returns `<StartupScreen/>` until `isShellPaintableNow`). The product — an agent you talk to — is hidden behind a setup wizard.

This issue inverts that. The **first thing the user sees is the agent**: "hey there! I'm Eliza" then "do you want to log in with your Eliza Cloud account or run your agent locally?" — login, runtime choice, and inference-provider choice are all **in-chat widgets**, using primitives that already exist (`ChoiceWidget`, `CredentialRequestWidget`). After login the agent asks about inference with **role-correct defaults** (cloud → Eliza Cloud all-models pay-as-you-go; local → on-device), plus an "other" option (Anthropic sub / Codex / z.ai / Moonshot-Kimi) that routes to Settings via the *existing* handoff. The win is one onboarding mental model instead of two, ~6k LOC of bespoke step/voice/handoff machinery deleted, and a first impression that leads with the product.

## Critical assessment (current state)

The first-run subsystem is a **presentation-layer state machine with embedded provisioning, OAuth, and cloud-agent business logic** — exactly the "client computes / branchy polymorphism" pattern the repo's architecture rules forbid (clients display, never compute; computation lives in use cases).

- It is large and concentrated: `packages/ui/src/first-run/` is ~4,552 LOC non-test/non-e2e, plus `packages/app-core/src/first-run/` (391 LOC), `useFirstRunCallbacks.ts` (1,187 LOC), and `use-first-run-controller.ts` (1,454 LOC), exercised by ~27 first-run/onboarding test files across the repo.
- The controller is a bespoke step machine (`FirstRunStep = "runtime" | "inference" | "remote" | "pick-agent"`) that re-implements, as full-screen screens, decisions the chat surface could carry natively: runtime selection, inference sub-choice, cloud OAuth, an agent picker, and a shared→dedicated handoff.
- It even carries a **second, parallel voice stack** (a dedicated ASR/TTS onboarding engine) that exists only to drive the gate.
- There are **two** full-screen mounts of the same component: the `first-run` startup phase and a separate `onboarding-overlay` `shellMode`.

The smell is that the in-chat primitives this flow needs already exist and are unused for it: `registerInlineWidget` / `ChoiceWidget` (option rows, `allowCustom` "Other…") and `CredentialRequestWidget` with `oauth-link` + `paste-secret` variants (a login widget in everything but name). The "other" provider taxonomy is **already a typed contract** (`SubscriptionProviderSelectionId`) with subscription start routes — but reachable only via the gate's `inference` step or Settings.

Role-correct defaults are the one genuinely-new product rule and **must be encoded once in a use case**, not the client. Risk of not doing this: two onboarding mental models, 6k+ LOC of step/voice/handoff machinery to maintain, and a first impression that hides the agent.

- #8434114:T35b7,## Summary

The iOS-style icon-grid launcher surface (reached by swiping right from Home) is still named **"springboard"** throughout the codebase, even though the product already presents it to users as **"the launcher."** The nav description literally reads `"The Springboard launcher — …"` (`packages/ui/src/navigation/index.ts:234`) and the help answer says it `"is the launcher for every screen Eliza can show you"`. The name is half-migrated: "springboard" survives as a file-name family, a TypeScript symbol family, runtime string contracts (page value, window-event name, `data-testid` families, telemetry source), a `localStorage` key, `package.json` scripts, and a body of comments and user-facing strings.

This is a mechanical but exhaustive rename. The point of the issue is completeness and atomicity: the cross-module string contracts (page value, event name, testids) are asserted by `packages/app/src/main.tsx` (the boot "home reached" gate) and ~10 `ui-smoke` specs, so the literals and every assertion must flip in the **same commit** or CI breaks mid-stack. Census: **74 non-generated source files** carry `springboard` (generated/committed artifacts, review-shots, and `.github/issue-evidence` excluded).

## Critical assessment (current state)

The rename was started at the copy layer ("launcher" in help/nav text) but never pushed down into code, leaving four distinct change-classes with different blast radii:

1. **File/module renames** — mechanical, but ripple through every importer.
2. **Exported symbol families** — `SPRINGBOARD_*` consts, `SpringboardLayout`, the `read/write/normalize/dedupe/compareSpringboard*` family, store fields + setters.
3. **Cross-boundary string literals** — page value `"springboard"`, window-event name, `data-testid` families, telemetry `source` literal, `localStorage` key. These cross runtime boundaries and are asserted by tests; changing one side without the other breaks the build/CI/persistence.
4. **User-facing strings** — nav label, "Open Springboard" buttons, help Q&A.

Two items are **not** mechanical and carry real risk:

- `SPRINGBOARD_STORAGE_KEY = "elizaos.views.springboard"` (`packages/ui/src/state/springboard-layout.ts:19`) — changing the persisted **string** silently discards every existing user's saved launcher layout (favorites, page order) with no migration.
- The page value `"springboard"` and the window-event name are cross-module contracts asserted by `packages/app/src/main.tsx:922` and the `ui-smoke` suite — they must change in lockstep with their assertions.

Confirmed there is **no** routable `/springboard` path, no `/springboard` slash command, and **no** `plugins/*` reference. The routable tab is `"views"`/`"apps"`; "springboard" survives only as a display label, a page sub-value, testids, a telemetry source, a `localStorage` key, and symbol/file names — so the migration is contained entirely within `packages/ui` + `packages/app` test fixtures (plus comment-only refs in `core`/`agent`).

## Critical assessment (current state)

**1. The "every control" spec is a crash sweep, not verification.** `all-views-interaction.spec.ts` enumerates controls but bounds at `MAX_CLICKS = 24` / `MAX_INPUTS = 8` (not "every"), fills every text input with `"test"` regardless of type, wraps each click/fill in `.catch(() => {})`, runs only at desktop 1440×1000, and asserts only `toEqual([])` on uncaught page errors. A button that silently does nothing, a save that 500s, or a form that rejects valid input all pass green.

**2. Existing per-view e2e is shallow and desktop-only, not absent — but the coverage registry treats one happy path as "covered."** `core-view-interaction-coverage.test.ts` registers owner specs per view. For **Character**, the owner is `settings-sections-interactions.spec.ts`'s "character editor deep round-trip" — it edits *one* field (bio), saves, and reads back; it does not exercise the rest of the 1680-line editor, the hub, or roster, and sets no mobile viewport. For **Wallet**, the owner is `apps-utility-interactions.spec.ts`'s "wallet inventory controls update visible deterministic state" — it asserts a single balance/hide flow at a fixed 1600×900 desktop viewport. These are real but minimal; the registry's pass/fail does not encode per-control breadth or any orientation matrix.

**3. Workflow node-graph editor: no Playwright e2e.** `WorkflowEditor.tsx` (1008 lines) has only a component-level `WorkflowEditor.test.tsx`; `automations.spec.ts` covers the *feed/triggers* API surface, not the editor's add-node / connect / param-edit / save flow. There is no `workflow`/`automations` entry in `core-view-interaction-coverage.test.ts`'s owner registry.

**4. Browser is the closest to covered** — `browser-workspace.spec.ts` drives tab CRUD via testids — but `BrowserWorkspaceView.tsx` is 2893 lines and the spec is desktop-only with no mobile or landscape pass; address-bar navigation, back/forward, and close-all are not asserted.

**5. No portrait/landscape matrix in CI.** The aesthetic audit's `VIEWPORTS` is `[desktop 1440×1000, mobile 390×844]` — both portrait. The only place defining `mobile-landscape` / `desktop-landscape` / `ipad-landscape` is `run-design-review.ts`, wired as a manual `design-review` npm script (`node --import tsx …`), NOT a spec in any `playwright.*.config.ts`. Landscape is never asserted in CI.

**6. Aesthetic audit has no minimalism metric.** `VerdictFinding` measures `blueColors` / `hoverViolations` / `borderRadiusViolations` / `readableChars` / `overlayPresent` only — there is no border/divider-density, text-density, or whitespace-ratio dimension, which is exactly the "Her"-minimal goal. Border/divide/rounded token counts in target views: WorkflowEditor 44, AutomationsFeed 43, CharacterEditor 33, VectorBrowserView 19, BrowserWorkspaceView 16, CharacterHubView 15, InventoryView 0 — none gated.

Root cause: the interaction harness was built for *breadth* (#8796, "no view silently omitted"), which optimizes for "didn't crash"; the per-view specs were each scoped to one round-trip; and the aesthetic gate (#8796) was scoped to brand color only. Nobody owns per-view *depth*, the mobile orientation matrix, or the minimalism axis. Risk: regressions in these four high-value views ship green; mobile/landscape breakage is invisible; the "Her" redesign has no objective done-condition.

- #9626 — build process bloat/duplication audit (sibling cleanup work order; open).116:T2e54,## Summary

elizaOS ships **three uncoordinated prompt-injection / social-engineering detectors**, and none of them actually gates the should-respond decision, escalates to an LLM adjudicator, or keys risk to the resolved sender role. The richest detector (`SecurityModule`, ~1400 lines, 38 injection patterns, full obfuscation primitives) is consumed only by a context **provider** — it injects advisory prompt text the model can ignore. The opt-in `securityEvaluator` is off by default. The only always-on core detector (`incoming-message-security.ts`) writes a `promptInjectionSuspected` flag that no core code reads — its sole consumer is `plugin-wallet`.

Net effect: a USER or GUEST can defeat all three with trivial obfuscation that the existing `SecurityModule` code could already catch, because that code path is never invoked at the gate. This is the dead-pipeline + defensive-code-that-obscures-failure pattern the repo `AGENTS.md` explicitly calls out, and it is a live security gap. We should add **one fast deterministic risk extractor in the `parallel_with_should_respond` hook**, key it to the role system, and escalate borderline USER/GUEST messages to a single `TEXT_LARGE` adjudication — only when `shouldRespond=true`.

## Critical assessment (current state)

**Three detectors, three seams, no decision authority.**

1. **`securityEvaluator`** — an `ALWAYS_BEFORE` action. Only checks invisible chars + ~10 chat-template tokens (`STRUCTURAL_INJECTION_PATTERNS`), and is **opt-in** (registered only with `enableEvaluators`). Its result does not drive the shouldRespond decision.
2. **`SecurityModule`** — the richest detection in the repo (38 `INJECTION_PATTERNS`; multilingual + base64 + leet + token-split; urgency/authority/intimidation/credential/phishing keyword banks; `calculateSocialEngineeringRisk`; and the exact obfuscation primitives this work needs: `normalizeForScan`, `reverseString`, `getKeywordPattern`, `containsObfuscatedKeyword`). It returns `action: "require_verification"` in three places — but `analyzeMessage` is consumed **only** by the `securityStatus` provider, so it produces advisory prompt text, not a gate. `require_verification` is a **dead value**: `ContextualPermissionSystem` only branches on `action === "block"`. The `analyzeSemantics` "semantic" check is a naive substring-count stub — the placeholder where a real LLM verify belongs. No `useModel` / `TEXT_LARGE` adjudication exists anywhere in the security code.
3. **`incoming-message-security.ts`** — the only injection detector wired into the live path (`incoming_before_compose`). Sets `message.content.metadata.promptInjectionSuspected` and wraps external content. That flag has **zero core consumers** — only `plugin-wallet` reads it. Write-only dead pipeline.

**Root cause:** three teams bolted detection onto three different seams with no shared risk score and no authority over whether/how to respond. The role signal a risk-keyed gate needs is **already computed** right before Stage 1 (`resolveStage1SenderRole` → OWNER/ADMIN/USER/GUEST), and the `parallel_with_should_respond` hook **already runs concurrently** with the shouldRespond model call — but no detector consumes the role, and none escalates a borderline message to a cheap verification.

**Risk:** USER/GUEST defeats all three with obfuscation the code could catch; a clean hit only yields advisory text the LLM may follow anyway. And there is **zero adversarial test coverage** of the gate.

## Scope & work order

High-confidence first.

- [ ] **Fast deterministic risk extractor in `parallel_with_should_respond`.** Run a pure-sync, no-I/O, no-LLM scorer in the hook at `message.ts:10090` (phase defined at `pipeline-hooks.ts:101`). **Reuse** the existing obfuscation primitives at `SecurityModule.ts:704` (`normalizeForScan` / `reverseString` / `getKeywordPattern` / `containsObfuscatedKeyword`) and the existing `INJECTION_PATTERNS` bank (`SecurityModule.ts:80`) — do NOT add a fourth pattern set.
