## Related

- #9853 — Cloud apps multi-tenant hardening & security (role/trust boundary at a different layer).
- #9874 — Planner confabulation/exhaustion (adjacent model-behavior hardening).117:T39b7,## Summary

elizaOS has the *vocabulary* of roles — OWNER / ADMIN / USER / GUEST — but no single, enforced security model. Roles are defined six different incompatible ways, enforced inconsistently across layers, and the HTTP boundary is effectively binary: a caller either passes `isAuthorized()` and reaches **every** endpoint (secrets, wallet, config), or gets a 401. There is no role tier at the boundary. The load-bearing assumption that "the deployed phone/desktop app is the OWNER" is implicit and emergent — it is never recorded as an explicit, auditable grant; it falls out of loopback HTTP trust plus the entityId the dashboard chat route stamps onto messages.

This matters now because secret-bearing surfaces are live and under-gated. The wallet plugin ships `public: true` POST signing routes (`personal-sign`, `sign-typed-data`, `sign-transaction`, `send-transaction`) that bypass the central auth gate, are protected only by a static shared bearer with no replay protection, and reflect the request `Origin` into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with `credentials: true`. Because no single file answers "can a non-owner reach the wallet?", hardening is unauditable. A misconfigured `ELIZA_API_BIND`, a forgotten `WALLET_BROWSER_SIGN_TOKEN`, or a DNS-rebind / CORS gap turns "local owner only" into "remote anyone."

## Critical assessment (current state)

**1. Role-model fragmentation (root cause).** There is no canonical `Role` type. Six definitions coexist with disagreeing membership:
- `RoleName = OWNER|ADMIN|USER|GUEST` with `ROLE_RANK` GUEST<USER<ADMIN<OWNER (no NONE/MEMBER).
- A competing `Role = OWNER|ADMIN|MEMBER|GUEST|NONE` (has MEMBER/NONE, lacks USER).
- A **third** `ROLE_RANK` table (NONE|GUEST|USER|MEMBER|ADMIN|OWNER) that ranks `USER == MEMBER == 2` and maps `USER -> MEMBER`. This is the table the action gate actually uses.
- `ConnectorAccountRole = OWNER|AGENT|TEAM` (orthogonal vocabulary).
- `WaifuChatRole = admin|user|guest` (lowercase, embed-only).
- A sixth lowercase spelling `RoleGate = "user"|"admin"|"owner"` in plugin provider role overrides.

`RoleGateRole = Role | "USER" | (string & {})` is a union hack papering over the USER/MEMBER split (and the trailing `(string & {})` makes it accept any string). **Two rank tables that disagree on membership is a silent authz hazard** — a gate decision depends on which enum the call path happened to import.

**2. The HTTP boundary is binary, not role-aware.** `isAuthorized()` returns one boolean: trusted-loopback OR shared service token OR matching `ELIZA_API_TOKEN` → full access, else 401. **Zero of 73 app-core API source files (`packages/app-core/src/api`) reference any role helper** (`roleRank`/`satisfiesRoleGate`/`ROLE_RANK`/`minRole`/`RoleGate`/`buildAccessContext`). Once a caller passes the gate, every endpoint is reachable. Role distinction only reappears later, at the agent message/world layer — too late to protect the HTTP surface.

**3. "Deployed app = OWNER" is implicit.** There is no explicit owner binding at auth/first-run. The dashboard chat stamps the message `entityId` to a resolved owner id (`resolveClientChatAdminEntityId`: canonical `ELIZA_ADMIN_ENTITY_ID`, else a deterministic `<agentName>-admin-entity` UUID) and sets world ownership to that id. OWNER is therefore *emergent* from loopback trust + the entityId the chat route stamps, never an explicit auditable grant. Anyone who passes `isAuthorized` and drives the dashboard chat route inherits the owner entityId and every OWNER-gated action (the wallet provider's `roleGate.minRole` is `OWNER`). With no world (DMs), role resolution defaults to `USER`.

**4. Access-control built but not wired.** `buildAccessContext` + `canReadScope` implement role/scope-aware reads but there is exactly **one** real (non-test, non-`.d.ts`, non-build-artifact) call site, and `accessContext` is threaded into essentially none of the ~166 `getMemories` calls. The role-based memory read filter is effectively unenforced — the same multi-tenant hole #9853 targets, present in core too.

**5. Guest/random paths.** The only real GUEST tier is the waifu.fun embed JWT (issuer/audience/wallet checks, scoped to chat-only routes). The main dashboard has **no** tier between full-OWNER and 401, and there is **no canonical role-gating primitive** in the UI: no `RoleGate` component and no `useRole` hook exist anywhere in `packages/ui/src`. Role gating in the UI is ad-hoc, per-component `isOwner` booleans pulled from disparate sources.

**6. Under-authenticated surfaces.** `public: true` appears **122 times across 45 files** (each bypasses `isAuthorized` via `route.public !== true`). The wallet sign routes are not truly open (internal `readSignToken` requires `WALLET_BROWSER_SIGN_TOKEN >= 16` chars), but they (a) bypass the central gate, (b) use a static shared bearer with no nonce/replay protection, and (c) reflect `Origin` into CORS with credentials. The compat sensitive-route gate trusts **any** same-machine request when no token is configured — same-machine == sensitive access by default.

## Related

- #9853 — Cloud apps: multi-tenant hardening & completion before GA (the `buildAccessContext` / role-scoped read gap is the same hole, present in core).
- #9626 — Build process: bloat/duplication/complexity audit (role-enum fragmentation is the same duplication smell at the type layer).118:T2975,## Summary

elizaOS ships a complete web dashboard (`packages/app`, a single Vite SPA) that already deploys to Cloudflare Pages (`app.elizacloud.ai`) with a same-origin `/api` + `/steward` proxy and Steward JWT auth, plus connector plugins for Discord, Telegram, WeChat, LINE, Slack, Feishu and WhatsApp. Every one of those chat platforms supports embedding an HTML app in-context — Discord Activities (Embedded App SDK), Telegram Mini Apps (`web_app` buttons), WeChat mini-programs, LINE LIFF, Slack App Home. Yet **none of the connectors expose any embedded-app launch surface today**, so the exact UI a user gets on `app.elizacloud.ai` cannot be opened from inside a Discord server or a Telegram chat, even though all the hosting, build, deploy, auth, and role primitives already exist and are wired into the connectors.

This is a researched work-order to add embedded-app distribution targets — **Discord and Telegram first** — reusing the existing single web bundle and auto-deploy pipeline, gated to OWNER/ADMIN with ADMIN-mode injection. The security-critical seam is one shared embed-auth handshake that verifies each platform's signed launch payload server-side before mapping to an Eliza entity and resolving its role; it must **fail closed**.

## Critical assessment (current state)

A grep across the seven chat-connector plugins (`plugin-discord`, `plugin-telegram`, `plugin-wechat`, `plugin-line`, `plugin-slack`, `plugin-feishu`, `plugin-whatsapp`) for `web_app|WebApp|Activities|LIFF|miniProgram|EmbeddedAppSDK|initData|Telegram.WebApp|launchActivity` returns **zero hits** — the only embed-adjacent match is Discord's unrelated `UseEmbeddedActivities` invite-permission bit (`permissions.ts:34`). No embedded-app integration exists in any connector. (Note: the string `web_app` does appear in `plugin-personal-assistant` LifeOps activity-profile code, which is a device-class label, not chat-platform embedding — unrelated.)

The opportunity is low-risk because every dependency is already shipped:

- **Hosting/build is a single artifact.** `packages/app` `build:web` produces one bundle deployed by `.github/workflows/cloud-cf-deploy.yml` (`deploy-app` job). An embedded target reuses the **same** artifact and the **same** auto-deploy pipeline — no new build, no forked bundle.
- **Auth is already first-party.** The SPA talks to the Cloud API over same-origin `/api` and `/steward` via `packages/app/functions/_proxy.ts`, keeping the Steward JWT first-party. But first-party Steward cookies do **not** cross into a 3rd-party-origin iframe, so an embedded surface needs a token-based auth path.
- **Role-gating already exists and is already used by a connector.** `hasRoleAccess(runtime, message, role)` (`packages/core/src/roles.ts:897`) is exactly the primitive an embed gate needs, and Telegram already calls it for OWNER/ADMIN in `command-registration.ts` to gate command access, with a fail-closed default when there is no identity.
- **Launch surfaces already exist per connector.** Discord has full slash-command registration (`plugins/plugin-discord/slash-commands.ts:448` / `service.ts:596`); Telegram already emits `InlineKeyboardButton` rows (`messageManager.ts:944`). They just never emit a `web_app`/Activity launch button.

The risk if left undone: the web app is the product's primary surface but is invisible from inside the platforms where users already are. The risk if done carelessly: an embedded webview that trusts the platform's *claimed* user id is an auth bypass — Telegram `initData` and Discord activity OAuth2 tokens MUST be HMAC/OAuth-verified server-side before mapping to an entity, and the role gate must fail closed (matching the fail-closed default in `command-registration.ts:184`).

## Evidence in code

- `.github/workflows/cloud-cf-deploy.yml:386` — `deploy-app` job builds (`:413`) + `wrangler pages deploy` (`:495`); the auto-deploy pipeline an embed route inherits for free.
- `packages/app/functions/_proxy.ts:40` — `proxyToApiWorker`, the same-origin `/api`/`/steward` proxy to `api.elizacloud.ai`; keeps Steward JWT first-party (won't survive a cross-origin iframe).
- `packages/app/functions/_middleware.ts:29` — `PROXY_PREFIXES` only proxies `/api/` + `/steward/` and falls everything else through to the SPA; there is **no** `frame-ancestors`/CSP frame handling today — this is where the per-platform iframe-embed policy must be added.
- `packages/core/src/roles.ts:897` — `hasRoleAccess(runtime, message, requiredRole)`, the single role primitive the embed gate calls.

- #9853 — Cloud apps multi-tenant hardening & security (the embed-auth handshake is the security-critical seam; the role gate and fail-closed contract must align with that work order).119:T382d,## Summary

elizaOS already ships a genuinely strong multimodal view stack: `@elizaos/ui/spatial` lets a plugin author one React tree from a primitive layout IR (`packages/ui/src/spatial/ir.ts`) that renders to GUI, XR, and TUI, and the agent terminal (`packages/agent/src/tui/agent-terminal-tui.ts`) mounts those views inline with an always-on chat composer. 27 plugins ship `register-terminal-view.tsx`, parity/framing tests glob all of them, and `packages/tui` has 479 passing unit tests across 25 files with no circular deps. The abstraction is real and the architecture is sound.

This issue is **not** "build the multimodal abstraction" — it largely exists. It is a work-order for three concrete, load-bearing gaps that keep TUI from being a first-class, tested run mode and make the headline "SSH into the agent terminal" use case a fiction: (1) the SSH path is unimplemented yet the code names it as if it exists; (2) the TUI is unauthenticated and loopback-only by construction, so it cannot work over a real tunnel; (3) the TUI's tests run on no PR CI lane, there is no real-PTY e2e, and XR has zero automated coverage on PRs.

## Critical assessment (current state)

1. **The "SSH-into-agent-terminal" use case is unimplemented and the code names it as if it exists.** `agent-terminal-tui.ts:509` hardcodes the conversation title `"SSH terminal"` and `agent-terminal-tui.test.ts:190,202` send/assert chat text `"hello over ssh"` — but there is no SSH server in the elizaOS agent anywhere. The elizaOS Linux image config ships no sshd (`packages/os/linux/elizaos/` has zero `openssh`/`sshd` references; the only matches in the tree are vendored upstream Tails under `packages/os/linux/tails/`, unrelated to the agent). The only run mode is `eliza-autonomous tui` / `tui-smoke` (`packages/agent/src/cli/index.ts:18-19`) pointed at an already-running backend over loopback HTTP. To "SSH in," a user would have to stand up an sshd themselves, ssh in, then know to run the undocumented `tui` subcommand locally. None of that is wired or documented. The naming actively misleads.

2. **The TUI client sends zero auth and depends on a loopback trust gate that breaks under tunneling.** The `readJson` helper in `agent-terminal-tui.ts:68-86` sets only `Content-Type` — no `Authorization`/`Bearer`/token anywhere in the file (grep-confirmed). It works only because it hits `127.0.0.1`, which the backend treats as trusted via `isTrustedLocalRequest`. That gate is *disabled* when `X-Forwarded-For` is present (`packages/agent/src/api/server-helpers-auth-trust.test.ts:72-77`) — exactly what a real SSH-tunnel/reverse-proxy "remote terminal" adds. So the one path that would make "talk to your agent over the network" work is the path the security model forbids, and the TUI has no token to fall back on. Default bind host is `127.0.0.1` (`packages/shared/src/runtime-env.ts:3`), reinforcing loopback-only.

3. **The TUI library's unit tests run on no PR CI lane.** `packages/tui` is in neither the `test:server` (`package.json:154`) nor `test:client` (`package.json:152`) package filters, so its 479 tests run only on a bare full `bun run test`, never on the per-area jobs that gate PRs in `.github/workflows/test.yml`. The PR jobs (`server-tests`, `client-tests`, `plugin-tests`) only *build* `packages/tui` as a dependency (`test.yml:181,247`) — they never run its vitest suite. `tui-smoke` (the readiness-marker mode, `cli/index.ts:19`) is referenced only in `build-linux-iso.yml`'s boot-serial smoke grep (`build-linux-iso.yml:210`), which runs on `workflow_dispatch`/nightly cron — never on `pull_request`. `verify-tui-slash.ts` is a hand-run script, not a test. The XR sim Playwright spec is wired into no workflow. Every verification surface that isn't a jsdom/fake-terminal unit test is manual-only.

4. **There is no real-PTY end-to-end test.** Every TUI test injects a fake `Terminal` (`agent-terminal-tui.test.ts`, `verify-tui-slash.ts`'s `DriverTerminal`). Nothing spawns a real pseudo-terminal, runs the packaged CLI, types bytes, and asserts on the rendered frame. Kitty-protocol negotiation, real stdin buffering (`packages/tui/src/stdin-buffer.ts`), resize, and bracketed paste — the things that only exist against a real TTY — are never exercised end-to-end. The fake-terminal tests cannot catch a regression in the part of the stack that only exists against a real terminal.

5. **The "what modality am I" contract is split asymmetrically.** TUI mounting is centralized: the host calls into the process-global terminal-view registry (`packages/tui/src/view-registry.ts`, keyed by `Symbol.for`). But GUI/XR modality is decided per-leaf via `detectDomModality()` reading `window.__elizaXRContext` (`packages/ui/src/spatial/dom.tsx:30-31`). `SpatialSurface` is used in 88 plugin view files but **0 times in `packages/app`** (the real GUI shell, which mounts via `DynamicViewLoader`). There is no single shell-level place that owns modality across all three surfaces; the contract is split between the host (TUI) and the leaf components (GUI/XR).

**The risk:** the multimodal framework is good enough to be sold as "first-class," but the run mode it most needs (remote/SSH agent terminal) is vaporware, the security model can't support it, and the CI safety net that would let people refactor it confidently doesn't cover it on PRs.

- #9626 Build process bloat/duplication/complexity audit + cross-platform11a:T2fdc,## Summary

The Settings and Views surface in `@elizaos/ui` has grown into a large, inconsistent area, and the agent's view-switching path is strictly weaker than the client's. The client slash system can already deep-link a *subview* (`/settings voice` jumps straight to the Voice section), but the agent's `VIEWS` action cannot — it can open Settings but not "Settings -> Voice", and the views provider never tells the planner which subviews exist (`subview` appears zero times in `plugins/plugin-app-control/src`).

Settings is ~24k LOC across 72 `.tsx` files in one directory, with the navigation gate (`developerOnly`) used on exactly one section even though a fully-built, shared advanced-disclosure primitive (`AdvancedToggle` + `useAdvancedSettingsEnabled()`) already exists and is wired into only ~6 sections. There is **zero** orientation handling anywhere in `settings/` or `views/`, so layout on landscape phone / portrait tablet ships unverified. A "fuzz every setting" pass is currently impossible to assert because 35 of 45 non-test section/view components have no test at all.

This is a work-order to (1) close the slash<->agent subview parity gap, (2) apply the existing advanced-mode primitive consistently with sane defaults, (3) make the surface orientation-aware on mobile + desktop, (4) add fuzz/edge-case e2e of every setting with screenshots+recordings, and (5) co-locate the duplicated provider/model controls.

## Critical assessment (current state)

**1. Subview parity gap (load-bearing).** The client already has first-class subview deep-linking; the agent does not. `SlashExecution` carries `{ kind: "navigate-settings"; section? }` and `{ kind: "navigate-view"; viewId; viewPath }`; `resolveSlashExecution` parses the optional `section` sub-argument; `runSlashExecution` dispatches `deps.navigateSettings(exec.section)`. `SettingsView` consumes this via an `initialSection` prop + `#hash` routing — so sections **are** addressable subviews, just not by the agent. The `VIEWS` action exposes 29 parameters but no `subview`/`section`; `navigateToView` POSTs only `{ path, viewType }`; the views-list provider surfaces only `{id,label,type,path,available}`; and `current_view` reports the active view with no notion of the open subview. Net: the agent can open the settings/wallet view but cannot deep-link a tab/section inside it, and the planner prompt never lists the subviews that already exist as hash sections. This is a parity smell — a client capability with no equivalent agent trigger.

**2. An advanced-mode primitive exists but is barely used; no defaults discipline.** 16 sections registered in `SECTION_VISUALS`, 72 `.tsx` files, ~24,148 LOC in `settings/`. A shared `AdvancedToggle` (persisted to `localStorage`, default OFF, with a global subscriber `useAdvancedSettingsEnabled()`) already exists with its own tests + stories, but it is only consumed by ~6 sections (Apps, Capabilities, Appearance, VoiceConfigView, Voice, Security). The section-routing gate `developerOnly: true` is set on exactly one section (`remote-plugins`). So the problem is not "there is no advanced mode" — it is that the existing one is applied inconsistently and most knobs are presented flat, the opposite of the Apple-minimal, defaults-first goal. Individual files are enormous (VoiceConfigView 1436 LOC, VaultInventoryPanel 1274, PolicyControlsView 1121, SecuritySettingsSection 1109, DesktopWorkspaceSection 1089). Provider/model selection is split across several parallel surfaces.

**3. No portrait/landscape responsiveness.** Grep for `orientation|portrait|landscape` across both dirs returns nothing. The only responsive lever in `SettingsView` is a single `useMediaQuery("(min-width: 1024px)")` width breakpoint — desktop two-pane vs mobile hub on width alone, ignoring landscape phone / portrait tablet. The `useMediaQuery` hook already accepts any media-query string, so an orientation query is a one-line addition. This is exactly the layout-break class the `audit:app` loop is meant to catch, but it has no orientation coverage today.

**Risk:** the agent's view UX is silently degraded vs the client; Settings is cognitively overwhelming and largely untestable; orientation breakage ships unverified. 35 of 45 non-test components have no unit test, so "fuzz every setting" cannot be asserted.

## Acceptance criteria

- The agent can execute `VIEWS` with a `subview`/`section` and land on the exact section the user reaches by typing the equivalent slash command; an e2e asserts the deep-link reaches the correct section.
- The views-list provider and `current_view` emit the addressable subviews; a planner trajectory shows the model selecting a valid subview value it discovered from the prompt.
- A fresh user sees a minimal defaults-first Settings; rare/deep controls live behind the existing `AdvancedToggle` in every section, with no second advanced-mode mechanism introduced.
- Settings and Views render correctly in all four of {mobile, desktop} x {portrait, landscape}, verified in the `audit:app` loop with screenshots; no page is `needs-work`/`broken`.
- Every settings input is exercised by a fuzz/edge-case e2e (empty/max/invalid/boundary) with before/after screenshots + a recording artifact.
- The provider/model surfaces are reduced to one module; no duplicated selection controls remain.
- `bun run --cwd packages/ui knip` shows no new dead exports from the consolidation; `bun run verify` is green.

- #9880 (voice wake word — adjacent to VoiceConfigView surface)11b:T2f9e,## Summary

`PR_EVIDENCE.md` is the repo-wide Definition of Done: a reviewer must confirm a change works **without reading code**, from attached screenshots/video/logs (`PR_EVIDENCE.md:7-10`). But the only *orchestrated* capture tooling we ship is **web Playwright, chromium-only** (`test:e2e:record`). Every other surface elizaOS actually ships on — Electrobun desktop, the iOS simulator, the Android emulator, and Linux/Windows desktop — has either no capture story, a one-off ad-hoc script nobody is required to run, or screenshot-only with no recording. The result: "video walkthrough" and "before/after screenshots" are checklist rows with no per-platform tooling behind them, so they get marked N/A or filled with a hand-recorded clip of unknown provenance.

This issue does two things: (a) edit `PR_EVIDENCE.md`, root `CLAUDE.md`, and root `AGENTS.md` to make screen-capture + screen-recording + structured logs **non-negotiable, with a per-platform evidence matrix**, and (b) lay down a work-order to build and verify the missing capture/record tooling on each target platform so the matrix is actually satisfiable with a single command per platform.

## Critical assessment (current state)

The evidence policy describes capabilities the tooling does not uniformly provide.

- **The doc claims "all already in the repo" but the orchestrator is web-only.** The evidence table rows "Full-page screenshots" and "Video walkthrough" (`PR_EVIDENCE.md:60-61`) both point at `audit:cloud` / `test:e2e:record`. That script (`package.json:143` → `scripts/e2e-recordings/run-all.mjs`) iterates the suites registered in `scripts/e2e-recordings/suites.mjs:6-80`, every one of which is a **Playwright web e2e** package. The Playwright config it drives, `packages/app/playwright.ui-smoke.config.ts:76-129`, defines only `chromium`, `chromium-voice-mic`, `mobile-chromium` (chromium emulating a phone viewport), and `audit-app` projects — **no webkit, no firefox, no native shells**. So "video walkthrough" = one browser engine, no native app.
- **No iOS/Android simulator capture is in the evidence pipeline.** The capability exists but is scattered and unorchestrated: `packages/app/scripts/ios-e2e.mjs` boots a simulator via `xcrun simctl` (`ios-e2e.mjs:38-77`) yet produces **no** `simctl io … screenshot`/`recordVideo` artifact (grep confirms zero capture calls in that file); `packages/app/test/android/onboarding-to-home.android.spec.ts:24-130` does a real `adb shell screenrecord` + page screenshot and attaches mp4/png — but it is a single hand-written spec, not referenced by `PR_EVIDENCE.md`, not in `suites.mjs`, and not invoked by `test:e2e:record`. There is **no** orchestrated `simctl io booted recordVideo` anywhere in the tree.
- **The desktop screenshot endpoint is screenshot-only and Electrobun-only.** `/api/dev/cursor-screenshot` (`packages/app-core/src/api/dev-stack.ts:79-90`, served by `packages/app-core/src/api/dev-compat-routes.ts:82-117`) returns a single PNG proxied from the Electrobun shell over loopback. It is a dev convenience for agents, not a recording, and only exists when desktop dev is running with the screenshot server enabled.
- **No Linux/Windows capture path at all.** Nothing in `scripts/` or `packages/*/scripts` provides headed desktop capture (ffmpeg/gdigrab/x11grab/scrcpy-style) for Linux or Windows runners.
- **No per-platform matrix in the policy.** `PR_EVIDENCE.md` never says ios, android, simulator, emulator, electrobun, linux, or windows; the only platform phrase is "desktop + mobile" at `PR_EVIDENCE.md:82`, inside the cloud-frontend `audit:cloud` note (viewport sizes, not OS targets). So an author shipping an iOS-only fix has no defined, runnable way to produce the required video, and reviewers have no standard to demand.

Root cause: the policy was written around the mature web audit tooling (`audit:cloud`, `audit:app`, `test:e2e:record`) and never extended as the product grew a native desktop shell plus two mobile targets. The risk is exactly the regression class `PR_EVIDENCE.md:118-126` says this whole policy exists to catch — behavioral/visual breaks on native surfaces that pass CI and are never seen by a human because no one was required (or able) to record them.

- #9880 — voice name-aware wake word (audio-capture evidence is the voice analog of this screen-capture work).11c:T3d57,## Summary

The elizaOS monorepo has a large test corpus — 150 plugins (10 with zero tests), 106 app `ui-smoke` Playwright specs, 331 Storybook stories, 101 `*.real.test.ts` live files, 525 `*.test.ts`/`*.spec.ts` files inside `packages/feed` alone. The problem is not quantity. It is that a meaningful fraction of those tests **never run in any CI lane**, the on-device/simulator/lifecycle surface is **manual-dispatch only**, the coverage gate is **permanently advisory**, and ~91% of Storybook stories are render-only with no interaction assertion.

The consequence: a green PR check overstates what is actually guarded. It can simultaneously mean `packages/feed` (525 test files) ran nowhere, no real touch-device run happened, no iOS device run happened, no sleep-wake/backgrounding spec exists on any platform, 20 of the 106 `ui-smoke` specs were skipped on the PR path, component interactions are unverified, and there is zero enforced coverage floor. This is the umbrella testing issue: it tracks the per-package coverage matrix and the work order to close gaps, un-skip, and make tests real. Voice/chat/wallet/tutorial e2e get their own sub-issues and should link here. The repo's own standard — "E2E must catch real bugs, not mock-mount smoke" — is the bar this fails to meet in several wired lanes.

## Critical assessment (current state)

**The single largest hole: `packages/feed` runs 525 test files in zero CI lanes.** feed is a nested monorepo with 525 `*.test.ts`/`*.spec.ts` files and 227 `.skip(` calls (the bulk of the entire repo's skip count). It is deliberately excluded from root `bun run test` — `run-all-tests.mjs` honors the `!packages/feed` workspace negation (`packages/scripts/run-all-tests.mjs:356-366`) on the stated assumption that "it has its own install/CI." But no workflow runs it: the only two feed workflows are `feed-apply-migrations.yml` (runs migrations) and `feed-env-audit.yml` (audits env). feed has a full `test:ci` script (`packages/feed/package.json:42`) that nothing invokes. A 525-file / 227-skip suite gates no PR and runs nowhere — pure dead weight giving false green.

**20 of 106 `ui-smoke` specs never run on a PR.** `scenario-pr.yml` is well-wired and runs an explicitly-named subset of **86 distinct specs** on every PR to develop/main — but it names them one by one rather than running the directory, so **20 specs are silently off the PR path**, including `springboard-interaction.spec.ts`, `multi-window-sync.spec.ts`, `multi-client-desync.spec.ts`, `wallet-keys.spec.ts`, `view-switching-core-matrix.spec.ts`, `provider-config.spec.ts`, and `vault-routing.spec.ts`. These are not cron-only by design; they fell out of the hand-maintained list. A directory-driven gate with an allow/deny manifest would prevent silent drop-off.

**On-device / simulator / sleep-wake / gesture coverage never gates a PR.** The native-device and live-e2e lanes are all `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` only — never `pull_request`: `android-device-e2e.yml` (workflow_dispatch only, confirmed at line 16-17), `app-live-e2e.yml` (cron + dispatch), `app-real-e2e.yml` (explicitly "never on pull_request", line 18), `hetzner-sleep-wake-smoke.yml` (push to the one-off branch `claude/hetzner-provision-smoke` + dispatch). There are 4 Android device specs but **zero iOS device specs** — iOS coverage is a single script (`packages/app/scripts/ios-onboarding-smoke.mjs`). Gesture/swipe coverage exists only as desktop-Chromium pointer simulation (`packages/app/test/ui-smoke/chat-clear-swipe.spec.ts:240` uses `page.mouse.move/down/up`), never a real touch device. Sleep-wake, app backgrounding/foregrounding, pinch, and long-press are uncovered on every platform.

**Storybook: 331 stories, 31 with interaction tests.** The story gate (`packages/ui/test/story-gate/run-story-gate.mjs`, wired via `ui-story-gate.yml`) is render-smoke only: it asserts a story renders without throwing/blank/new-console-error. Only 31 of 331 `*.stories.tsx` export a `play`. The gate proves "it mounts," not "it works" — clicks, form fills, and state transitions inside components are unverified at the story level for the other ~300 stories.

**Coverage gate is permanently advisory; no thresholds anywhere.** `coverage-gate.yml:88` hard-codes `COVERAGE_GATE_ENFORCE: "0"` with a "flip to 1 once baseline established" comment, and the test step runs with `|| true` (`coverage-gate.yml:79`), so the gate cannot fail a PR. There is no `coverage.thresholds`/`statements`/`lines` config in any vitest/vite config repo-wide (0 found). 22 workflows use `continue-on-error: true`, including `mobile-build-smoke.yml:193,218` ("Flip back to a hard fail when the generator pipeline lands") — those tests run but cannot fail a build.

**Skip hygiene is fine — except feed.** Excluding feed, the source has 61 `.skip` calls, almost all env-gated live-suite fallbacks. Zero `.only` leaks in real test files (every `.only` match repo-wide lives under build/dist/cache artifacts — `packages/app/electrobun/build/**`, `packages/ui/storybook-static/`, the riscv64 WebKit src-cache — 0 in source specs). Zero `.todo`. The one genuinely-disabled suite is `packages/cloud/api/test/e2e/group-g2-mcp-registry.test.ts:117` (`describe.skip` — a PGlite-over-TCP broken-pipe harness limitation, documented at lines 103-117), leaving MCP-registry CRUD auth gates and revenue-split paths untested in CI.

**Risk.** Size creates false confidence. Regressions in gestures, mobile lifecycle, component interactions, the 20 unwired ui-smoke specs, and feed land undetected until a daily cron or manual dispatch surfaces them — or until a user does.

- #8434 cloud 10-user launch tracker — gated-vs-ungated lane visibility matters for launch.11d:T2792,## Summary

The root `package.json` carries **208 npm scripts**, and the workspace totals **2,300+ scripts across 220+ `package.json` files** (plus 130 loose `.mjs` files under `packages/scripts/` and 32 under top-level `scripts/`). The root block has stopped being a curated set of entrypoints and become a dumping ground: it mixes the day-to-day commands (`dev`, `build`, `verify`, `test`) with one-off audit scripts that no gate ever runs, package-specific scripts that belong inside their owning packages, and a manual-only report pipeline that fans out into ~52 subprocess files.

This matters now because the accumulation actively hides failures. Several plugins ship `lint`/`typecheck` scripts that are literally `echo "...skipped"` — so turbo reports green while those packages are never linted or typechecked. That is the exact "silent fallback that masks real failures" the repo's own AGENTS.md forbids. The goal of this issue is a concrete inventory + work-order: delete dead scripts, relocate package-specific ones, replace the fake-success no-ops with real checks, and add a guard so the inventory cannot re-rot.

## Critical assessment (current state)

Four grounded smells, ranked by confidence:

1. **Ungated "audit" scripts that gate nothing (high).** Seven root `audit:*`/`lint:*` scripts exist only in root `package.json` and are invoked by nothing — not the 138 workflows in `.github/workflows`, not `verify`/`check`/`lint`/`test`, not another root script, not docs. An audit nobody runs is dead code with a maintenance cost: its underlying logic (e.g. the 53 KB `audit-duplicate-components.mjs`) is never exercised and could be silently broken.

2. **Package-specific scripts hoisted to root (high).** **38** root scripts are bare `bun run --cwd <pkg> <task>` passthroughs, of which **11** are `smartglasses:*` aliases all forwarding into a single example package (`packages/examples/smartglasses`). On top of those, the `voice:*` (7) and `eliza1:*` (3) root clusters reach **directly into a package's internal `scripts/` directory** (e.g. `node packages/app-core/scripts/voice-latency-report.mjs`) — arguably worse than a passthrough, since the root now depends on a package's private file layout. None of these are referenced by CI. The repo root is not the place for one example's hardware-doctor command.

3. **Fake-success no-op scripts (high; violates the fail-loudly rule).** **14** package `lint`/`typecheck` scripts across **10 packages** are `echo "...skipped"` no-ops. They make turbo's quality gate report success for packages that are in fact never checked. This is a correctness bug in CI, not a style nit. Affected: plugin-ainex, plugin-aosp-local-inference, plugin-eliza-classic, plugin-remote-desktop, plugin-signal, plugin-tee, plugin-todos, plugin-twitch, plugin-vision, plugin-x.

4. **Script-command drift (medium).** The same logical task name has many divergent bodies across packages: `lint` has ~21 distinct bodies, `typecheck` ~18, `clean` ~16, `test` ~30, `build` ~62. Much per-package repetition is inherent Turbo fan-out and is fine; the *variant divergence* (`biome check --write --unsafe .` vs `biome check src` vs `biome check src/` vs `echo skipped`) is drift that causes packages to lint different file sets.

**Not a defect (documented to prevent a wrong cleanup):** the `build-benchmark-*` / `build-scenario-*` / `build-corpus-*` report-generator `.mjs` files in `packages/scripts/` (43 such files on disk) look dead (0 refs in CI/pkg.json) but **52 of them are spawned as subprocesses** by `build-benchmark-analysis-reports.mjs` (run via `bench:analysis:build`) through a `script: "<path>"` array passed to `spawnSync`. Do not delete them. The real issue there is that `bench:analysis:build` itself is in no workflow, and the pipeline is one command fanning out to 52 string-path subprocess files — an architecture smell, not deletable dead code.

- #9626 — Build process bloat/duplication/complexity audit + cross-platform (this is the script-layer slice of the same accumulation problem).11e:T2eb4,## Summary

The runtime stack already invented the right decoupling seams — a core `AppRoutePluginRegistry`, a build-time `@elizaos/registry` generator that derives connector/channel maps from registry-entry data, a build-time `appRegister` package.json scan in `packages/app`, and a structural native bridge in `packages/ui`. Those seams are sound and mostly adopted. But a handful of concrete hardcoded `@elizaos/plugin-*` couplings remain, and each violates "dependencies point inward only": the innermost layer (`@elizaos/core`) ships a dead, divergent copy of the env→plugin auto-enable rule; the Application layer (`app-core`) names three specific Infrastructure plugins to paper over a boot race; and `app-core`'s TTS wiring dynamic-imports two named vendor plugins instead of resolving a capability.

This is a structural refactor with near-zero behavioral risk. The work is to **extend the seams that already exist** and delete the couplings that bypass them — not invent a new mechanism. `madge --circular` (re-run for this issue) reports **0 cycles** in `packages/core/src` and `packages/agent/src`, so there is no circular-dependency work here; the coupling is one-directional hardcoding.

## Critical assessment (current state)

**1. `@elizaos/core` ships a dead, divergent copy of the env→plugin map.** `buildCharacterPlugins()` (`packages/core/src/character.ts:232`) is an env-var→plugin-name resolver (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`→`plugin-anthropic`, `DISCORD_API_TOKEN`→`plugin-discord`, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`→`plugin-telegram`, `X_*`→`plugin-x`, fallback→`plugin-ollama`). This is the worst violation: a connector/provider-plugin business rule hardcoded in the **innermost** layer. It is also **dead** — the only non-build-artifact reference in the entire repo is its own definition. It is not exported from any core barrel (`index.node.ts` / `index.browser.ts` / `index.edge.ts`), and the only other hit is a gitignored compiled declaration. It is a divergent copy of `PROVIDER_PLUGIN_MAP` (`packages/agent/src/runtime/plugin-collector.ts:168`) plus a few inline channel keys — and it is already out of sync: core keys only `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`, while the live agent map also keys `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, and the agent map covers ~15 providers core never mentions.

**2. `app-core` re-couples to three named plugins to work around a side-effect boot race.** The `AppRoutePluginRegistry` seam is the correct inward-pointing mechanism and is consumed correctly via `listAppRoutePluginLoaders()`. But `getAppRoutePluginLoaders()` (`packages/app-core/src/runtime/eliza.ts:535-583`) then hardcodes fallback loaders for exactly `@elizaos/plugin-workflow/plugin-routes` (`:547`), `@elizaos/plugin-wallet/routes/plugin` (`:561`), and `@elizaos/plugin-agent-orchestrator/setup-routes` (`:575`) — because each plugin registers its route loader only as a module-init **side effect** that races the post-ready boot snapshot (the in-code comments say so explicitly). The Application layer should not name three Infrastructure plugins; the fix belongs in the three plugins (register eagerly), not in the consumer.

**3. `app-core` TTS wiring names single-vendor plugins instead of resolving a capability.** `ensure-text-to-speech-handler.ts:86` dynamic-imports `@elizaos/plugin-edge-tts` as the sole TTS handler fallback, and `tts-cache-wiring.ts:64` imports `@elizaos/plugin-local-inference/services` directly for the cache. Runtime wiring naming specific Infrastructure plugins rather than resolving a `TEXT_TO_SPEECH` capability.

**What is already correct (extend, do not reinvent):**
- `packages/app/src/plugin-registrations.ts` build-time-scans each plugin's `package.json` `elizaos.appRegister` marker (`SIDE_EFFECT_APP_MODULE_LOADERS`) — zero hardcoded list.
- `packages/ui/src/bridge/native-plugins.ts` models Capacitor plugins purely structurally — zero `@elizaos/plugin-*` imports.
- `CHANNEL_PLUGIN_MAP` (`plugin-collector.ts:164`) is **already** registry-derived: it is `channelPluginMap` loaded from `@elizaos/registry/first-party/channel-plugin-map.json`, generated from each connector entry's `channels` (`packages/registry/src/first-party/generate.ts:79`). The in-code comment already says "edit the owning connector's registry-entry.json `channels` and regenerate — not this list." This is the seam to extend, not move.
- `OPTIONAL_PLUGIN_MAP` (`plugin-collector.ts:240`) is a **legacy short-id→package alias map** (`evm`/`solana`/`wallet`→`plugin-wallet`, `coding-agent`→`plugin-coding-tools`) for backward-compat config resolution — a separate concern from the env→provider rule. Do not conflate or move it.
- `packages/agent/src/runtime/core-plugins.ts` list constants are legitimate — agent is the composition root for the bundled set. `DEFERRED_CORE_PLUGINS` already derives from `CORE_PLUGINS` via `.filter` (`:253`).

- #9626 — Build process bloat/duplication/complexity audit (shares the duplication root cause).
11f:T298b,## Summary

This is the umbrella tech-debt issue for code-smell / patch-over patterns across the runtime. The headline finding, after grounding the smell counts in real code, is the opposite of the usual story: lint-level slop is near-zero (`as any` in production `packages/{core,agent,app-core}/src` = **0** — every hit is in `.test.ts` / `.stories.tsx`; `@ts-ignore` = 0; `@ts-expect-error` = 0; no `FIXME`/`HACK`/`temporary` markers in prod), and `biome-ignore` comments carry real justifications. The actual debt is **structural fallback sludge** — ~2,295 production empty-fallbacks (`?? ""` = 706, `?? []` = 773, `?? 0` = 403, `?? {}` = 413) concentrated in a handful of mega-files — plus **one genuinely dangerous trust-boundary cast** that launders untrusted remote-plugin RPC output straight into the runtime.

This matters now because both patterns violate architecture rule 8 ("DTO fields required by default; no `?? 0` / `as` papering over a broken pipeline"). An empty-fallback at a pipeline edge conflates *"not loaded" / "broken upstream"* with *"legitimately empty"*, so a broken pipeline renders as a silent no-op instead of failing observably. The `as unknown as` at the remote-plugin bridge is worse: it is the only finding with a security dimension. This issue catalogs the patterns and the worst offenders and defers the big structural fixes (mega-file decomposition, strong typing, dead code) to their own linked issues.

## Critical assessment (current state)

**What is actually fine — do not waste effort here.** `as any` in production = 0 (the single non-test grep hit, `app-core/src/api/credential-resolver.ts`, is the English word "any" in a comment, not a cast). `@ts-ignore` / `@ts-expect-error` in prod = 0. No `FIXME`/`HACK`/`temporary`/`workaround` TODOs in prod. The `biome-ignore`s are justified (a11y, ambient shims for optional deps, Drizzle fluent-API typing). Many catch blocks are correct: `packages/agent/src/runtime/plugin-resolver.ts:177`/`:192`/`:1011`/`:1443` discriminate `ENOENT` and rethrow everything else — this is the gold-standard pattern. `message.ts:2633` carries a comment distinguishing a safe plain `as` from `as unknown as` — the team already recognizes the laundering anti-pattern; the gap is enforcing it at scale.

**The real debt (rule-8 violations).** Production empty-fallbacks across `core`/`agent`/`app-core` src: `?? ""` = 706, `?? []` = 773, `?? 0` = 403, `?? {}` = 413 (~2,295 total). The subset that feeds an *external call* or a *decision* (vision `image_url ?? ""`, `getUserMessageText(...) ?? ""`, candidate-actions `?? []`) is the dangerous part: a broken upstream silently degrades to an empty prompt / empty URL / empty action list instead of erroring.

**Root cause: mega-files + weak source types.** Concentration is extreme. Four files total **28,952 lines** and are the catch-all + fallback hotspots: `message.ts` (11,445 lines, 103 empty-fallbacks, 193 `??`), `runtime.ts` (9,521 lines, 17 catch blocks, 27 empty-fallbacks, 136 `??`), `eliza.ts` (5,922 lines, 82 catch blocks), `remote-plugin-adapter.ts` (2,364 lines, 80 empty-fallbacks). Nobody can reason about 80+ catch blocks or 100+ fallbacks in one file, so each new edit just adds another defensive `?? []`. Underneath that, weak/optional source types force the defenses: `runtime.providers` is typed optional but is invariant in practice, so every consumer defends with `?? []` — which then hides the genuinely-broken case.

**The risk.** Broken pipelines look healthy. A malformed plugin manifest, an undefined provider list, a missing user-message text, or a hostile remote-plugin payload all flow through as "empty but fine" rather than surfacing. There is no test that asserts a broken input *fails* — the smell is untested by construction.

## Evidence in code

- `packages/agent/src/services/remote-plugin-bridge.ts:561` — `return result as unknown as ReturnType<Action["handler"]>` launders an untrusted remote-plugin RPC result into the runtime with **zero validation** at the trust boundary. (Verified: 6 such casts in this file at `:561`, `:707`, `:845`, `:852`, `:863`, `:882`, re-casting remote payloads into `Memory` / `emitEvent` params / route handlers.)
- `packages/agent/src/providers/media-provider.ts:757` — `image_url: { url: options.imageUrl ?? "" }` forwards an empty string straight into the OpenAI vision request body (`https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`, lines 759-771) instead of validating presence; a missing URL surfaces as an opaque downstream API error.
- `packages/agent/src/providers/media-provider.ts:497`/`:498`/`:619`/`:681`/`:1475` — ~16 hardcoded model ids / base URLs as `??` defaults (`fal-ai/flux-pro`, `dall-e-3`, `sora-1.0-turbo`, `fal-ai/stable-audio`, `https://fal.run`).
- `packages/core/src/services/message.ts:665` — `runtime.providers ?? []` defends a field that is invariant in practice; this is the template every consumer copies. (`:2151` `memory.content.text?.trim() ?? ""`, `:2563` `getUserMessageText(params.message) ?? ""` feed empty text into response selection.)
- `packages/core/src/services/message.ts` — 11,445 lines; 103 empty-fallbacks, 193 `??`, 35 catch blocks. The message pipeline; structurally unreviewable.
- `packages/core/src/runtime.ts` — 9,521 lines; 17 catch blocks, 136 `??`, 27 empty-fallbacks. The `AgentRuntime` core.
- `packages/agent/src/runtime/eliza.ts` — 5,922 lines; 82 catch blocks. Many are legitimate shutdown-path teardown (`:792`-`:812` `beforeShutdown` / sandbox-stop log-warn-and-continue is correct best-effort); the raw count makes real-vs-cosmetic indistinguishable.

- `packages/core/src/features/trajectories/TrajectoriesService.ts` — 2,831 lines; 44 empty-fallbacks; defends with `?? []` throughout instead of trusting validated input.
- `packages/agent/src/runtime/plugin-resolver.ts:177`/`:192`/`:1011`/`:1443` — **counter-example of good handling**: discriminate `(error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT"` and rethrow / short-circuit otherwise. The target pattern for the swallow-and-continue rewrites.
- `packages/core/src/services/message.ts:2633` — inline comment distinguishing a safe plain `as` from `as unknown as`. Proof the laundering anti-pattern is already recognized internally.

High-confidence first.

- #9874 — Planner confabulation/exhaustion follow-ups (downstream of empty-prompt composition from fallbacks).120:Td0a,## What

The cloud should feel like the app: a user creates **an agent** and chats **instantly**, with no perceived wait, while their dedicated container provisions in the background — then they're **silently swapped** onto it. Every agent ends up dedicated; "shared" is a transient invisible bridge, never a final state, never user-facing.

## How it works

`create-both` → instant shared chat (container-free, in-Worker) → background dedicated provision → copy the shared transcript into the dedicated → silently re-point the client → delete the shared bridge. All invisible to the user — the chat never blocks and never visibly switches.

121:Teaf,## Summary

A dedicated cloud-agent chat turn takes **~6–9s** end-to-end and feels slow, even though the underlying model (cerebras `gpt-oss-120b`) answers in **~0.3s**. I root-caused this live in prod (read-only) against agent `316438e9` and the result is unambiguous: **100% of the overhead is cloud-api pre-forward time-to-first-token (TTFT)** — i.e. work the `cloud-api` Worker does *before* it forwards to cerebras. It is **not** cerebras, **not** reasoning tokens, **not** the agent pipeline, **not** the BitRouter (these models already route cerebras-direct), and **not** streaming throughput.

## Evidence (measured, same model `gpt-oss-120b`, same prompt)

Per-token streaming timing (TTFT = time to first content token; gen = streaming the rest):

| Path | TTFT | generation | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api.elizacloud.ai/api/v1/chat/completions` (cloud-api Worker) | **6.8–7.4s** | 0.05s | 6.8–7.5s |
| `api.cerebras.ai/v1/chat/completions` (direct) | **0.24s** | 0.04s | 0.28s |

Generation streams fast on **both** (~0.05s) → the Worker does not throttle tokens. The entire delta is TTFT.

Non-streaming totals corroborate: cloud `credits/balance` 200 / both models 200; cloud chat 6.4–8.6s vs cerebras-direct 0.36–0.40s.

Agent `[InferenceTiming]` logs from a live turn: one `RESPONSE_HANDLER` call (which resolves to `gpt-oss-120b`, cerebras) = **94–97% of the whole turn** (5.6–10.4s). Everything else (providers ~30ms each, embeddings, should-respond) is noise.

## Where the 6.5s lives

`packages/cloud-api/v1/chat/completions/route.ts` runs these **serially** before forwarding, each a Cloudflare-Worker → Railway-Postgres round-trip (cross-region):

1. `requireAuthOrApiKeyWithOrg(req)` — api-key + org lookup
2. `enforceOrgRateLimit(...)` — per-org tier limit
3. `getCachedGatewayModelById(model)` — reasoning-detection catalog lookup (cached 1h, but on the hot path)
4. `contentModerationService.shouldBlockUser(user.id)` — suspension check
5. `reserveCredits(...)` — a **DB write**

`getLanguageModel()` (`packages/cloud-shared/src/lib/providers/language-model.ts:423`) already routes `gpt-oss-120b` / `zai-glm-4.7` **cerebras-direct** (`https://api.cerebras.ai/v1`, wrapped in `withRateLimitFailFast`). So the upstream is the 0.24s endpoint — the ~6.5s is purely the pre-forward chain. Billing/usage recording is already deferred via `waitUntil` (good).

## Why prior fixes didn't catch it

The 30s→~10s work (#46 / #8769) was **agent-side** (serial embeddings, crash, 1536 embedding dim). Related: `b499abfc` (cerebras ~20s TTFT recovery), #9491 (suppress gpt-oss reasoning), #8839 (cerebras 429 fast-fail). None touched the cloud-api pre-forward chain, which is why chat works but stays slow.

## Proposed fix (all in `cloud-api`, our lane — no BitRouter/infra change)

1. **Add per-step pre-forward timing instrumentation** so prod logs show `auth/rateLimit/catalog/moderation/reserve` ms breakdown — turns the remaining guess into data.
2. **Parallelize the independent pre-forward checks**: after auth + body-parse, run `{rate-limit, app-lookup, catalog, moderation}` concurrently (one wave) instead of serially; keep `reserveCredits` last and preserve exact early-return priority (429 → 403 → 402). Collapses ~4 serial cross-region round-trips into 1.
3. **Skip the catalog lookup for cerebras-native ids** (use name-pattern reasoning detection — already the fallback) to drop a read from the hottest path.
4. Follow-up (bigger): edge-cache auth/org/moderation (KV) so the hot path doesn't hit Railway Postgres per request.

PR incoming. Filing separately from the #9887 `local_inference` fix stack (that one is the route-module/topology bug; this is pure latency). Tracking: #8434.

124:T432,## Verified money leak (apps Product-2 launch scan) — present on develop

`POST /api/v1/apps/:id/domains/buy` debits the org balance then registers the domain on **our Cloudflare account**. But `creditsService.deductCredits()` → `reserveAndDeductCredits()` **returns `{success:false, reason:"insufficient_balance"}` on a too-low balance — it does NOT throw.** So:

1. The route's `try/catch (InsufficientCreditsError)` is **dead code** (that error is never thrown for insufficient balance).
2. The returned `{success:false}` is **discarded**.
3. An org with insufficient credit sails past the zero-effect debit into `cloudflareRegistrarService.registerDomain()` → **a real, paid domain registered on our CF account for free.**

## Fix
Capture the `deductCredits` result and **return 402 when `!debit.success`** before any registration (using `reason` for the message). The existing try/catch stays as a defensive re-throw for genuinely-unexpected errors. One file.

Found by the apps launch-readiness scan; this is the launch-blocking money item on the domains flow.125:T8ce,## What

Upgrades `@biomejs/biome` from **2.4.16 → 2.5.1** (latest stable) across the entire workspace and reformats the tree to 2.5.1's canonical style.

## Why

The workspace had a **biome version skew**: `package.json` files declared a mix of `2.4.16`, `2.5.0`, and `^2.4.14`, while `bun.lock` (and therefore CI's `bun install --frozen-lockfile`) resolved **2.4.16**. Because PR CI lint is path-gated (it only lints changed files), 2.5.x-formatted files merged via PRs that didn't touch them could slip in and then fail a full repo `bun run lint`. Pinning one version everywhere removes that whole class of intermittent lint drift.

## Changes

**Commit 1 — version bump (config only):**
- Pin `@biomejs/biome` to `2.5.1` in all **97** `package.json` files
- Regenerate `bun.lock` (resolves `2.4.16` → `2.5.1`)
- Bump `$schema` to `2.5.1` in all **68** `biome.json` configs
- Migrate the deprecated `linter.rules.recommended: true` → `linter.rules.preset: "recommended"` in **50** configs (behavior-identical; removes the 2.5.x deprecation diagnostic)

**Commit 2 — mechanical reformat:**
- `biome check --write` under the 2.5.1 toolchain (formatting + organizeImports only — **no logic changes**). The bulk of the diff is the trailing-comma behavior change between 2.4 and 2.5.

## Verification

- **Per-package lint green at 2.5.1:** serial sweep of all no-write first-party packages → **51 pass, 0 needing fixes, 0 residual lint errors**.
- `packages/core` typechecks clean (the reformat is format + import-ordering, which cannot change types).
- All `biome.json` configs validate at 2.5.1 (no `deserialize`/deprecation diagnostics; verified core/agent/app).

## Notes for the reviewer

- This is a large (~1100-file) **mechanical** change. The meaningful review surface is **commit 1** (versions + config). Commit 2 is pure formatter output.
- It's a repo-wide reformat, so it can go stale against an active `develop`. If it can't fast-forward at merge time, the cleanest sync is to **regenerate** rather than rebase: `bun install` then `bunx @biomejs/biome check --write .` on the latest `develop`. 128:T1679,## Summary

Decomposes the ~7.5K-LOC `plugin-lifeops` monolith into a slim orchestrator (`plugin-personal-assistant`) plus 6 new focused plugins, with the `/lifeops` dashboard view removed in favor of per-domain plugin views. Existing domain plugins (todos, health, calendar, documents, phone) gain the owner-facing actions and views they should have owned all along. Stub future homes for runtime primitives (owner-state, scheduled-task, registries, dispatch) are scaffolded in `@elizaos/core` and `@elizaos/app-core` to mark where the still-in-PA implementations will eventually migrate.

No backwards-compat shims — `@elizaos/plugin-lifeops` is gone, not aliased.

## What changed

### New plugins (Phase 1)
- **plugin-relationships** — entity/relationship graph (`ENTITY` action + Drizzle `app_relationships` schema). Absorbs lifeops `entities/`, `relationships/`, voice-observer bridge.
- **plugin-inbox** — cross-channel inbox (`INBOX` action + triage + Drizzle `app_inbox` + `/inbox` view). Distinct from plugin-messages (which stays Android-SMS-only).
- **plugin-goals** — life goals + self-care (`OWNER_GOALS`/`ROUTINES`/`REMINDERS`/`ALARMS` + `CheckinService` + Drizzle `app_goals` + `/goals` view).
- **plugin-blocker** — focus/distraction control (`BLOCK` action + website + app blocker services + `/focus` view).
- **plugin-finances** — owner finances (`OWNER_FINANCES` + Drizzle `app_finances` + `/finances` view).
- **plugin-remote-desktop** — `REMOTE_DESKTOP` action.

### Extended plugins (Phase 2)
- **plugin-todos** — `+ /todos` view (Today/Upcoming/Someday lanes); doc-block folds `OWNER_TODOS`.
- **plugin-health** — `+ OWNER_HEALTH`, `OWNER_SCREENTIME` actions; `+ /health` view (Sleep/Circadian/Screen-time/Activity/Connectors).
- **plugin-calendar** — `+ CALENDAR` (8 ops), `CONFLICT_DETECT` actions; `+ /calendar` view.
- **plugin-documents** — `+ OWNER_DOCUMENTS` action; `+ /documents` view.
- **plugin-phone** — `+ VOICE_CALL` (Twilio) action.

### Rename + view kill (Phase 3)
- `plugin-lifeops` → `plugin-personal-assistant` (727+50 file renames, 299 cross-workspace updates, zero remaining `@elizaos/plugin-lifeops` references).
- Internal exports renamed (`appLifeOpsPlugin` → `personalAssistantPlugin` etc.).
- `packages/shared/src/contracts/lifeops.ts` → `personal-assistant.ts`.
- App registry entry `apps/lifeops.json` → `apps/personal-assistant.json`.
- `/lifeops` view deleted (LifeOpsPageView, LifeOpsTuiView, XR variant, `lifeops.overview` widget). PA no longer ships a view — domain plugins do.
- `.github/workflows/lifeops-bench*.yml` filenames kept (benchmark-suite identifier, not the plugin name) — required-check refs would break.

### Core foundations (Phase 3, structural only)
Scaffold-only future homes; code still lives in `plugin-personal-assistant` until the next migration pass:
- `packages/core/src/owner-state/` — OwnerFactsStore, HandoffStore, GlobalPauseStore, FirstRunService, PendingPromptsStore interfaces.
- `packages/core/src/registries/` — Anchor, Gate, EventKind, EscalationLadder, Family, Blocker registry interfaces.
- `packages/core/src/scheduled-task/` — ScheduledTask types extending core's existing task-scheduler with gates/escalation/completionCheck/anchors.
- `packages/app-core/src/dispatch/` — ConnectorRegistry, ChannelRegistry, ApprovalQueue, send-policy interfaces.
Each module has a README with `TODO(migrate:)` pointing back to the still-canonical source.

### What stayed in `plugin-personal-assistant`
The cross-domain orchestration role:
- `BRIEF`, `PRIORITIZE`, `PERSONAL_ASSISTANT`, `SCHEDULED_TASKS`, `RESOLVE_REQUEST` actions.
- Default-pack composition (daily-rhythm, morning-brief, followup-starter, habit-starters, executive-assistant).
- The entity/relationship store, scheduled-task runner, owner-state, registries, connector/channel registries — all still here, will migrate into core/app-core in follow-up passes once the new homes exist.

- [x] `bun run lint` — exit 0
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — exit 0 workspace-wide
- [x] `bun run build` — exit 0 workspace-wide
- [ ] Manual smoke: load PA + the new domain plugins in dev-ui, confirm each registered view renders

## Follow-up

This PR establishes the structural decomposition. The remaining migration moves the implementations out of `plugin-personal-assistant` into the new homes:
1. Move EntityStore + RelationshipStore + merge engine → plugin-relationships.
2. Move INBOX action body + TriageRepository → plugin-inbox.
3. Move OWNER_GOALS/ROUTINES/REMINDERS/ALARMS bodies + CheckinService + default-pack fragments → plugin-goals.
4. Move BLOCK + website-blocker/ + app-blocker/ → plugin-blocker.
5. Move OWNER_FINANCES body → plugin-finances.
6. Move CALENDAR/CONFLICT_DETECT bodies + calendar-gate + travel-time → plugin-calendar.
7. Move OWNER_DOCUMENTS body → plugin-documents.
8. Move OWNER_HEALTH/SCREENTIME bodies + ActivityTracker + PresenceSignalBridge → plugin-health.
9. Move ScheduledTaskRunner + Anchor/Gate/EventKind/EscalationLadder registries + OwnerState services → @elizaos/core.
10. Move ConnectorRegistry + ChannelRegistry + ApprovalQueue + send-policy → @elizaos/app-core.
11. After (1)-(10), PA becomes ~10% of its current size — pure BRIEF/PRIORITIZE/PA orchestration + default-pack composition.

<h3>Greptile Summary</h3>

This PR introduces an **agent-surface framework** that makes every plugin view agent-controllable (registry, overlay, `useAgentElement` hook, and capability dispatch), plus a **view-action affinity layer** that upweights view-scoped runtime actions in the planner's prompt while the user is looking at that view. It also ships **sleep/wake lifecycle endpoints** for deep cold-storage of agent compute, **incremental diff backups** for agent sandboxes, and a **scheduled-backup cron** to keep agents continuously snapshotted.

- Agent-surface: `ViewAgentRegistry`, `AgentSurfaceProvider`, `useAgentElement`, `AgentElementOverlay`, and capability handlers wired into both `DynamicViewLoader` and the new `ShellViewAgentSurface` wrapper.
- Incremental backups: `agent-backup-diff.ts` computes field-level deltas; migration 0136 adds `backup_kind`/`parent_backup_id`/`content_hash` safely.
- Sleep/wake: `executeSleep` backs up then frees compute; `executeWake` re-provisions and restores.

<h3>Confidence Score: 4/5</h3>

Safe to merge; the most consequential new paths are well-tested and the DB change is backwards-compatible.

The three main feature areas all land with test coverage and the migration is safe. The pre-shutdown backup inconsistency leaves content_hash null on the most important backup rows, but is functionally safe since the column is nullable.

132:Tb3a,## What

Replaces the 27-deep `LifeOpsService` class-mixin chain with **namespaced sub-service composition**. The mixin system is removed entirely.

### Before
`service.ts` composed 26 `withX` mixins via a 27-deep generic chain. TypeScript can't track type identity past ~6 chained generic mixins (TS2589 instantiation-depth), so every mixin carried an `as unknown as MixinClass<>` return cast and an `as unknown as <X>MixinDependencies` dependency cast; `service.ts` added a `Constructor<StatusMixinDependencies>` cast and 4 `Omit<>` collision deconflicts plus a `noUnsafeDeclarationMerging` interface merge. ~39 load-bearing casts in one package, hiding real cross-domain type drift.

### After
- **`LifeOpsContext`** (`lifeops-context.ts`) — the shared state/infra surface (runtime, repository, identity, ownership, generic audit, logging, events), derived via `Pick<LifeOpsServiceBase>` so it can't drift.
- **26 domain sub-services** under `lifeops/domains/*-service.ts`, each `class XDomain { constructor(ctx, deps) }` — cast-free, taking cross-domain dependencies as typed `deps` (no `this`-casts). The **browser↔screentime cycle** is broken via DI; the **reminders hub** (~5500 LOC) is one domain that its 5 consumers (definitions/goals/workflows/x/status) inject.
- **`LifeOpsService`** is now a single **concrete** `class extends LifeOpsServiceBase` holding the 26 domains, 263 flat delegators (preserving every existing call site byte-identically), and 26 typed **namespace getters** (`service.goals.x()`, `service.gmail.y()`, …). A concrete class surfaces every method directly, so the interface-merge, the 4 `Omit<>`s, and all assembly casts are gone.

## Why
The mixin god-class was not ideally factored: 22.9k LOC of 27 domains melted onto one class via a cast-laden inheritance chain whose casts were a genuine workaround for TS depth limits + method-name collisions. Composition removes the depth limit, the collisions, and the casts, and gives real domain separation.

## Result
- Repo-wide `as unknown as` **117 → 82** (−35); the plugin's mixin/assembly casts went from ~39 to **2** documented bridge casts for genuine pre-existing cross-package type drift (`LifeOpsGoalRecord` narrow re-decl; `LifeOpsDerivedEvent` vs `LifeOpsWorkflowEvent`). Domains are cast-free. Type-safety ratchet baseline lowered 117 → 82 to lock it in.
- **No behaviour change** — pure structural refactor; the flat public surface is preserved.

## Verification
- `tsgo` typecheck: **0 errors** in `src/lifeops/` (and `src/`).
- `vitest run src/lifeops/`: **16 files / 112 tests pass**.
- Each of the 8 commits is an independently-green slice (foundation → leaf domains → cross-dep domains → cycle break → reminders hub → dependent cluster → facade collapse → residual-cast cleanup).

136:Tbb7,# Walkthrough — Voice UX & Default UI Preference Layout

I have successfully implemented both the voice control system for the Interactive Canvas and the default dashboard interface toggle preference in the Eliza Cloud platform.

---

## 1. Default UI Interface & Layout Preference

### Core Implementation
- **State & Persistence:** Added `defaultUiMode` (`'canvas' | 'classic'`) state and the action `setDefaultUiMode(mode)` in the Zustand store [canvas-store.ts](file:///Users/home/Documents/eliza/packages/cloud-frontend/src/lib/stores/canvas-store.ts). This preference is persisted in the local storage config.
- **Settings tab:** Added the **Default interface** configuration card inside the general settings page [general-tab.tsx](file:///Users/home/Documents/eliza/packages/cloud-frontend/src/dashboard/settings/_components/tabs/general-tab.tsx). Users can choose their startup layout using a drop-down selector.
- **Layout switcher:** Integrated the conditional layout render inside the layout router [App.tsx](file:///Users/home/Documents/eliza/packages/cloud-frontend/src/App.tsx).
  - If `canvasOpen` is true, `<CanvasLayout />` renders.
  - If `canvasOpen` is false, `<DashboardLayout />` renders instead, unmounting the canvas to prevent page navigation from triggering unintended canvas events.
  - While in `<DashboardLayout />`, the floating assistant pill [cloud-assistant-pill.tsx](file:///Users/home/Documents/eliza/packages/cloud-frontend/src/components/canvas/cloud-assistant-pill.tsx) remains overlayed in the bottom-center of the viewport, so pressing `cmd + k` or clicking the orb seamlessly slides back into the Interactive Canvas.

---

## 2. Voice-Driven Canvas Interaction UX

### Core Features
- **Unified Voice Hooks:** Integrated `useVoiceChat` and `useContinuousChat` from `@elizaos/ui/hooks` with a stabilized React Ref (`handleSendRef`) to avoid stale closure state during voice/speech callbacks.
- **Dual-Mode UX State Flow:**
  - **Text Mode:** Canvas is open with the text input bar expanded. A microphone button is available next to the close button to switch to voice mode.
  - **Voice Mode:** Input bar collapses into a floating circular orb (56x56 px). centring states like recording (`Mic`), thinking (`Loader2`), or speaking (`Volume2` bounce animation). Real-time preview transcript is shown in a small card overlay.
- **TTS Responses:** Automatically speaks out assistant responses on query execution success, along with helpful voice-guided prompts.

---

## Verification & Build Quality

### 1. Build Verification
- Verified compiling and typechecking of `packages/ui` package with zero TS errors:
  ```bash
  bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
  ```
- Verified the build pipeline in `packages/cloud-frontend` builds and finishes with zero warnings or errors:
  ```bash
  bun run verify
  ```

### 2. Biome Formatting
- Checked and formatted modified files to align with the Biome rules:
  ```bash
  bunx @biomejs/biome check --write --unsafe
  ```

iOS fused voice loop + multi-account coding-agent orchestration. Merges current `develop`.

# Risks

**Medium.**
- **iOS / voice (on-device):** new model-grind + voice-bundle detection + an OmniVoice TTS route. The CoreML Kokoro path is **WIP and intentionally not staged into any shipping bundle** (documented fidelity gap; iOS `synthesizeSpeech` keeps using the validated fused-GGUF Kokoro), so there is no TTS regression risk from it.
- **Multi-account orchestration:** the AccountPool→spawn selector bridge is a no-op when zero accounts are linked (bridge returns null → prior single-login behavior), so spawning never regresses. Subscription tokens only ever flow to the first-party coding subprocess, never into runtime `process.env`.
- **Merge:** brings `develop` (Cloudflare deploy verify, plugin-commands wiring, shared-runtime startup-shell adapter, lifeops decomposition) into the branch; conflicts resolved toward `develop` for infra/deps/tests.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

**iOS fused voice slice**
- On-device **model-grind** self-test: loads + exercises every Eliza-1 model and captures per-model memory + load result (localizes the text-load hang); launch-flag plumbed into the runtime.
- **Voice-bundle detection** (CoreML optional) + an **OmniVoice TTS route**.
- **CoreML Kokoro → fused E2E exporter** (`packages/training/scripts/kokoro/coreml/`): single `kokoro_5s.mlmodelc` matching the Swift `KokoroCoreMlModel` contract, plus `diag_stages.py` to localize the remaining CoreML-vs-torch divergence (narrowed to the vocoder `F.interpolate`/iSTFT ops). Fidelity gap documented; not shipped until parity lands.
- Voice/latency **instrumentation + review** (`memory-and-e2e-latency-review.md`): the mic→VAD→ASR→LM→TTS waterfall, `GET /api/dev/voice-latency`, and a ranked memory/eviction + latency optimization plan.

**Multi-account coding-agent orchestration** (`plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator`)
- `coding-account-bridge` (`Symbol.for("eliza.account-pool.coding-agent.v1")`) wires the existing `AccountPool` (least-used / quota-aware) into the **sub-agent spawn path**: per-agent credential injection (claude → `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, codex → per-account `CODEX_HOME/auth.json`), parent API-key drop so the selected subscription wins, account stamped on session metadata + `SpawnResult`.
- Exclude-on-failure retry, usage attribution (pool `recordCall` + JSONL), `/api/orchestrator/accounts` route + dashboard widget, structural **interruption decider** (deliver/queue/interrupt/ignore; busy = `tool_running`).
- **MCP forwarding** to sub-agents (opt-in via `ELIZA_ACP_MCP_SERVERS`) for Codex/Claude-Code parity.

**UI / voice**
- Hands-free + dictation capture intents in the shell controller; `deriveAgentReady` / agent-ready refactor in `useShellController`; first-run dedicated-cloud-sandbox + shared-runtime opt-in.

## What kind of change is this?

Features (non-breaking) + Improvements + Updates (merge of `develop`).

Updated alongside the code: `multi-account-orchestration.md`, `SUBAGENT_FLOW_AND_PARITY.md`, `memory-and-e2e-latency-review.md`, `kokoro/coreml/README.md`, `ondevice-model-grind.md`.

## Scope notes

## Testing

Third in the focused-PR split, after #8443 and #8444.14c:Td61,Completes the **#9956** recall-bench work-order, building on the IR-metrics foundation **#10153** laid (`metrics.ts` + `metrics.test.ts`). This adds the real-`@elizaos/core` harness, per-mode metrics, the fail-open regression gate, registry registration, and a CI lane — exactly the checklist #10153's README left open.

## What it does
Drives the **genuine** recall pipeline (no Python/mock reimpl) over a deterministic, seeded, labelled corpus:
- Boots a real `AgentRuntime` + `@elizaos/plugin-sql` (PGlite, in-process) + the real `documentsPlugin`, registers a deterministic content-hash `TEXT_EMBEDDING` model, ingests via the real `DocumentService.addDocument`, then runs `searchDocuments` (hybrid/vector/keyword), the low-level `searchMemories`+`embedRecallQuery` path, and the `scoreMemoryText` keyword chat-search surface.
- Emits per-`SearchMode` **Precision@K / Recall@K / MRR / nDCG@K / HitRate@K + p50/p95 latency** via the shared `metrics.ts`, with the memperf honesty contract (`null`, never `0`, for unmeasured rows).
- **Hard fail-open assertion:** forces `embedRecallQuery → null` and asserts hybrid/vector recall collapses to the keyword baseline — the silent-degradation risk #9956 names, now a CI gate.
- Registered as `recall_bench` in the orchestrator (`commands.py`/`scores.py`/`__init__.py`/`adapters.py`/`ci_coverage.py`) **and** ships a memperf-style `budgets.json` + `.github/workflows/recall-bench.yml` exit-code gate.

## Measured baseline (live run, standard tier — 1040 fragments / 200 queries)
| mode | recall@5 | nDCG@10 |
|---|---|---|
| hybrid | 0.553 | 0.693 |
| vector | 0.551 | 0.692 |
| keyword | 0.466 | 0.571 |
| **runtime-vector** (raw cosine, no BM25 rerank) | **0.787** | **0.966** |
| keyword-chat-search (`scoreMemoryText`) | 0.281 | 0.448 |

**Fail-open delta = 0.000** (forcing the query embed to throw collapses hybrid+vector recall@5 to the keyword baseline 0.466). Vector/hybrid beat keyword; pure runtime-vector is strongest.

**Real finding (documented):** `runtime.searchMemories(…, { query })` BM25-reranks vector hits and drops zero-lexical-overlap candidates, capping `DocumentService` vector/hybrid recall; `runtime-vector` (no rerank) isolates the embedding's true semantic recall.

## Design note
The embedding is a **deterministic content-hash** model registered through the real `Plugin.models` layer — so it *is* the real recall path (the runtime dispatches to it exactly like a cloud model), just reproducible and key-free, which makes it a reliable CI regression gate. An optional real-provider embedding mode (OpenAI 1536 / local gte-small 384) for absolute semantic-quality numbers is a documented follow-up, as is the FACTS-provider slice (the four other recall surfaces fully exercise the path).

Lets users deploy arbitrary container apps with a **per-tenant database, sign-in, a per-app URL, and metered hosting billing**, isolated from the shared Eliza **agent** system. Layered onto 2AM's `/api/v1/containers` surface — never rebuilt.

- **Per-tenant DB isolation** — `tenant_db_clusters` pool (race-safe `tryClaimSlot`), `SqlTenantDbProvisioner` + `DirectPgExecutor`, composer `makeTenantDbProvisioning`. Strategy: DATABASE+ROLE-per-tenant with `REVOKE CONNECT … FROM PUBLIC` (a hard auth-layer boundary), pluggable provider. Migration `0140` (journal-registered).
- **Per-tenant network isolation** — `--internal` network + `--cap-drop=ALL`/`no-new-privileges`/`pids-limit`, default-deny egress proxy. Never `NET_ADMIN`/tun (those stay agent-only).

- **Deploy orchestration + adapters** — `AppDeployRunner` (ensure tenant DB → create container row carrying the per-tenant DSN → enqueue `CONTAINER_PROVISION` → link via `apps.metadata.containerId`), `AppContainerStore` (maps host placement into `containers.metadata`), `ContainerJobsWriter`.
- **Per-app URL** — reuses the shared `derivePublicHostname` (ingress source of truth) to stamp `public_hostname`/`load_balancer_url` + `apps.production_url`.
- **`APP_DEPLOY` trigger** — the Worker enqueues `APP_DEPLOY` (pg-free); the daemon claims it and runs the node runner, so `pg`/SSH never touch the workerd request path.

150:T7f9,## Problem

A planner that re-issues a tool call **identical** to one that already **succeeded** this turn (same tool name + arguments) cannot get new information — but nothing stopped it.

Observed live: `gpt-5.5` re-issued the same `WEB_FETCH` (same URL) on every planner iteration; each call succeeded, the evaluator said `CONTINUE`, and the loop ran until `maxTrajectoryPromptTokens` aborted the turn — the user got a generic *"sorry, something went wrong"* apology instead of the data that had been fetched 17 times.

This is the success-side analog of the existing `maxRepeatedFailures` guard (which only catches *failing* repeats).

## Fix

In `runPlannerLoop`:

- **Identity:** identify calls by name + **sorted-key** argument serialization (`canonicalParamsString`), so re-emissions that differ only in key insertion order (common across LLM turns) map to one identity.
- **Skip redundant:** partition each iteration's non-terminal calls into genuinely-fresh vs repeats of an already-succeeded call; execute only the fresh ones.
- **Bound + synthesize:** when every planned call is a redundant repeat, count a dead round; past the new `maxRepeatedToolCalls` bound (default **2**), force **one** tool-less synthesis call so the model writes the final answer from results already in the trajectory.
- **Relax toolChoice:** once a non-terminal tool has executed, relax `toolChoice` from `required` → `auto` (made explicit, since `callPlanner` defaults `undefined` back to `required`) so the planner may synthesize a terminal `REPLY` instead of being pushed to re-call a tool every iteration.

All structural (tool-call identity + trajectory state), no text heuristics.

## Test

Adds `stops re-executing an identical successful call and forces a terminal synthesis` to `planner-loop.test.ts` — same `WEB_FETCH` returned every iteration, asserts it executes **once** and the loop terminates with the synthesized answer. Full planner-loop suite: **45/45 pass**.
