🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)154:T13b7,Closes #10202.

The app is an OS shell for loadable plugin/system/developer **views**, but the shell had only two states — mounted (active tab) or unmounted. No `hide`/`pause`/`evict` vocabulary, per-view crash isolation only for remote plugin views, no per-view render/memory/resource telemetry, and three places (`retained-lazy`, `DynamicViewLoader`, `GameViewOverlay`) each re-implementing their own visibility/memory-pressure pause+evict listeners. This delivers a real, **code-level** view lifecycle contract.

## New primitives (`packages/ui`, exported from the barrel)

- **`ViewLifecycleController`** (`state/view-lifecycle.ts`) — the single state machine + registry: phases `mounted/active/inactive/paused/evicted/crashed/recovering`, a device-memory keep-alive **LRU** with **pinned exemptions** (`chat`, `background` never evicted), and **one** shared `APP_PAUSE/APP_RESUME/visibilitychange/memorypressure` signal bus. `resolveViewLifecyclePolicy` + `registerViewPolicy`.
- **`KeepAliveViewHost`** — the new view host: renders active ∪ retained keep-alive, each wrapped per-view boundary → telemetry profiler → lifecycle slot. **Default policy is unmount-on-hide**, so builtin-view mounting is behaviorally identical to the old `ViewRouter` (the `App.navigate-view-wiring` suite stays green).
- **`useViewLifecycle` / `usePausableInterval` / `usePauseAware`** — the view-author pause/resume API for timers, polling, media, and native subscriptions.
- **`ViewErrorBoundary`** — standardized, keyed, resettable per-view crash container with crash telemetry + recovery, wired into `App.tsx` and `DynamicViewLoader` (the canonical `ErrorBoundary` gains an optional `onError` hook).
- **`ViewTelemetryProfiler` + `view-runtime-telemetry.ts` + `resource-counters.ts`** — per-view render count / p95 commit duration / JS heap / active subscriptions / pending timers / heavy resources (WebGL/audio/video) on a bounded ring + CustomEvent + `[ViewTelemetry]` log; plus per-view rerender-storm detection.
- **`bounded-view-lru.ts`** — single home for the device-memory tier helpers (deduped out of `retained-lazy` + `DynamicViewLoader`) + keep-alive sizing.
- **`view-memory-budget.ts`** — pure monotonic-growth detector for repeated view-switch heap samples (mirrors `hooks/frame-budget.ts`).
- `AppShellPageRegistration` gains `keepAlive?`/`pausable?` so plugin pages opt into retention.

Contract doc: **`packages/ui/src/components/views/VIEW_LIFECYCLE.md`**.

## Acceptance criteria → where met

- documented contract reflected in code-level primitives → `VIEW_LIFECYCLE.md` + the primitives above
- consistent pause/resume for timers/polling/media/native subs → `useViewLifecycle` + `usePausableInterval` + the controller signal bus
- bounded eviction with explicit exemptions → keep-alive LRU + `PINNED_VIEW_IDS`
- per-view error boundaries so one crash can't destabilize the shell → `ViewErrorBoundary` on every routed view
- telemetry makes expensive/leaking views visible in logs/artifacts → `view-runtime-telemetry`
- tests catch **1 rerender storm, 1 listener leak, 1 crash, 1 unbounded memory growth** + full matrix → see below

## Tests (all green)

Unit (jsdom): controller state machine + LRU + exemptions + signal bus + TTL; resource-counters leak/pause; memory detector; crash containment + recovery; rerender storm + sibling containment; **full builtin view-matrix coverage** (every tab). Existing `retained-lazy`, `agent-surface`, and `App.navigate-view-wiring` suites stay green (306 tests in the regression sweep).

E2E (`bun run --cwd packages/ui test:view-lifecycle-e2e`, esbuild → headless Chromium over the **real** `KeepAliveViewHost`): bounded retention (max 3 ≤ cap), RAF pause flatlines, LRU eviction, leaky-sub visible, per-view storm flagged (not calm siblings), crash containment + recovery, and a gc'd heap trend (24 samples) fed to the pure detector → **not leaking**. 0 unexpected page errors.

**Real-LLM trajectory / backend logs / audio:** N/A — presentation + runtime-infra + test work; no agent/model/prompt/server path touched.

## Note: `main.tsx` `appModuleCache` left unbounded — by design

It caches module *promises*; module code stays in the JS heap once imported regardless, so evicting yields no memory benefit and risks re-import races. The bounded-eviction criterion is met by the keep-alive view-**instance** LRU.

## Mobile Resource Workbench

End-to-end on-device resource profiling for elizaOS local inference on **iOS + Android** — battery, peak/steady RSS, prefill/decode tokens/sec, TTFT, thermal-state timeline, and low-power transitions — built on the proven `loadperf` budgets/results/CI-gate pattern. `loadperf` measures host load; this measures the *phone*.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] iOS native probe returns a **live** resource snapshot (resident `phys_footprint`, available RAM via `os_proc_available_memory`, thermal state, low-power mode, CPU time) — not the one-shot `getDeviceCapabilities` with `availableRamGb: NSNull()`.
- [x] iOS **MetricKit** (`MXMetricManager`) payloads (CPU/energy/runtime) captured to disk and ingested by the harness.
- [x] Android exposes a `ResourceProbe.getResourceSnapshot` Capacitor method (parity with iOS): thermal status, `BatteryManager` level/charge-counter, `Debug.getMemoryInfo` PSS; `dumpsys` hooks in the host probe.
- [x] Per-generation **prefill and decode tokens/sec** computed from the on-device `generateResult` (`durationMs`/token counts + measured TTFT) and aggregated per workload, per tier.
- [x] **Peak and steady RSS** recorded on-device with an RSS-leak flag (reused leak heuristic).
- [x] **TTFT** recorded on-device (text now; voice loop wired, tied to #8785/#8786).
- [x] **Battery drain** (% and, where available, µAh) across a fixed-duration workload.
- [x] **Thermal-state timeline** + low-power transitions across a sustained run (not a single probe).
- [x] CPU/GPU/ANE/NPU utilisation captured where the OS exposes it (MetricKit / batterystats), else explicitly recorded as missing — never faked.
- [x] `budgets.json` + `BASELINE.md` per device-class × tier (`0_8b`/`2b`/`4b`); runner writes `results/<workload>/latest.json` + a report and exits non-zero on budget regression.
- [x] `workflow_dispatch` (+ nightly) CI job: PR-path-filtered harness smoke + dispatch-only Android (self-hosted arm64) / iOS-sim lanes, uploading the report; kept off PR-blocking lanes until baselines are stable.
- [x] Missing measurements recorded as null/missing, never fabricated zeros (AGENTS.md §3/§7).

### What changed

**Shared / runtime (unit-tested):**
- `@elizaos/shared/local-inference` `computeGenerationThroughput` — differences `generateResult` into prefill/decode/combined tok/s (TTFT split); `null` when unmeasurable.
- Capacitor adapter captures first-token wall-clock (TTFT) → relayed through both hand-synced `device-bridge` copies → surfaced via `subscribeGenerationMetrics` + a recent-metrics buffer + `GET /api/dev/device-resource-metrics`.
- `DeviceResourceMetrics` accumulator generalises `VoiceRunMetrics` (tok/s, RSS+leak, battery, thermal timeline, low-power).

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->158:T834,## Problem

Live-data turns — "current bitcoin price", "weather in tokyo" — mis-routed: the agent **showed a VIEWS panel** or **spawned a coding sub-agent** instead of fetching the data and answering. On a text connector (Discord) that means a useless panel or a 3-minute multi-spawn with "working on it" acks, often ending in "Sorry, something went wrong."

## Three structural causes, each fixed

1. **VIEWS view-emphasis** (`plugin-app-control`) — `VIEW_ACTION_CONTEXTS` listed `web/crypto/finance/research/browser/payments`, which the action catalog turns into **keyword-retrieval terms**, so "price"/"weather" *retrieved VIEWS* and the planner navigated to a panel. VIEWS only displays panels — it doesn't fetch — so those live-data contexts are dropped.
2. **Stage-1 candidate-narrow drops the top tool** (`core/action-tiering`) — WEB_FETCH retrieved at score **1.0**, but Stage-1's `candidateActions` came back `[MESSAGE_SEARCH, VIEWS]`, so `tierActionResults` **demoted WEB_FETCH off the surface** — the planner physically couldn't pick it. Now a **near-certain match (score ≥ 0.97)** stays exposed even when Stage-1's narrow omits it. It does not force the choice — only keeps a dominant match available.
3. **Planner routing** (`core/planner` template) — a one-shot live/current/public-data lookup is *not* coding work: call WEB_FETCH / WEB_SEARCH directly; don't spawn a sub-agent.

All structural — no text heuristics on model output.

## Verification

- `action-tiering.test.ts`: **14/14** incl. new cases (near-certain non-candidate match stays exposed; a merely-good 0.8 match still demotes).
- **Live across all three planner backends** (cerebras/zai-glm, claude, codex): the same weather query routes to WEB_FETCH and answers cleanly on each.

> Note (for the planner side): a weak planner model (`gpt-oss-120b`) still mis-routes even with these fixes; a reasoning model (`zai-glm-4.7`, claude, gpt-5.5) routes correctly. These fixes make the *right* route reachable; the model has to take it.

159:Tc5c,## What & why

Closes the **deepest** part of #9967: "the Kotlin that runs on a phone is executed by
no test, on no device." Before this PR the entire `plugin-native-*` set had **zero**
Android instrumented tests; the only coverage drove the React views against a **mocked
`Capacitor.Plugins` bridge in desktop Chromium**, so the real Kotlin — the launcher's
Phone/SMS/Home/Assistant gating — ran untested.

Root cause of *why* it was untested: the native logic was welded to the Capacitor
`Plugin`/`Bridge`/`PluginCall` objects, which only exist inside a running app, so it
could not be asserted from `androidTest`. This PR fixes that at the source.

### Changes
- **`RoleStatus`** (added in the prior commit): the launcher/comms role read is
  extracted out of `SystemPlugin` into a pure, `Context`-taking object — `RoleManager`
  / `TelecomManager` / `PackageManager` / `Telephony` reads with **no** bridge
  dependency. `SystemPlugin.getStatus` just delegates, so runtime behavior is unchanged.
- **`RoleStatusInstrumentedTest`** now lives in the plugin's *own* `androidTest` source
  set (`@elizaos/capacitor-system`) and runs the real `RoleStatus.read()` against the
  device's actual system services — the first on-device test in the native set.
- **plugin `build.gradle`** gains `AndroidJUnitRunner` + `androidTest` deps so the
  plugin library is instrumentable **standalone** — no full-app build (voice/inference
  JNI, fused `.so`, omnivoice submodule) is needed to run it. That's the pattern the
  rest of the native-plugin × view matrix can follow.

## Evidence — real Pixel 6a (Android 16)

```
> Task :system:connectedDebugAndroidTest
Starting 3 tests on Pixel 6a - 16
Finished 3 tests on Pixel 6a - 16
BUILD SUCCESSFUL
testsuite ... tests="3" failures="0" errors="0" skipped="0"
```

The three tests prove the read returns **live** device state, not a stub:
- `read_reportsRealPackageNameFromContext` — packageName comes from the real `Context`.
- `read_enumeratesAllFourRolesFromRealRoleManager` — all 4 roles (home/dialer/sms/
  assistant) enumerate from the real `RoleManager`, each mapping to its constant.
- `read_homeHolderMatchesTheDeviceDefaultHome` — the home holder equals the device's
  actual default launcher (`com.google.android.apps.nexuslauncher`), cross-checked
  against `adb shell cmd role get-role-holders`.

Artifacts in `.github/issue-evidence/9967-androidtest-*`: gradle HTML report, JUnit XML,
`TestRunner` logcat, the live role-holder dump, device screenshot, and a screenrecord.

This is the **foundational slice** of the #9967 work-order: it makes the previously
untestable native Kotlin testable and proves it on hardware, establishing the
standalone-instrumentation pattern. It does **not** yet cover the issue's other asks —
deterministic gradle wiring so all 9 native plugins compile into the launcher APK
(gap #1), the full native-plugin × view matrix across the remaining plugins, and the
launcher-as-home behavior tests. Those build directly on this pattern and are tracked
as the remaining #9967 surface.

15b:Teb4,## What

Lands the first **"Needs CI infra"** deliverable spun out of #9476 (tracked by #10333): run the MiniWoB++ benchmark suite against a **real Chromium engine** instead of JSDOM web mode.

The benchmark adapter was already engine-agnostic (`BrowserCommandExecutor`), so this is a **new executor + a gated lane — not a rewrite**. `report.engine` flips from `"jsdom-web"` to `"chromium"` and every action runs through a real browser process, mirroring how plugin-computeruse's OSWorld `*.real.test.ts` lanes drive a real OS.

## How

- **`src/benchmark/chromium-executor.ts`** — `createChromiumBenchmarkExecutor` (puppeteer-core, already a dep), `launchChromiumBenchmarkBrowser` (one browser per suite, fresh page per episode), `resolveChromiumExecutablePath` (env → playwright-core → system Chrome; `null` → lane self-skips). Command semantics mirror `browser-workspace-web.ts` **exactly** (type appends, fill replaces, check sets `checked`, get value/checked/text/count/url/title, snapshot, network-route via request interception with a hard external-network seal), so the **identical oracle sequences solve every task on both engines** — the engine-parity proof.
- **`src/benchmark/__tests__/miniwob-chromium.real.test.ts`** — gated `.real.test.ts` lane: oracle solves every task on every seed (reward 1), noop scores 0, on real Chromium.
- **`vitest.real.config.ts`** — opts the `.real.test.ts` lane back in (the root config excludes `**/*.real.test.ts`) while keeping the `@elizaos/*` source aliases. The "(or a dedicated config)" the issue called for.
- **`.github/workflows/browser-real-bench.yml`** — CI gate: `bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium`, run the lane + upload artifacts (nightly + dispatch + on benchmark changes), alongside the other heavy real lanes.
- **`scripts/run-miniwob-chromium-benchmark.mjs`** + `bench:miniwob:chromium` / `test:real-chromium` scripts.
- `BrowserWorkspaceMode` gains `"chromium"` (emitted only by this executor, never by `executeBrowserWorkspaceCommand`) so results carry an accurate engine tag.


15f:Tede,## What

Closes the one Definition-of-Done deliverable [verified missing on `develop`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/issues/9476#issuecomment-4830133507) for #9476:

> **≥1 benchmark wired through `plugin-browser`** (mirror `plugin-computeruse/src/osworld/adapter.ts`), with a committed run artifact.

The other three DoD items already landed (CI-asserted parity matrix, JSDOM real-code lane, typed error contract). The web benchmarks (Mind2Web, WebShop, VisualWebBench) all **bypass** plugin-browser via the inference layer — no benchmark drove the BROWSER command surface end-to-end. This adds one that does.

## How

A **MiniWoB++-style** web-interaction benchmark (the canonical web-agent benchmark) under `plugins/plugin-browser/src/benchmark/`, the plugin-browser analog of `plugin-computeruse/src/osworld/`:

- **`adapter.ts`** — `BrowserBenchmarkAdapter` with the same observation/action/step seam as `OSWorldAdapter`, driving an engine-agnostic `BrowserCommandExecutor`. The workspace executor binds the **real** `executeBrowserWorkspaceCommand` router (the same mock-free path the `browser-workspace-web-real-code` lane uses) — no mock service stands in for the browser.
- **`tasks.ts`** — 6 tasks (`click-button`, `click-link`, `enter-text`, `enter-text-dynamic`, `click-checkboxes`, `multistep-purchase`). Pure markup, **no page scripts** (web mode hard-blocks script exec, GHSA-mhhr-9ph9-64j7); deterministic per seed; reward computed from **observable DOM state** read back through real BROWSER `get` commands (`value`/`checked`/`url`/`title`).
- **`policy.ts`** — `OraclePolicy` (deterministic solver) + `NoopPolicy`/`WrongPolicy` negative baselines.
- **`runner.ts`** — `runBenchmarkSuite` drives every task×seed episode, scores it, aggregates.
- **`__tests__/miniwob-adapter.test.ts`** — CI-asserted real-code lane (runs in the default `vitest run`).
- **`scripts/run-miniwob-benchmark.mjs`** + `bench:miniwob` — runnable harness that writes a JSON run report.

## Evidence (real, on a Windows 11 host) — see `.github/issue-evidence/9476-browser-benchmark/`

| Policy | Result | Proves |
|--------|--------|--------|
| oracle | **18/18 solved (100%)** | the suite is solvable end-to-end through real BROWSER commands; every action step records `resultMode: "web"` (the live router ran it) |
| noop   | **0/18** | doing nothing scores 0 — reward is grounded in real DOM state, not hard-coded |
| wrong  | **0/18** | wrong-target / wrong-text near-misses score 0 — reward discriminates |

164:Te26,# Relates to

# Risks

Medium.

This PR adds a new opt-in plugin under `packages/plugin-agent-commerce-pqc`. No existing runtime behavior is modified.

The plugin registers:

- 1 Service (`agent_commerce`)
- 4 Actions
- 1 Provider

State is persisted through the existing `runtime.createMemory()` API using the `erc8183:job:` namespace.

Known operational risks:

- hydration currently loads up to 1000 job records per agent
- rate limiting is process-local and not distributed
- reputation persistence is memory-backed by default

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds an ERC-8183-inspired commerce workflow for elizaOS agents.

The plugin enables one agent to:

1. Create a job
2. Fund a job
3. Submit a deliverable
4. Evaluate the result
5. Complete, refund, expire, or abort the workflow

State machine:

OPEN → FUNDED → SUBMITTED → COMPLETE
                           ↘ REFUND
              ↘ EXPIRED
         ↘ ABORTED

## Registered extension points

| Type | Name |
|--------|--------|
| Service | agent_commerce |
| Action | CREATE_SECURE_JOB |
| Action | FUND_SECURE_JOB |
| Action | SUBMIT_DELIVERABLE |
| Action | JOB_STATUS |
| Provider | COMMERCE_CONTEXT |

## Persistence

Jobs are stored through `runtime.createMemory()` using:

erc8183:job:<jobId>

Each state transition appends a new memory record.

On restart, the store lazily hydrates from memory records and reconstructs the latest job state using the highest `updatedAt` value.

## Security features

- SHA-256 payload attestation
- Deliverable hash verification
- Reputation-based funding gate
- Rate limiting
- State transition validation
- Idempotent terminal transitions

## What kind of change is this?

Feature (non-breaking).

All changes are additive.

# Documentation changes needed?

No.

The package includes its own README.

- **`DELETE_APP`** — DESTRUCTIVE → **two-phase, connector-agnostic confirm** (`safety.ts`): first ask names the app + what's destroyed (container + tenant DB) and does NOT delete; only an explicit confirmation in the follow-up calls `deleteApp`. Never relies on GUI buttons; a bare "yes" is insufficient.

## Safety + memory
- **`safety.ts`** — reusable two-phase confirm + a neutral `buildConnectorCta({label,url,kind})` (https-only) seam for the deferred paid actions; money/credentials never transit the connector.
- **`app-facts.ts`** — on a verified-live deploy, writes ONE durable fact to the real `facts` memory table via `runtime.createMemory`, keyed on `app.id`, idempotent (re-deploy updates in place). Convenience recall cache — **explicitly NOT the completion gate**. (This is the "save completed app to facts/knowledge" idea, done right.)

Discord Activity OAuth is intentionally left fail-closed here; the branch adds the guarded link-command path but does not claim full Discord Activity OAuth support.16b:Tf2c,## Summary

This PR hardens the desktop/mobile shell for Cloud-first startup and limited Cloud-agent bases:

- removes the separate native desktop pill window path; the in-canvas chat pill remains the single desktop surface
- wires external Cloud API bases into Electrobun renderers early and avoids local desktop RPC fallbacks for configured external bases
- recovers localhost/dev shells with stale local-backend state into first-run/Cloud selection instead of wedging on `Booting up...`
- gates full app-shell routes when the active base is a shared/dedicated Cloud chat adapter, avoiding unsupported `/api/views`, `/api/apps/runs`, `/api/workbench/todos`, `/api/approvals`, `/api/lifeops/inbox`, `/api/computer-use/approvals`, `/api/coding-agents`, and `/api/orchestrator/*` calls
- prevents localhost `:2138` Cloud sign-in from probing `/api/cloud/status` when no local backend exists
- polishes chat overlay, springboard/home ordering and image-backed tiles, route back behavior, and related startup failure UI

## Why

The reproduced browser logs were three separate problems:

1. Local Vite shell running without app-core behind it returned same-origin `/api/*` 502s.
2. A selected Cloud agent base is a limited chat adapter, not a full app-shell runtime, so desktop widgets/hydration were polling unsupported routes and creating CORS/404 noise.
3. The `My Eliza Cloud key isn't authorized for inference` message was traced in #8434 to a revoked key on a throwaway validation agent; that remains a cloud/phone provisioning self-heal follow-up, not a desktop UI route issue.

This PR fixes the desktop/UI-side causes and leaves the provisioning guard to the cloud/phone lane.

## #9948 — canonical role model
- **One `CANONICAL_ROLE_RANK`** source of truth; `roles.ts` + `context-gates.ts` derive from it (kills the two-disagreeing-rank-tables hazard).
- **Drop the `RoleGateRole = … | (string & {})` escape** → `Role | "USER"` (a gate can no longer name an arbitrary string that silently ranks 0). Core typechecks clean; every `minRole`/`roles` literal across agent+plugins is already canonical.
- **`resolveBoundaryRole` + `ensureMinRole`** — a role tier on the binary HTTP boundary; the tokenless same-machine caller resolves to a NAMED OWNER principal instead of ambient trust. Fails closed.
- **Provider role-gating** routed through the canonical `satisfiesRoleGate` (the 6th lowercase vocabulary is now just an override-map alias).
- **`public:true` allowlist regression test** — a new public route can't be added unauthenticated without tripping the guard.
- **Wallet sign routes**: loopback-only CORS, dropped credential reflection.

## #9949 — should-respond injection gate
- Pure `extractRiskFactors` in the `parallel_with_should_respond` hook, role-keyed (OWNER/ADMIN bypass), borderline USER/GUEST → one fail-closed `TEXT_LARGE` adjudication, only when `shouldRespond=true`. 23 adversarial tests.
- **One injection pattern bank**: `SecurityModule` and `external-content` now share `injection-primitives` (prompt-injection phrasing vs external-content dangerous-command indicators are split deliberately so the gate doesn't flag dev chat).

## #9947 — connector embed seam
- Fail-closed **embed-auth handshake** (Telegram `initData` HMAC, timing-safe + 24h replay guard; Discord OAuth2), maps to entity, OWNER/ADMIN-only via the single core `hasRoleAccess` (the duplicate `hasRoleAccess` is consolidated).
- **`/embed` route** per-platform CSP `frame-ancestors` (telegram.org / discord.com, else `'none'`).
- **Role-gated launch surfaces**: Telegram `web_app` button (https-enforced, OWNER/ADMIN-gated) + Discord `/app` Activity command. Live launch needs platform creds.

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>173:T834,## What

New `@elizaos/plugin-cloud-apps` — lets the agent answer **"what apps do I have on Eliza Cloud?"** and "tell me about app X" from chat, on **every connector** (in-app, Discord, Telegram, cloud-hosted) from one registration. Closes the gap where the "What apps do I have?" suggestion chip was a false promise (no action behind it).

This is the **read-core**; the mutating actions (create/deploy/manage/monetize) land in a follow-up PR.

## How

- **`LIST_CLOUD_APPS`** (similes `MY_APPS`/`WHAT_APPS_DO_I_HAVE`/…) → `ElizaCloudClient.listApps()`, formats name/url/status; empty + no-key + error handled.
- **`GET_APP`** → by name or id, formatted detail; graceful not-found.
- **`CLOUD_APPS` provider** → injects the user's app inventory into context, modeled on `creditBalanceProvider`: 60s cache, context-gated to apps/finance/settings topics, EMPTY when no cloud key.
- **Dual registration (both sites — the whole point):**
  - (a) `core-plugins.ts` `CORE_PLUGINS` — reaches local/native + Discord/Telegram via the shared runtime pipeline (default on, read-only).
  - (b) `agent-loader.ts resolvePlugins()` — as a **full** plugin (not via `AVAILABLE_PLUGINS`, which strips to models-only), gated behind **`CLOUD_APPS_PLUGIN_ENABLED`** (**default OFF** — it runs on every dedicated prod agent, so it must be staged + proven with real trajectories first).
- Suggestion chip `"What apps do I have?"` now matched by `LIST_CLOUD_APPS`'s similes.

<details><summary><h3>Greptile Summary</h3></summary>

This PR adds end-to-end support for custom Docker image provisioning through the Eliza cloud API: the `dockerImage` field is now accepted on agent creation, validated with a regex schema, persisted to the database, and surfaced in list and detail API responses. The dashboard is wired to pass the persisted image through sandbox creation, and new E2E tests cover both the API path and the dashboard UI flow.

- **API layer** (`route.ts` for both agents and `[agentId]`): `dockerImage` is validated via a zod schema with a character-class regex, stored on create, and returned in list/detail DTOs — including the fix in `Page.tsx` that was previously hardcoding `docker_image: null`.
- **E2E stack hardening** (`stack.ts`): migrations now run as an explicit logged step before the API server starts, `DATABASE_URL` is set earlier in the process, and the stack switches to `cloud-api-e2e-server.mjs`.
- **Frontend fixes** (`agent-card.tsx`, `glass-composer.tsx`, `sandbox-proxy/page.tsx`, `vite.config.ts`): accessibility improvements (aria-label, aria-pressed), an inlined Vite alias for es-toolkit/compat shims, and a switch from `process.env.NODE_ENV` to `import.meta.env.PROD` for the sandbox proxy guard.
</details>

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client

    CloudAPI->>SandboxSvc: "createAgent({agentName, dockerImage})"
    SandboxSvc->>DB: "INSERT (docker_image = dockerImage)"
    DB-->>SandboxSvc: agent row
    SandboxSvc-->>CloudAPI: agent
    CloudAPI-->>Client: "201 {id, dockerImage}"

    Client->>ProvisionAPI: POST /api/v1/eliza/agents/:id/provision
    ProvisionAPI->>DB: read docker_image
    ProvisionAPI->>ControlPlane: schedule provisioning job (image)
    ControlPlane-->>ProvisionAPI: 202 accepted
```

<details><summary><h3>Comments Outside Diff (1)</h3></summary>

1. `.github/workflows/coverage-gate.yml`, line 10 ([link](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/blob/cb8cb4c0614d1f25b9cddf8a24bc2cef9237a3f0/.github/workflows/coverage-gate.yml#L10)) 

   <a href="#"><img alt="P1" src="https://greptile-static-assets.s3.amazonaws.com/badges/p1.svg?v=9" align="top"></a> **Lockfile integrity bypassed on failure**

   The `|| bun install --no-frozen-lockfile` fallback means that whenever the lockfile is out of sync with `package.json` — the exact condition `--frozen-lockfile` is supposed to catch — CI silently falls through to an unconstrained install. Packages resolved during that fallback install may differ from what the lockfile records, making the build non-reproducible and removing the supply-chain integrity guarantee the frozen flag provides. If the frozen install is failing in CI today, the correct fix is to regenerate the lockfile and commit it, not to bypass the check on every future run.
